[define-project-implementation](/Users/am/Documents/My_Repos/caprmedio-graph-driven-framework/.caprmedio_caprmedio/101_LAYER_1_FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY/METHODOLOGY_SOURCES/001_CORE_META_MODEL/04_requirement/draft/CA-R-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-DEFINITION--define-project-implementation.md:37) says Resources members remain unplaced, and [R2180@4](/Users/am/Documents/My_Repos/caprmedio-graph-driven-framework/.caprmedio_caprmedio/101_LAYER_1_FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY/METHODOLOGY_SOURCES/001_CORE_META_MODEL/04_requirement/draft/CA-R-2180@4-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-DEFINITION--define-documentation.md:40) refers to remaining Resources. The main Model and Asset Definition already record the accepted retirement/classification.

Consequence: The packet gives a stale account of what remains to decide.

Smallest correction: Update the readiness sentences to the Asset/Prompt/Documentation distinction while preserving the caveat that Current migration is not done.

### Confirmed alignment

The inspected primary definitions agree on the corrected Package/Module and Scope Unit/Project structures, Workflow–Step–Substep counts and leaf-call boundaries, permitted direct/indirect Workflow-call recursion, and no inheritance through containment. Counts apply independently to direct values; subjects{0} permits its declared children. Required Claim prose, an independently optional R Formal claim, string-valued Subjects, removal of list/map/ref Formats and YAML null/empty-value treatment agree in the inspected Claims. Remaining contradictions are in the supporting preparation packet described above.

### Remaining preparation and limits

The proposal explicitly retains incomplete primitive-Format definitions and final Type-catalog reconciliation. This bounded review does not certify a complete corpus migration, every old constraint transfer, parser behavior, source promotion or runtime enforcement. It does not assess the excluded advanced expression language. The historical FPF report was not altered or treated as a new run.

## TLDR

Repair the conflicting Draft clauses before promotion. Preserve the chosen primary model and the latest direct-value/Claim decisions. If named-relation cardinality is retained, settle its counting direction; otherwise keep those constraints in prose. Leave advanced expressions in their separate proposals.

# Summary

Close the plain Model review repairs

## Question

Were the ten reported A1298 finding groups repaired in the prepared packet, using settled decisions and the simplest remaining choice, without promoting sources or including advanced expressions?

## Scope

The original main proposal and 45 RMED Drafts, plus one new Relation Definition replacement Draft. Advanced formulas, functions and conditions in [] remain separate proposals under A1297 and were excluded. Current source adoption, full legacy migration, Engine/code and runtime were outside this work.

## Approach

Four workers edited disjoint Draft-body scopes: notation; Definition Claims; carrier rules; and structural examples. The parent handled the generator, replacement Relation Definition, metadata, Journal and integration. Read-only reviewers rechecked the reported findings. No FPF command ran.

## Results

All ten reported groups are repaired in the prepared packet:

| Finding | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| PR-01 Relation Type versus concrete edge | Prepared a replacement Relation Definition; reusable Type metadata is separate from actual (source, Relation Type, target) edges. Removed concrete endpoint/Type slots from the generic Type inventory. |
| PR-02 Stale containment | Restored parentless Project Implementation and exactly one Package per Module in declarations, methods and evaluation cases. |
| PR-03 Heading nesting | A1299 uses sibling ## Summary and ## Claim sections, with optional ### Formal claim beneath Claim. |
| PR-04 Claim authority | Moved the reported operative Definition and carrier conditions into direct Claim prose; retained explanations/provenance outside. |
| PR-05 Containment grammar | Distinguished schema kind declarations/references from ordinary full Subject selectors. |
| PR-06 Prior target existence | Defining GOVERNS paths can introduce their target; explicit existing-kind/named-instance references retain their meaning. |
| PR-07 Named-relation counts | Removed undefined relation-cardinality suffixes. Exactly-one Workflow and File-Carrier bindings remain in prose; no new counting-direction grammar introduced. |
| PR-08 Scope headings | Six legacy ## Scope headings now use ## Claim scope. |
| PR-09 Formal child boundaries | Ordinary Claim prose moved before Formal claim; the child retains its fenced expression. |
| PR-10 Resources status | Updated obsolete unplaced-Resources notes to the accepted Asset/Prompt/Documentation distinction. |

The Relation replacement also preserves useful concrete Source/Target Reference meanings from R1986/R1987 in prose. R1963/R1986/R1987 are tracked for replacement/retirement after adoption; their Current versions were not changed or archived by this repair.

## Verification

- Checked 47 carriers, including 46 RMED Drafts, and 72 local links.
- Confirmed sibling Summary/Claim headings, required direct Claim prose, no old Scope heading and no named-relation cardinality suffix in the prepared packet.
- Confirmed removed list/map/ref Formats, independent property cardinalities and the advanced-expression exclusion remain intact.
- Read-only acceptance passed for Relation structure/counts, containment/grammar/status wording, target introduction and the reported Claim/carrier placements. One parent paragraph-placement error was caught and corrected before the final boundary recheck passed.
- Parent recorded the 17 worker-edited Drafts without changing their proposed Versions. Generator outputs and the new Definition have their own recorded changes.
- All 977 non-Draft/non-archive Core files matched their pre-repair hashes. No Current source promotion or runtime change occurred.

## Limits

This closes the ten reported findings in a bounded prepared packet, not every possible issue in all methodology. The original A1298 review remains unchanged as a point-in-time report. Primitive Format definitions, final Type-catalog reconciliation, broader source migration/adoption and any code support remain separate work. No full test suite or runtime/parser verification was run for these documentation repairs.

## TLDR

The reported Draft inconsistencies are repaired. No new Operator question is needed for them. Keep advanced expressions separate; review/promote the prepared sources only through the later adoption work.

### Summary

Track Entity candidate implementation Questions

## Latest candidate

[CA-A-1302 — Entity graph candidate with four root branches](draft/CA-A-1302@1-draft-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--entity-graph-candidate-with-four-root-branches.md), with A1303/A1304 refinements. The Operator’s latest words override older decisions; implementation evidence uses only the last 48 hours. This proposal tracks every Question created while implementing CA-P-2683.

## Questions and chosen continuation

- [CA-C-605 — Where should Term and Selection belong under Entity?](../01_concern/CA-C-605-QUESTION--where-should-term-and-selection-belong-under-entity.md): Keep the existing persistent Term and Selection classifications under Object/Continuant for this migration. This preserves the latest explicit lower-level tree instead of adding a fifth root. The four-root candidate left their exact placement open; this choice is provisional and does not implement the Terms Graph.

- [CA-C-606 — Does a zero-direct-value property need a value Format?](../01_concern/CA-C-606-QUESTION--does-a-zero-direct-value-property-need-a-value-format.md): For a grouping property with cardinality {0}, state that a direct-value Format is not applicable; define the Formats of its children independently. Do not invent void/list/map as Formats. This reconciles the required property coverage with the approved direct-value semantics.

## Boundaries

The six legacy Graph Rule Subject paths are held for source-specific preservation/retirement during the Definition pass. Missing-ID legacy RMED carriers without Subjects are explicitly unchanged in the Subject-only pass. Neither creates a new entity or requires Engine changes. The Current frontier is 1,100 RMED carriers; 17 legacy records have no explicit Atom ID or Subjects. Existing archived/draft carriers and Engine sources are excluded.

- [CA-C-607 — legacy generic Node/Project Model targets](../01_concern/CA-C-607-QUESTION--which-targets-replace-generic-node-and-project-model-subjects.md): use Entity for the old generic Subject/Node, and Object/Continuant for the persistent grouping during the mechanical pass; narrow or retire actual defining sources during coverage.

- [CA-C-608 — duplicate Terms Projection kind](../01_concern/CA-C-608-QUESTION--does-terms-projection-need-a-separate-kind.md): reuse existing Projection/Type: Terms Graph; leave the duplicate Draft unpromoted. Terms Graph implementation remains deferred.

## Stage 3 chosen continuations

- [CA-C-609 — Should all derived reverse views have a name?](../01_concern/CA-C-609-QUESTION--should-all-derived-reverse-views-have-a-name.md): Keep the direct Relation Types and derive their reverse lookup. Preserve already declared inverse names such as CONTAINS, BEARS and IS_CARRIED_BY. Do not invent a second name or stored fact where the Current definition declares no inverse name. This supplies every reverse view without introducing aliases. The open choice is whether those unnamed views need separate names later.

- [CA-C-610 — Which Runtime owns automatic context initialization?](../01_concern/CA-C-610-QUESTION--which-runtime-owns-automatic-context-initialization.md): Preserve legacy REQU-507's automatic session/context initialization commitment as a framework outcome, rather than dropping it for a malformed header. Use the existing Runtime/Session vocabulary and leave its concrete implementation owner to the later Engine Epic. This does not add a Session Engine entity or implement startup code.

- [CA-C-611 — How should installed Extension lifecycle be represented?](../01_concern/CA-C-611-QUESTION--how-should-installed-extension-lifecycle-be-represented.md): Preserve legacy REQU-697's install, uninstall, update and downgrade commitment. Govern the framework capability and refer to the existing installed-Extensions Scope Units; do not introduce another Extension object or application-binding system. Concrete execution belongs to the later Engine work.

- [CA-C-612 — generic Execution Result value Format](../01_concern/CA-C-612-QUESTION--how-should-unconstrained-execution-result-values-be-formatted.md): use the reusable scalar Format and direct-value cardinality; retain producer-specific output constraints.

## Property and Relation completion choices

- [CA-C-613 — Confirm minimal shared Property value schemas](../01_concern/CA-C-613-QUESTION--confirm-minimal-shared-property-value-schemas.md): The implementation uses string for identifiers/names/locators, integers for counts, optional explicit Scope Unit Label, and one or more string values for an ordered Scope Unit Path. Settings/registry/configuration groups have zero direct scalar values; their children keep independent counts. Producer- or invocation-specific properties read within their defining Claim scope. These choices complete the existing model without new stored fields or advanced conditions; change them only if a concrete source requires a different shape.

- [CA-C-614 — Does a concrete Relation connection need a separate kind?](../01_concern/CA-C-614-QUESTION--does-a-concrete-relation-connection-need-a-separate-kind.md): For now an actual directed connection remains the tuple (source, Relation Type, target), without a new Connection entity or separate ID. R2247 preserves source/target reference meanings; R1986 and R1987 were retired because those are not reusable Type metadata. Existing direct facts and derived inverses stay governed. A separate endpoint-record kind can be reconsidered only if a concrete operation needs it.

## Actual readback reference disposition

- [CA-C-615](../01_concern/CA-C-615-QUESTION--should-legacy-concern-resolution-links-be-restored-as-history.md): Remove the three unresolvable legacy resolution_of links from Current R1646, R1647 and R1648. Their Current Claims remain unchanged; the exact former links remain in the newly preserved predecessors and Journal history. Do not invent canonical Concern IDs or migrate C/A. If those old Concern records are recovered, consider source-traceable historical references rather than guessing a Current native target.

## Delivery classification continuation

- [CA-C-616](../01_concern/CA-C-616-QUESTION--should-delivery-policy-ownership-require-child-scope-units.md): Use the latest reusable D Policy versus individual D Decision distinction for the Core representation rules. A Core D Policy can govern an Object/property kind across applicable cases without its owning Scope Unit having children. Preserve the actual-child condition on Method Eng Policy. This avoids inventing Scope Units solely to allow the explicitly requested Core D Policies.

## Governing-configuration boundary

- [CA-C-617](../01_concern/CA-C-617-QUESTION--where-should-stable-scope-unit-ids-be-carried.md): Keep the adopted logical Scope Unit.ID definition and its string cardinality, but preserve the existing governing-configuration bytes and registered Scope Unit Name references. R1988 expressly adds no storage field or rename procedure; the latest 48-hour decisions do not specify a concrete migration protocol. Do not invent a new TOML key, allocate IDs to excluded Engine Scope Units, or revise the Scope Unit structure in this methodology-only Epic. Define the concrete ID encoding/data migration in the already separate Engine/Scope Unit work before requiring it from those readers.

### Summary

Track Entity candidate implementation Questions

## Latest candidate

[CA-A-1302 — Entity graph candidate with four root branches](draft/CA-A-1302@1-draft-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--entity-graph-candidate-with-four-root-branches.md), with A1303/A1304 refinements. The Operator’s latest words override older decisions; implementation evidence uses only the last 48 hours. This proposal tracks every Question created while implementing CA-P-2683.

## Questions and chosen continuation

- [CA-C-605 — Where should Term and Selection belong under Entity?](../01_concern/CA-C-605-QUESTION--where-should-term-and-selection-belong-under-entity.md): Keep the existing persistent Term and Selection classifications under Object/Continuant for this migration. This preserves the latest explicit lower-level tree instead of adding a fifth root. The four-root candidate left their exact placement open; this choice is provisional and does not implement the Terms Graph.

- [CA-C-606 — Does a zero-direct-value property need a value Format?](../01_concern/CA-C-606-QUESTION--does-a-zero-direct-value-property-need-a-value-format.md): For a grouping property with cardinality {0}, state that a direct-value Format is not applicable; define the Formats of its children independently. Do not invent void/list/map as Formats. This reconciles the required property coverage with the approved direct-value semantics.

## Boundaries

The six legacy Graph Rule Subject paths are held for source-specific preservation/retirement during the Definition pass. Missing-ID legacy RMED carriers without Subjects are explicitly unchanged in the Subject-only pass. Neither creates a new entity or requires Engine changes. The Current frontier is 1,100 RMED carriers; 17 legacy records have no explicit Atom ID or Subjects. Existing archived/draft carriers and Engine sources are excluded.

- [CA-C-607 — legacy generic Node/Project Model targets](../01_concern/CA-C-607-QUESTION--which-targets-replace-generic-node-and-project-model-subjects.md): use Entity for the old generic Subject/Node, and Object/Continuant for the persistent grouping during the mechanical pass; narrow or retire actual defining sources during coverage.

- [CA-C-608 — duplicate Terms Projection kind](../01_concern/CA-C-608-QUESTION--does-terms-projection-need-a-separate-kind.md): reuse existing Projection/Type: Terms Graph; leave the duplicate Draft unpromoted. Terms Graph implementation remains deferred.

## Stage 3 chosen continuations

- [CA-C-609 — Should all derived reverse views have a name?](../01_concern/CA-C-609-QUESTION--should-all-derived-reverse-views-have-a-name.md): Keep the direct Relation Types and derive their reverse lookup. Preserve already declared inverse names such as CONTAINS, BEARS and IS_CARRIED_BY. Do not invent a second name or stored fact where the Current definition declares no inverse name. This supplies every reverse view without introducing aliases. The open choice is whether those unnamed views need separate names later.

- [CA-C-610 — Which Runtime owns automatic context initialization?](../01_concern/CA-C-610-QUESTION--which-runtime-owns-automatic-context-initialization.md): Preserve legacy REQU-507's automatic session/context initialization commitment as a framework outcome, rather than dropping it for a malformed header. Use the existing Runtime/Session vocabulary and leave its concrete implementation owner to the later Engine Epic. This does not add a Session Engine entity or implement startup code.

- [CA-C-611 — How should installed Extension lifecycle be represented?](../01_concern/CA-C-611-QUESTION--how-should-installed-extension-lifecycle-be-represented.md): Preserve legacy REQU-697's install, uninstall, update and downgrade commitment. Govern the framework capability and refer to the existing installed-Extensions Scope Units; do not introduce another Extension object or application-binding system. Concrete execution belongs to the later Engine work.

- [CA-C-612 — generic Execution Result value Format](../01_concern/CA-C-612-QUESTION--how-should-unconstrained-execution-result-values-be-formatted.md): use the reusable scalar Format and direct-value cardinality; retain producer-specific output constraints.

## Property and Relation completion choices

- [CA-C-613 — Confirm minimal shared Property value schemas](../01_concern/CA-C-613-QUESTION--confirm-minimal-shared-property-value-schemas.md): The implementation uses string for identifiers/names/locators, integers for counts, optional explicit Scope Unit Label, and one or more string values for an ordered Scope Unit Path. Settings/registry/configuration groups have zero direct scalar values; their children keep independent counts. Producer- or invocation-specific properties read within their defining Claim scope. These choices complete the existing model without new stored fields or advanced conditions; change them only if a concrete source requires a different shape.

- [CA-C-614 — Does a concrete Relation connection need a separate kind?](../01_concern/CA-C-614-QUESTION--does-a-concrete-relation-connection-need-a-separate-kind.md): For now an actual directed connection remains the tuple (source, Relation Type, target), without a new Connection entity or separate ID. R2247 preserves source/target reference meanings; R1986 and R1987 were retired because those are not reusable Type metadata. Existing direct facts and derived inverses stay governed. A separate endpoint-record kind can be reconsidered only if a concrete operation needs it.

## Actual readback reference disposition

- [CA-C-615](../01_concern/CA-C-615-QUESTION--should-legacy-concern-resolution-links-be-restored-as-history.md): Remove the three unresolvable legacy resolution_of links from Current R1646, R1647 and R1648. Their Current Claims remain unchanged; the exact former links remain in the newly preserved predecessors and Journal history. Do not invent canonical Concern IDs or migrate C/A. If those old Concern records are recovered, consider source-traceable historical references rather than guessing a Current native target.

## Delivery classification continuation

- [CA-C-616](../01_concern/CA-C-616-QUESTION--should-delivery-policy-ownership-require-child-scope-units.md): Use the latest reusable D Policy versus individual D Decision distinction for the Core representation rules. A Core D Policy can govern an Object/property kind across applicable cases without its owning Scope Unit having children. Preserve the actual-child condition on Method Eng Policy. This avoids inventing Scope Units solely to allow the explicitly requested Core D Policies.

## Governing-configuration boundary

- [CA-C-617](../01_concern/CA-C-617-QUESTION--where-should-stable-scope-unit-ids-be-carried.md): Keep the adopted logical Scope Unit.ID definition and its string cardinality, but preserve the existing governing-configuration bytes and registered Scope Unit Name references. R1988 expressly adds no storage field or rename procedure; the latest 48-hour decisions do not specify a concrete migration protocol. Do not invent a new TOML key, allocate IDs to excluded Engine Scope Units, or revise the Scope Unit structure in this methodology-only Epic. Define the concrete ID encoding/data migration in the already separate Engine/Scope Unit work before requiring it from those readers.

## Summary

Trial global Object, Carrier and Graph Syntax Definitions with scoped Aspects

## Proposal

Each Object (Continuant or Occurrent), Carrier and Graph Syntax entity has one dedicated global R/Entity Definition, with an exact governed entity. An Object remains the same Object across Scope Units. Local Rs may add applicable constraints; they are not competing Definitions. The accepted Relation Definition template remains eligible without introducing a subtype hierarchy.

Aspect definitions use a looser rule and may differ by Scope Unit or explicit applicability scope. Do not force a separate Definition for every shared Aspect topic or characteristic. Additional Rs may add coherent requirements while one Atom still has one Claim. Report where the dedicated-Definition trial adds redundancy or fits badly.

The Operator confirmed all 133 shared/formal starting cases. The initial 337 parsed paths split into 280 strict and 57 Aspect paths. Normalize equivalent property spelling to one logical identity. Keep the Epic Active; review the full combined cohort for coherence, then fix findings and rebuild.

## Status

Accepted for the current trial. This supersedes the blanket exact-one rule for Aspects. Subtype restructuring and Engine implementation remain deferred.

[CA-A-1311](done/CA-A-1311-SPEC_PROPOSAL--one-canonical-entity-definition-with-additional-scoped-requirements.md) records the later Operator decision. The loose-Aspect Definition exception above is superseded; keep one canonical Definition for Aspects too, with scoped additional requirements instead.

# Summary

Subject model Candidate #10

## Question

What is the proposed main Subject structure, and which R Atom defines each primary entity or topic?

## Content Scope

Main structure and definitions only. No instances, property lists, instance names, actual Relation Type or Graph Rule instances, source migration or implementation. Namespace and topic headings are explicitly distinguished from independently modeled things.

## Proposal

This Specification Proposal records the accepted design and decisions. Its reviewed definitions and Subject mappings are now adopted in Current RMED. Those source Atoms remain authoritative; this Analysis is not their replacement or the rebuilt Projection.

```text
Subject  [CA-R-1275]
	/CAPRMEDIO  [CA-R-2206]
		/Graph  [CA-R-2208]
			/Node  [CA-R-1994]

					/Implementation  [CA-R-2173]
						/Code  [CA-R-2174]
						/Documentation  [CA-R-2180]
						/Prompts  [CA-R-2179]
						/Resources  [CA-R-2189]
					/Occurrent  [CA-R-1972]
					/Project  [CA-R-2220]
					/Projection  [CA-R-1746]
					/Runtime  [CA-R-2194]
					/Scope Unit  [CA-R-1757]
					/Selection  [CA-R-1966]
					/Term  [CA-R-1318]
				/Aspect  [CA-R-2210]

					/Domain  [CA-R-2213]
					/Engineering  [CA-R-2214]
					/Product  [CA-R-2211]
					/Project  [CA-R-2212]
					/UX  [CA-R-2215]
			/Relation  [CA-R-1963]
			/Rule  [CA-R-1995]
		/Carrier  [CA-R-1958]
	/<Project Name>  [namespace pattern; CA-R-2207 governs Subject]
```

`<Project Name>` describes a namespace pattern; it is not an instantiated project Subject. CAPRMEDIO is the shared framework vocabulary namespace. Projects use that vocabulary and add their own Subjects without copying it. Namespace, Graph and Project Model headings organize the vocabulary; they do not assert that every child is a subtype of a new real-world entity.

Event and Execution retain existing meanings rather than disappearing during regrouping. History/Journal/Release describe preserved material, while Event, Execution and Runtime describe actual occurrences or contexts. Implementation is directly edited and is not a Projection.

## Definition boundaries

- Project Model names project things, including Implementation. Aspects name topics addressing those things. CAPRMEDO Atoms and I Implementation are different structures inside the model; not every Project Model item is an Atom.
- Content Role is a classification axis and remains a valid Subject; it is not another primary entity between Atom and role-qualified Atom kinds. The R1531 Draft defines this distinction. No role values or instances are expanded in this main tree.
- A Carrier is distinct from what it represents. A graph can represent a Carrier as a node without merging representation with represented content.
- Documentation under Implementation is actual content; Documentation under Aspect is the topic governing its organization and authoring.
- Subject, Content Role and owning Scope Unit stay independent. A shared Subject does not become project-specific because its governing Atom lives in Project Configuration.

`<Project Name>` describes a namespace pattern; it is not an instantiated project Subject. CAPRMEDIO is the shared framework vocabulary namespace. The completed bounded review found no concern from the outline alone; it did not establish complete grammar admission. The project-name placeholder does not choose name normalization or collision/rename handling. These are unresolved proposal details, not new runtime requirements. Existing Entity terminology is preserved rather than silently retired. Existing Term paths are relocated under Project Model/Term; Terms Graph work stays deferred.

# Summary

Clarify mixed Subject targets

## Question

Can the Subject graph intentionally mix actual things, descriptions and abstract topics without treating them as one uniform entity kind?

## Proposal

Yes. The mix is intended: a Subject names the thing or topic an Atom governs or depends on.

A Node identifies a thing or topic addressed by the graph. Its description and Carrier are separate. A description can itself be another Subject. Carrying a record of an occurrence does not carry the actual occurrence.

## Decision

Accepted by the Operator: “The mix is intended, and your recommendation is good.” Then: “This is why it's subject.”

This resolves C10-I01 and accepts clarification C10-F01 from the Candidate #10 FPF review. It does not introduce a new entity, force a uniform category, or approve source promotion or migration.

## Content Scope

The meaning of Node and Project Model in the primary Subject structure. No instances, property inventory, runtime implementation or additional graph machinery.

## Proposed specification changes

- R1994@11-draft clarifies Node and distinguishes a thing, its description and its Carrier.
- R2209@1-draft identifies Project Model as a vocabulary grouping rather than another copy of the represented things.
- A1218 records these accepted definitions. The definitions are Current: R1994@11 and R2209@2; their adoption is recorded in P2681.

Project means the whole project as one entity, distinct from any particular part such as an Atom or Implementation.

# Summary

Govern Nodes with generic Type rules

## Question

Where do generic Type definitions and checks belong when there is no Node/Type Subject?

## Proposal

Use Subject/CAPRMEDIO/Graph/Node for CA-R-1284, CA-R-1285, CA-R-1286, CA-R-1349, CA-R-1350 and CA-E-387. Their existing Content Scope and Claims retain the precise Type-classification, allowed-value and assignment boundaries.

Do not add Node/Type or Node.Type as a shared classification axis or universal property. Type remains optional for a Node unless a specific rule requires it. Map references to these general Type rules' old Graph Node.Type target to Graph/Node as well.

CA-D-393 is different: its Scope and Claim govern external Type names derived from internal Content Role Types. Its Subject is Subject/CAPRMEDIO/Graph/Node/Project Model/Atom.Type. Do not blanket-map every Type-related Atom to Graph/Node.

## Decision

Operator: “we don't have Node/Type, and we don't need it. so, Graph/Node. Are you sure it's all about Graph/Node?”

The six selected sources were read individually. R1284 explicitly addresses optional Type Properties for Graph Nodes; R1285/R1349/R1350 and E387 constrain such assignments, and R1286 keeps their qualified allowed-value sets expandable. None requires every Node to bear Type. D393 is excluded from this general mapping.

## Adoption

Subjects-only successors; existing Scope, Claim, relations and identity stay unchanged. Stage for review before replacing Current sources.

## References

- [Candidate #10](CA-A-1218-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--subject-model-candidate-10.md).

# Summary

Distinguish Events from Journal records

## Question

How do Event, Occurrent, Event Record and Journal relate?

## Operator decision

- An Event happening in a Runtime is an Occurrent.
- A record about that Event in a Journal is a Continuant.
- A Journal contains Event Records: Journal > Event Record.

The occurrence and its record are different things. The containment statement concerns Journal records, not the actual Events.

## Interpretation boundary

Keep Event as an actual occurrence under the existing Occurrent classification. Do not infer an instantaneous-only Event criterion or a new lifecycle from this answer. The answer establishes the occurrence/record distinction and Journal containment; it does not require a new Subject path for Event Record or merging Event and Occurrent definitions.

## Review disposition

This addresses C10-I04 / C10-G03 with the Operator's intended distinction. Existing Continuant/Occurrent meanings stay settled. C10-I06 / C10-G04 (Runtime boundary), optional Prompts/Documentation clarification, general stale drafting language and Projection source-count correction remain separate items.

## Adoption result

Current R1968@9 and R1745@32 now state the accepted Event/record distinction and Journal containment. R1972 already classified actual Events as Occurrents; its separate editorial correction is recorded in A1228. No narrower Event discriminator or new Subject path was introduced.

# Summary

Use Named Relation Notation

## Decision

The Operator accepted `Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` as the general notation for a Relation without a short spelling, including the three examples below. No separate backward notation is needed because reverse navigation uses each Relation's defined derived inverse. This is a notation decision, not source admission of undefined Relation Types or approval of a parser/runtime change.

### General named-relation notation

`Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` expresses the named directed Relation from Source to Target. Use this general form where no short operator exists; it may also spell a defined Relation explicitly without changing its meaning. The name between `((` and `))` identifies one declared Relation Type, not a new kind, arbitrary prose label or automatically registered Relation. Endpoint restrictions and counts come from the Relation definition and applicable Graph Rules.

There is no separate backward notation. To navigate or display the opposite direction, use the defined derived inverse Relation name in the same form with the endpoints exchanged. Persist the direct fact only, not a second independent inverse fact. No inverse name or inverse meaning is guessed from spelling.

The matching unescaped `((` and `))` delimit the Relation Type name. Existing backslash escaping handles literal delimiter characters. Existing `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `::`, `>`, `@(...)` and format/cardinality annotations keep their meanings. The double parentheses are relation syntax, not a function invocation. This decision defines a binary relation expression; it does not silently choose precedence for arbitrary mixed chains or turn a whole relation statement into a node selector for subjects.governs.

The Operator supplied these schema-level examples:

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
Runtime ((EXECUTES)) Workflow Run
```

These expressions connect modeled kinds and do not create actual Runs or records. Their Relation Type definitions and derived-inverse declarations must be authored before source admission; notation alone does not establish that they are already registered. The Runtime in the last expression is the live executor, not the Engineering topic or stored engine Code.

## Draft adoption

The existing successor Drafts R1931@13, R2150@11, M228@29, M232@27, E383@35 and D269@25 are refined in place. The Formal Model primary/properties review Draft CA-A-1239@1-draft includes the decision and examples. No Current RMED source is promoted or migrated. Existing stored direct/inverse policy is retained; no new reverse operator, Relation Type, endpoint permission, cardinality or inference rule is invented by this record.

## Remaining work

Prepare the requested Relation definitions and their declared inverse meanings, then review their endpoint rules before admission. IS_EXECUTION_OF, RECORDS and EXECUTES are not claimed to be registered merely because their names occur here. Formal Claim count constraints discussed separately remain outside this notation-only increment.

# Summary

Connect Workflow definitions, runs and Event Records

## Decision

Add the requested direct connections: Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow; Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run. A Workflow is a reusable definition, Workflow Run an actual Occurrent, and Event Record a persistent description in Journal. None is the same thing as another.

Prepare HAS_EXECUTION as the derived inverse name of IS_EXECUTION_OF, and IS_RECORDED_BY as the derived inverse name of RECORDS. These names are proposed in the Relation Definition Drafts, not automatically registered runtime behavior. Store each direct fact once; derive the opposite view.

The general RECORDS meaning is not limited to Workflow Runs: an Event Record can describe other actual occurrences. No universal one-record-per-run, one-run-per-record or record-existence obligation is introduced. R1510 already requires exactly one Workflow definition per Workflow Run; its prepared successor makes that binding formal.

## Prepared Drafts

- CA-R-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-DEFINITION--define-is-execution-of-relation.md
- CA-R-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-DEFINITION--define-records-relation.md
- CA-R-1510@17-draft successor: Workflow Run binding.
- Existing Event Record Definition Draft, refined in place.

## Scope

This increment defines the two requested links. Runtime ((EXECUTES)) Workflow Run remains an earlier example awaiting its own Relation Definition. No actual Runs, Journal facts, Current sources, parser or runtime are changed.

# Summary

Distinguish Relation Type instances from graph connections

## Decision

Relation instances define the real Relation Types used throughout the graph. Relation describes their structure; Relation//RECORDS and Relation//IS_EXECUTION_OF are named instances of that structure. An actual graph connection uses one of those Types and is identified by its source, Relation Type and target.

Keep the existing // selectors for these reusable Type instances. Correct the stale Definition that still describes the same target as one actual connection. Type-level meaning, direction and derived-inverse declarations must stay distinct from a particular connection's concrete endpoints. This clarification adds no new primary entity branch.

## Review disposition

FM-02 is resolved as a design decision: preserve the Type-instance approach. FX-02's alternative Relation.Type: RECORDS selector is not adopted. Aligning the prepared Definitions and properties remains uncompleted repair work. FM-01 and FM-03 remain open repairs under the already established Claim boundary and latest canonical paths.

## State

This file records the Operator's clarification. The historical FPF report is unchanged; no Current Atom, Definition Draft or runtime was modified by this record.

A Workflow may call itself directly, or indirectly through other Workflows. The Workflow-call graph is not required to be acyclic.

# Summary

Use compact cardinality notation

## Decision

Cardinality annotations count occurrences. `{n}` requires exactly n, `{n+}` requires at least n with no upper bound, and `{n..m}` permits the inclusive range from n to m. Bounds are non-negative integers and a bounded range requires n <= m.

A suffix on a property constrains that property's values for one bearer. In `X >{n+} Y`, it counts immediate Y parts per X whole. It does not change the separately established rule that each contained part has exactly one immediate whole. An omitted annotation leaves cardinality unspecified; it does not imply optionality or an unlimited count.

| Notation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{n}` | Exactly n | `{1}`: exactly one |
| `{n+}` | At least n, no upper bound | `{2+}`: two or more |
| `{n..m}` | From n to m, inclusive | `{2..5}`: two through five |
| `{0}` | None | A forbidden part or property |
| `{0+}` | Zero or more | Optional collection of any size |
| `{1+}` | One or more | At least one part or value |
| `{0..1}` | Zero or one | An optional single value |
| `{0..m}` | At most m | `{0..3}`: zero through three |

Use the compact forms in the prepared model:

```text
Workflow >{1+} Step >{0+} Substep
Substep >{0} @(Substep)
```

The latest compact spelling replaces the earlier >= and open-range spellings in this prepared packet. Historical proposals remain unchanged; no parser aliases or runtime implementation are introduced.

## State

A Cardinality Notation Definition Draft and the affected notation, authoring, evaluation, delivery and container Drafts are prepared. Current methodology and Engine behavior remain unchanged.

# Summary

Defer general formula expressions

## Decision

Defer formula expressions in general, rather than only the Atom ID formula. Retain them as a separate Specification Proposal; they are not part of the syntax being prepared for adoption now.

The retained syntax includes relationship operators and existing-kind references, cardinality `{...}`, value format `[...]` and general named relations `Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target`. Keep cardinality counts, direct/inverse meanings and literal allowed values. Do not use `@(...)` as a property-value interpolation mechanism in this increment.

## Deferred proposal

Preserve this composed-value example for future design:

```text
atom.id: (@(Project.name.prefix)-@(content role.first letter)-number[int, unique(its current kind)]){1}
```

The proposal would group a composed allowed value in parentheses and apply its count to the whole group. It would need property-value binding, value construction, component formats, named-selection uniqueness and a complete expression grammar. Those mechanisms, function-style forms such as `unique(...)` and formula-based count calculations remain deferred. No executor, parser or automatic migration is requested.

Earlier A1265 and A1281 preserve the design discussion; this later decision defers its adoption. The independent content-getter proposal A1237 remains separate and deferred too.

## State

The main Model proposal and affected R/M/E/D syntax Drafts omit operative formulas and interpolation/grouping requirements. Existing ID rules remain in force; no new ID-generation model or Subject rename is introduced. Current methodology and runtime are unchanged.

# Summary

Count direct values independently at each property path

## Decision

Cardinality counts only the direct values of the addressed property. It does not count nested keys or include values belonging to child properties. A parent with `{0}` has no direct values; its declared children remain permitted and obey their own independent counts. Use explicit `{0}` for grouping properties rather than inferring it from an omitted annotation.

```text
claim[string]{1}
claim.formal_claim[string]{0..1}
subjects{0}
subjects.governs[ref]{1}
subjects.depend_on[ref]{0+}
```

Claim requires exactly one prose value. Its optional Formal claim is counted separately and cannot satisfy that prose requirement. Formal and prose still address one Type-defined contribution; Semantics remains separate. The formal child remains R-only.

Subjects has no direct value. It groups one governing reference and zero or more dependency references. The logical example uses depend_on; the existing YAML key subjects.depends_on is not renamed by this decision.

## Carrier distinction

A YAML property key occurs once within its mapping. Multiple values are serialized as a sequence under that one key. For `property[string]{2}`:

```yaml
property:
  - string1
  - string2
```

Repeated keys such as two sibling version keys are invalid. A mapping under subjects represents child properties, not an additional direct subjects value. A YAML sequence represents multiple values, not a separate list value Format. Remove list from the proposed Formats. This decision does not settle map as an independent value Format.

## State

The cardinality, Claim, base-property, Definition-Type and R/M/E/D Drafts and main Model proposal are aligned. Formal-only prepared Definitions receive a prose Claim from their already recorded meaning. Existing Current sources and runtime are unchanged; Drafts can still be incomplete before promotion.

# Summary

Count YAML null and empty strings as values

## Decision

Follow standard YAML value interpretation rather than inventing another null or empty-string policy. Both null and an empty string are values and each contributes one direct value to cardinality. An omitted property has zero direct values. Null is not silently converted into absence.

```yaml
plain_string: asdf
null_value: null
also_null:
empty_string: ""
quoted_null_string: "null"
```

The first value is a string; the next two are null; the last two are strings. Quoting and the YAML parser determine the resulting values. The installed YAML parser was checked on these examples when this proposal was recorded.

The declared value Format and any applicable conditions in prose determine admissibility. An empty string passes the basic string type but may fail a separate nonempty-content condition. Null contributes one value even when it fails a property's declared format. Cardinality alone is not a complete validity check. This adds no universal null prohibition, universal nonempty-string condition or new null Format.

The grouping rule remains independent: subjects{0} has no direct values but may have declared child properties. A YAML mapping carrying those children does not become an extra direct value. A direct subjects null would instead contribute one direct value.

## State

The Cardinality and Value Format Definition Drafts, related R/M/E/D syntax guidance and the main Model proposal state this distinction. Current sources, YAML reader code and runtime remain unchanged.

## Summary

Keep Goals outside and define Scope Contracts inside each Scope Unit

## Proposal

Each Scope Unit has exactly one external Scope Unit Declaration and one or more separate external Goals. Its internal Tier-0 Atoms are Scope Contracts. A Scope Unit may have no local Scope Contracts; do not require every RMEDO Role.

The Declaration has Role Requirement and Form Scope Unit Declaration. Its active Subject identifies the specific Scope Unit. Its Claim declares ID where applicable, Name, optional Label, order.ordered, conditional order.number and direct containment. Scope Constraints are external and may be part of the Declaration. Do not copy Goal Claims into it or create another Definition Atom for each individual Scope Unit.

A Declaration may contain several statements forming one coherent declaration. Its Summary may name that topic. Other Forms keep their existing Claim and Summary rules.

“Outside” means outside the declared Scope Unit’s ownership. Non-root Declarations and Goals belong to its parent. The Project Declaration and Project Goal are externally Operator-owned. The Operator is an Actor, not a Scope Unit. The Project Goal keeps Tier −1.

Scope Unit Declarations replace project_structure.toml entirely. They are the sole structural source. Remove the old file, its governing rules, TOML readers and row writers. Keep the existing Scope Unit workflow definitions; remove their four TOML-specific executable bindings and implementation. Do not build replacement Scope Unit tools in this adoption.

## Ordering and identity

order groups the sibling Properties ordered and number. ordered has exactly one Boolean value. number has exactly one positive integer value when ordered is true, and no value otherwise. Scope Units have no Navigation Number. Step and Plan numbering remains separate.

Non-root Scope Unit IDs are stable CA-SU-<number> values through rename and move. The Project root is Unordered, has no Scope Unit ID or order.number, and is not moved or renamed through Scope Unit operations.

## Folders

The Project Authority Folder remains .caprmedio_<project name>; Delivery is the repository root. For non-root units:

| Unit | Authority Folder | Delivery Folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordered | <id>_<label>_<order>_<name> | <label>_<order>_<name> |
| Unordered | <id>_<label>_<name> | <label>_<name> |

Place each under its respective parent. Omit absent optional segments and their separators. Derive these names; do not independently author folder paths in each Declaration. Move existing Authority and Delivery folders to these names during adoption.

Applicable Methodology is a special Projection, not a separately declared Scope Unit. Preserve its Projection content.

## Writing

Keep the Operator’s wording as close as possible. Use simple grammar and coherent statements. Preserve terms and key concepts such as DRY and MECE; do not replace them with synonyms.

Project Model is only an optional organizational view, not a base classification.

This Draft contains the primary tree, then one flat property block for every selected primary kind with known direct or inherited properties, in the same declaration order as the tree. It includes no named instances. It does not promote Drafts, migrate Current Atoms, rename YAML fields or change code. Terms Graph work and the function proposals in CA-A-1237 remain deferred.

Each property block shows its proposed full `subjects.governs` selector. These describe the proposed governing targets; they are not claims that existing source Atom headers already use the new paths. Inline cardinality/format annotations belong to Claims, not to these selectors.

## Reading the annotations

- `/` specializes; `::` groups; `>` contains, and each contained part belongs to exactly one whole; `@(...)` refers to an existing declaration. `((RELATION_TYPE))` names a defined Relation without a short operator. Only actual specialization carries inherited properties.
- `[int]`, `[string]`, `[bool]`, `[datetime]`, `[decimal]` and `[float]` name proposed value formats. Format is for value types only. List and map are carrier structures, not value Formats; child paths define nesting under CA-A-1283 and CA-A-1286. Carrier.Format continues to describe representation formats; Markdown/YAML/TOML/JSON are not placed under this new Format branch.
- General formula and function-style expressions are deferred to CA-A-1282. Existing-kind `@(...)` references remain; general property-value interpolation and executable composition do not enter this syntax increment. A1291 remains a separate bracketed-condition proposal, excluded from this review under A1297.
- Cardinalities under CA-A-1280: `{n}` means exactly n; `{n+}` means at least n without an upper bound; `{n..m}` is an inclusive range. Bounds are non-negative integers with n <= m. Common forms are `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0+}`, `{1+}` and `{0..1}`. A property suffix counts only its own direct values, never nested keys or child values; explicit `{0}` permits a grouping path with independently counted children; `>{1+}` and `>{0+}` count immediate parts per whole. Omitted counts remain unspecified; explicit `{0}` is used for grouping properties. No parser implementation is claimed.
- `[inherited]` marks actual specialization inheritance. Grouping and containment do not supply it. A local additive Status declaration retains inherited values.
- Omitted format or cardinality is undefined in this declaration. In particular, subjects without a suffix is not subjects{0}, subjects{1} or subjects{0+}. Explicit counts remain distinct; independently applicable rules still apply. CA-A-1284 records this distinction. Definition and rule references use Atom IDs only; no definition text is copied into the tree.
- Format annotations are proposed readable constraints unless a cited rule explicitly specifies the datatype. CA-A-1287 removes ref as a value Format. Reference-valued identifiers use string; their definitions preserve target meanings such as Actor, Scope Unit, Operator and Project. Existing-kind @ references are separate syntax and remain admitted.
- Base counts describe the complete-Atom contract, with the Claim structure in CA-A-1243 and the R-only formalization scope in CA-A-1244. Every complete RMED Atom has content.claim{1}. Only R admits an optional content.claim.formal_claim{0..1} child, alongside its mandatory direct prose. The formal child cannot satisfy the prose count. M/E/D keep prose Claims. The Role/Type defines what forms one complete Claim. No separate atom.claim/formal_claim or content.claim.prose field is used. Drafts may be incomplete. Project Goal ownership remains exceptional. Effective Label is required, but its stored explicit value is optional and falls back to Type.

## Cardinality notation

| Notation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{n}` | Exactly n | `{1}`: exactly one |
| `{n+}` | At least n, no upper bound | `{2+}`: two or more |
| `{n..m}` | From n to m, inclusive | `{2..5}`: two through five |
| `{0}` | No direct values or no contained parts | A group can still have declared child properties |
| `{0+}` | Zero or more direct values or parts | An optional multi-value property |
| `{1+}` | One or more | At least one part or value |
| `{0..1}` | Zero or one | An optional single value |
| `{0..m}` | At most m | `{0..3}`: zero through three |

The suffix counts only direct values at that path, or immediate parts per whole after >. It never counts nested keys. Grouping subjects{0} permits governs{1} and dependency{0+} as independently counted children. YAML sequences carry multiple values under one unique property key; list is not a value Format. The exactly-one immediate whole rule is unchanged. CA-A-1283 records this decision.

## Deferred formula proposal

General formula expressions are preserved separately in [CA-A-1282](../CA-A-1282-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--defer-general-formula-expressions.md), rather than admitted in this Model Draft. This includes composed ID values, property-value interpolation, formula grouping, function-style uniqueness expressions and calculated counts. Existing scalar IDs and their governing prose rules remain unchanged. Bracketed conditions and implicit value materialization remain separate proposals under A1291, outside the current review. The explicit execution function remains deferred. Cardinalities, formats, literal allowed values, relationship operators and existing-kind references stay in scope.

## Property and rule qualifications

Under A1296, YAML null and an empty string each count as one direct value; an omitted property has zero. YAML interpretation determines the value. Its Format and applicable prose conditions decide admissibility; the count alone does not. There is no universal null or empty-string prohibition.

Subject values use string under CA-A-1285. The basic format check validates the string and its admitted Model notation without requiring the target to pre-exist its defining Atom. A Definition may introduce its entity and governed path together. Syntax alone does not define the entity or grant authority.

- `id` and `version_number` use the Operator's latest example spellings. They do not rename `atom_id` or `version` in YAML. Use atom.version_number for the YAML part and atom.content.claim for the Markdown part. No atom.property, property/text subgroup or colon-based lookup layer is introduced.
- Version Number is positive and increases for updates. Tier uses [int] in this review packet. Its lower bound is -1; the numeric and more-specific conditions stay in prose under A1297: Project ordinary >=0, other ordinary >=1, Project Goal -1 with Operator ownership. No case-specific lookup function or conditional expression is needed. Numbers are graph ordering, not a second Global Tier.
- RMED content.claim_scope can be omitted only when the Claim covers the whole governed thing/topic and whole owning context. Conditional requirements still apply to a property shown as 0..1. Other Content Roles retain their registered scope contract.
- Analysis Question/Analysis counts depend on its applicable Type. Analysis Done is admitted by the applicable Analysis Report/Rationale rules, not asserted as a new universal Status on every Analysis Type.
- Every complete RMED Atom carries exactly one content.claim. Its own direct text is one required prose value. Only R admits optional content.claim.formal_claim with one fenced formal expression for now; M/E/D stay prose, including their syntax/format/relation policies and decisions. Illustrative code does not create an operative formal child. A Definition may combine required prose and optional complementary formal structure as one Type-defined unit, not separate Atoms for each representation or condition. Semantics is outside Claim and adds no operative constraints.
- The RMED section order is ## Summary, optional ## Claim scope, required ## Claim, optional ## Semantics, optional ## Details. R alone may add optional ### Formal claim under Claim. The Summary value is below ## Summary, not substituted into the heading. Optional sections are omitted when absent. A formal child needs a defined syntax/schema. All top-level RMED sections are siblings at ##; Summary never contains Claim. Heading hierarchy maps Claim → Formal claim to content.claim.formal_claim; normalized components are lowercase with spaces replaced by underscores and characters other than letters, numbers, underscore and hyphen stripped.
- Enabled Relations.Contains is a kind-level capability, with base default False and Plan/Workflow/Step enabling True. It is not a mandatory Boolean field to add to every Atom instance. The existing Step rule CA-R-1992 still describes nested Steps; this Draft retains its enabling value but follows the Operator's newer distinct-Substep decision for the contained kind.
- The Project Goal Owner targets Operator, Target Scope Unit targets Project, and its single Tier is exactly -1. Its absence of Local Scope Unit is the explicit exception, not permission to omit that field on ordinary Atoms.
- Governing Objects classifies Atom and Governing Configuration without granting additional authority to any Content Role. Structural Unit classifies Scope Unit; Project specializes Scope Unit and is its single parentless root. Scope Units recursively contain Scope Units and may contain Atom/Projection parts. No numeric structural rank or ownership-field rename is introduced by these groups.
- Event Record is declared only under History/Journal. Project Implementation specializes Package and is the root Package. Implementation is only a section heading. Package contains nested Packages, Modules, Prompts, runtime/evaluation Assets and Documentation; Code Units belong inside Modules, with Class and Function specializations. There is no separate Code kind in this proposed model. Prompt is executable instructions for an LLM AI Agent engine; Module is executable on its language engine; both runtime code and evaluation code, including tests, are Modules. Asset is non-executable Implementation content needed by runtime or evaluations. Documentation provides descriptive/reference information separately from those required inputs. Neither definition automatically captures every non-executable repository file. Module's one File Carrier and Package's proposed Directory representation remain distinct Delivery concerns. Documentation is a Package part separate from Asset. Resources is retired in this proposal under CA-A-1278; its non-executable implementation inputs specialize Asset. Containment does not confer property inheritance.
- Projection remains a direct Continuant and Terms Projection specializes it. Term remains separate as in the Operator's tree. This classification does not create a Terms Projection artifact or start Terms Graph implementation.
- Carrier, Actor, Execution, Project, History, Projection and their descendants do not inherit Scope Unit fields through the former Project Model grouping. The old projection's spurious Scope Unit subtree is excluded.
- Current source rules and operative formal graph-rule paths still use older Subject paths. This review Draft does not claim those paths were migrated to Model.

## Deferred or unresolved details

- Format has a new Definition Draft; individual primitive-format definitions remain to be completed before adoption. This Draft does not assert a closed primitive vocabulary, specific numeric precision, float special-value policy or reference encoding.
- Formula design and property-value bindings remain outside this adoption increment under CA-A-1282. A1295 permits future functions only when recurring patterns establish reusable operations that reduce overall complexity; no per-case or per-instance function proliferation is admitted. No new ID component field or contextual named Selection is created.
- Substep is a leaf: it calls one Action with parameters, cannot call a Workflow and cannot contain further Substeps. A leaf Step can call one Action or one Workflow with parameters; a Step containing Substeps has no own call. A1262–A1264 record these decisions. Catalog reconciliation and Substep numeric identity remain preparation work, not an open choice about the settled container hierarchy. Containment supplies no inheritance.
- Code Unit is declared under Module, with Class and Function as specializations. Modules belong to Packages; the former Code-versus-Package question is closed. Package is a declared kind; Project Implementation is its root specialization, not a containing Implementation kind. Tool is not a separate primary kind under CA-A-1273: use Scope Unit instances and existing Package implementation structure. R2197 is a retirement candidate; R2205 meaning is preserved in Engineering API Self Documentation. R2204 Effect Result meaning is mapped to Execution.Result under CA-A-1276; its API result contract stays in Engineering/API. Current retirement is pending. Current source definitions are not deleted by these candidate placements.
- The Operator confirms Workflow >{1+} Step >{0+} Substep. CA-A-1279 reconfirms this settled hierarchy with the latest cardinality spelling. It is prepared in Definition Drafts; Current source adoption is still pending.
- Complete Type inventories and property formats/counts absent from sources remain deferred. Useful legacy graph constraints need incorporation into the appropriate Definition Claims before retiring their Current sources. No Graph Rule instance registry or substitute Rule population is introduced.
- The read-only property inventory retains older direct labels for evidence. Retired Substance, Atom.Entity, duplicate Governed Subject vs Subjects.Governs, and accidental inherited Scope Unit fields are not copied into the Draft. No extra Scope Unit Status or Global Tier is introduced.

## General named relations

`Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` expresses the named directed Relation from Source to Target. Use this general form where no short operator exists; it may also spell a defined Relation explicitly without changing its meaning. The name between `((` and `))` identifies one declared Relation Type, not a new kind, arbitrary prose label or automatically registered Relation. Endpoint restrictions and counts come from the Relation definition and constraints in the relevant Model Definition Claim.

There is no separate backward notation. To navigate or display the opposite direction, use the defined derived inverse Relation name in the same form with the endpoints exchanged. Persist the direct fact only, not a second independent inverse fact. No inverse name or inverse meaning is guessed from spelling.

The matching unescaped `((` and `))` delimit the Relation Type name. Existing backslash escaping handles literal delimiter characters. Existing `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `::`, `>`, `@(...)` and format/cardinality annotations keep their meanings. The double parentheses are relation syntax, not a function invocation. This decision defines a binary relation expression; it does not silently choose precedence for arbitrary mixed chains or turn a whole relation statement into a node selector for subjects.governs.

The Operator supplied these schema-level examples:

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
Runtime ((EXECUTES)) Workflow Run
```

These expressions connect modeled kinds and do not create actual Runs or records. Their Relation Type definitions and derived-inverse declarations must be authored before source admission; notation alone does not establish that they are already registered. The Runtime in the last expression is the live executor, not the Engineering topic or stored engine Code.

Decision record: [CA-A-1240](../CA-A-1240-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--use-named-relation-notation.md).

## Definition, execution and record connections

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
```

Every Workflow Run executes exactly one Workflow; this binding is stated in prose rather than an undefined suffix on a named relation. Workflow is the reusable definition; Workflow Run is an actual Occurrent; Event Record is its persistent description in Journal. The displayed RECORDS target is one supported case, not a closed range restricting every record to Workflow Run. The inverse views HAS_EXECUTION and IS_RECORDED_BY are proposed in the two Definition Drafts; direct facts are stored once. No actual Run or record is created here.

## Step and Substep call boundaries

A leaf Step calls one Action or one Workflow with parameters. A Step containing Substeps makes no call of its own. A Substep is a leaf that calls one Action with parameters: no Workflow calls and no nested Substeps.

```text
Workflow >{1+} Step
Step >{0+} Substep
Substep >{0} @(Substep)
```

Containment connects a Workflow to its Steps and a Step to its Substeps. It does not mean the caller contains the called Workflow or Action definition. No wrapper Action or new execution kind is introduced for Workflow calls.

# Summary

Model draft: primary kinds and properties

## Status and scope

Review Draft extending Candidate #12 (CA-A-1238). The latest Operator naming decision is Model, replacing the earlier name Formal Model. Prepared selectors use Model::...; Current sources are not migrated by this proposal. Its five base branches are Continuant, Occurrent, Aspect, Carrier and Graph Syntax. Relation and value Format are grouped under Graph Syntax. Structural constraints belong to model Definition Claims, not a separate Graph Rule branch or instance population. Project Model is only an optional organizational view, not a base classification.

This Draft contains the primary tree, then one flat property block for every selected primary kind with known direct or inherited properties, in the same declaration order as the tree. It includes no named instances. It does not promote Drafts, migrate Current Atoms, rename YAML fields or change code. Terms Graph work and the function proposals in CA-A-1237 remain deferred.

Each property block shows its proposed full `subjects.governs` selector. These describe the proposed governing targets; they are not claims that existing source Atom headers already use the new paths. Inline cardinality/format annotations belong to Claims, not to these selectors.

## Reading the annotations

- `/` specializes; `::` groups; `>` contains, and each contained part belongs to exactly one whole; `@(...)` refers to an existing declaration. `((RELATION_TYPE))` names a defined Relation without a short operator. Only actual specialization carries inherited properties.
- `[int]`, `[string]`, `[bool]`, `[datetime]`, `[decimal]` and `[float]` name proposed value formats. Format is for value types only. List and map are carrier structures, not value Formats; child paths define nesting under CA-A-1283 and CA-A-1286. Carrier.Format continues to describe representation formats; Markdown/YAML/TOML/JSON are not placed under this new Format branch.
- General formula and function-style expressions are deferred to CA-A-1282. Existing-kind `@(...)` references remain; general property-value interpolation and executable composition do not enter this syntax increment. A1291 remains a separate bracketed-condition proposal, excluded from this review under A1297.
- Cardinalities under CA-A-1280: `{n}` means exactly n; `{n+}` means at least n without an upper bound; `{n..m}` is an inclusive range. Bounds are non-negative integers with n <= m. Common forms are `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0+}`, `{1+}` and `{0..1}`. A property suffix counts only its own direct values, never nested keys or child values; explicit `{0}` permits a grouping path with independently counted children; `>{1+}` and `>{0+}` count immediate parts per whole. Omitted counts remain unspecified; explicit `{0}` is used for grouping properties. No parser implementation is claimed.
- `[inherited]` marks actual specialization inheritance. Grouping and containment do not supply it. A local additive Status declaration retains inherited values.
- Omitted format or cardinality is undefined in this declaration. In particular, subjects without a suffix is not subjects{0}, subjects{1} or subjects{0+}. Explicit counts remain distinct; independently applicable rules still apply. CA-A-1284 records this distinction. Definition and rule references use Atom IDs only; no definition text is copied into the tree.
- Format annotations are proposed readable constraints unless a cited rule explicitly specifies the datatype. CA-A-1287 removes ref as a value Format. Reference-valued identifiers use string; their definitions preserve target meanings such as Actor, Scope Unit, Operator and Project. Existing-kind @ references are separate syntax and remain admitted.
- Base counts describe the complete-Atom contract, with the Claim structure in CA-A-1243 and the R-only formalization scope in CA-A-1244. Every complete RMED Atom has content.claim{1}. Only R admits an optional content.claim.formal_claim{0..1} child, alongside its mandatory direct prose. The formal child cannot satisfy the prose count. M/E/D keep prose Claims. The Role/Type defines what forms one complete Claim. No separate atom.claim/formal_claim or content.claim.prose field is used. Drafts may be incomplete. Project Goal ownership remains exceptional. Effective Label is required, but its stored explicit value is optional and falls back to Type.

## Cardinality notation

| Notation | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{n}` | Exactly n | `{1}`: exactly one |
| `{n+}` | At least n, no upper bound | `{2+}`: two or more |
| `{n..m}` | From n to m, inclusive | `{2..5}`: two through five |
| `{0}` | No direct values or no contained parts | A group can still have declared child properties |
| `{0+}` | Zero or more direct values or parts | An optional multi-value property |
| `{1+}` | One or more | At least one part or value |
| `{0..1}` | Zero or one | An optional single value |
| `{0..m}` | At most m | `{0..3}`: zero through three |

The suffix counts only direct values at that path, or immediate parts per whole after >. It never counts nested keys. Grouping subjects{0} permits governs{1} and dependency{0+} as independently counted children. YAML sequences carry multiple values under one unique property key; list is not a value Format. The exactly-one immediate whole rule is unchanged. CA-A-1283 records this decision.

## Deferred formula proposal

General formula expressions are preserved separately in [CA-A-1282](../CA-A-1282-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--defer-general-formula-expressions.md), rather than admitted in this Model Draft. This includes composed ID values, property-value interpolation, formula grouping, function-style uniqueness expressions and calculated counts. Existing scalar IDs and their governing prose rules remain unchanged. Bracketed conditions and implicit value materialization remain separate proposals under A1291, outside the current review. The explicit execution function remains deferred. Cardinalities, formats, literal allowed values, relationship operators and existing-kind references stay in scope.

## Property and rule qualifications

Under A1296, YAML null and an empty string each count as one direct value; an omitted property has zero. YAML interpretation determines the value. Its Format and applicable prose conditions decide admissibility; the count alone does not. There is no universal null or empty-string prohibition.

Subject values use string under CA-A-1285. The basic format check validates the string and its admitted Model notation without requiring the target to pre-exist its defining Atom. A Definition may introduce its entity and governed path together. Syntax alone does not define the entity or grant authority.

- `id` and `version_number` use the Operator's latest example spellings. They do not rename `atom_id` or `version` in YAML. Use atom.version_number for the YAML part and atom.content.claim for the Markdown part. No atom.property, property/text subgroup or colon-based lookup layer is introduced.
- Version Number is positive and increases for updates. Tier uses [int] in this review packet. Its lower bound is -1; the numeric and more-specific conditions stay in prose under A1297: Project ordinary >=0, other ordinary >=1, Project Goal -1 with Operator ownership. No case-specific lookup function or conditional expression is needed. Numbers are graph ordering, not a second Global Tier.

## General named relations

`Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` expresses the named directed Relation from Source to Target. Use this general form where no short operator exists; it may also spell a defined Relation explicitly without changing its meaning. The name between `((` and `))` identifies one declared Relation Type, not a new kind, arbitrary prose label or automatically registered Relation. Endpoint restrictions and counts come from the Relation definition and constraints in the relevant Model Definition Claim.

There is no separate backward notation. To navigate or display the opposite direction, use the defined derived inverse Relation name in the same form with the endpoints exchanged. Persist the direct fact only, not a second independent inverse fact. No inverse name or inverse meaning is guessed from spelling.

The matching unescaped `((` and `))` delimit the Relation Type name. Existing backslash escaping handles literal delimiter characters. Existing `/`, `//`, `.`, `:`, `::`, `>`, `@(...)` and format/cardinality annotations keep their meanings. The double parentheses are relation syntax, not a function invocation. This decision defines a binary relation expression; it does not silently choose precedence for arbitrary mixed chains or turn a whole relation statement into a node selector for subjects.governs.

The Operator supplied these schema-level examples:

```text
Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
Runtime ((EXECUTES)) Workflow Run
```

These expressions connect modeled kinds and do not create actual Runs or records. Their Relation Type definitions and derived-inverse declarations must be authored before source admission; notation alone does not establish that they are already registered. The Runtime in the last expression is the live executor, not the Engineering topic or stored engine Code.

Decision record: [CA-A-1240](../CA-A-1240-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--use-named-relation-notation.md).

Workflow Run ((IS_EXECUTION_OF)) Workflow
Event Record ((RECORDS)) Workflow Run
```

Every Workflow Run executes exactly one Workflow; this binding is stated in prose rather than an undefined suffix on a named relation. Workflow is the reusable definition; Workflow Run is an actual Occurrent; Event Record is its persistent description in Journal. The displayed RECORDS target is one supported case, not a closed range restricting every record to Workflow Run. The inverse views HAS_EXECUTION and IS_RECORDED_BY are proposed in the two Definition Drafts; direct facts are stored once. No actual Run or record is created here.

## Step and Substep call boundaries

A leaf Step calls one Action or one Workflow with parameters. A Step containing Substeps makes no call of its own. A Substep is a leaf that calls one Action with parameters: no Workflow calls and no nested Substeps.

```text
Workflow >{1+} Step
Step >{0+} Substep
Substep >{0} @(Substep)
```

Containment connects a Workflow to its Steps and a Step to its Substeps. It does not mean the caller contains the called Workflow or Action definition. No wrapper Action or new execution kind is introduced for Workflow calls.

# Summary

Entity graph candidate with four root branches

## Root decision

Entity is the single root. Every primary graph node and every dependent property is an Entity. Object is narrower: Objects are the abstractions described by the framework, with Continuant and Occurrent specializations. Not every Entity is an Object.

Carrier is a sibling root branch, not a specialization of Object/Continuant. It describes how Objects or their information are represented/stored. A live Occurrent is not stored as the occurrence itself; a persistent record about it can have a Carrier. Do not conflate the occurrence with its record.

## Primary structure — three levels

```text
Entity
	/Object
		/Continuant
		/Occurrent
	/Aspect
		/Design
		/Documentation Aspect
		/Domain
		/Engineering
		/Product
		/Project Aspect
		/UX
	/Graph Syntax
		> Relation
		> Format
		> Cardinality
	/Carrier
		/Database
		/Directory
		/Docker Image
		/File
		/Git Branch
		/Git Commit
		/Git Index
		/Git Repository
		/Pull Request
```

This is the current classification skeleton, not a new namespace or project-scope hierarchy. Retain organizational/provenance views separately. The previous detailed candidate A1239 supplies the lower-level inventory pending remapping; do not treat its old Model root or bare Definition Type as the latest decision. Term and Selection placements remain explicit follow-up work rather than silently declaring that every Entity is an Object.

## Operations Types

```text
Atom/Content Role: Operations
	/Type: Workflow
		>{1+} Atom/Content Role: Operations/Type: Step
			>{0+} Atom/Content Role: Operations/Type: Sub-step
	/Type: Action
```

These are fully qualified Operations Atom Types. Repeat the Role/Type at each containment boundary rather than relying on inheritance through >. Step and Sub-step are declared only inside their required containers. Keep the settled leaf-call and recursion rules. A1304 defines the explicit presentation and operator spacing; relative-navigation syntax remains undecided.

## Relation Definition Type and notation

R/Type: Relation Definition defines named Relation Types. content.notation_for_subject is a fenced Markdown property under ## Notation for subject when a short Subject notation is defined. Retained short operators are :, >, /, // and .; their actual meaning/direction stays with the corresponding Relation Definition. The general named form remains ((RELATION_TYPE)). No organizational :: operator is needed in this candidate.

## Definition coverage

Every Entity, including a dependent property, needs R/Type: Entity Definition authority. Reuse existing Rs that already define it before creating missing Definitions. Each property's governing Entity Definition must state its cardinality and value format in the Formal claim. Preserve the settled direct-value semantics: counts are independent of child properties, subjects{0} allows declared children, an omitted count is undefined, and list/map/ref are not value Formats.
