# Summary

Replace overly broad child_of and parent_of relations

## Objective

Replace generic Atom parentage with precise relations. Preserve the meaning of each supported link, distinguish refinement from a separate constraint, and retire child_of / parent_of after their Current uses and consumers are resolved.

## Details

This is a separate Epic, not a change to [CA-P-1959](18-CA-P-1959-EPIC--improve-entity-model-stage-2.md). The Operator requested its creation instead of starting the migration. No relation definition, link, runtime behavior or projection changes as part of creating this Plan.

### Accepted direction

- Reuse existing precise relations: IS_CONTAINED_BY for containment; derived_from for provenance; method_for, evaluation_for, delivery_for and rationale_for for their distinct purposes; depends_on for a real prerequisite.
- Add refines for a more specific statement of the same rule or Claim: same-role RMED, compatible applicability and no contradiction on shared scope.
- Add is_constrained_by when an RMED Atom must obey a separate explicit normative RMED constraint. This is not the same fact as serving or evaluating a Requirement.
- Neither new relation grants automatic inheritance or permission to override its target. Do not recreate generic tier-parent traversal under another name.
- Store only the direct relation. Derive inverse views; do not author duplicate inverse lists. IS_CONTAINED_BY remains child to container, with CONTAINS derived.
- Do not replace links by Content Role alone. For example, an M Atom can both serve an R Atom and be constrained by it; method_for does not automatically replace its old authority link.

### Work sequence

This grouping Plan has no own implementation work. Before execution, create bounded child Tasks with at most 15 minutes of own work each.

1. [ ] Inventory Current source definitions, child_of / parent_of uses, and affected registry, validation, query and projection consumers. Follow configured authority paths, not delivery mirrors. Record supported mappings and unresolved cases with source IDs, Versions and reasons; do not infer meaning from relation names or role letters alone.
2. [ ] Update RMEDO first. Define the two new relation meanings and descriptive metadata; put endpoint permissions and other constraints in the separate rule contracts. Align conflicting parentage Requirements and Evaluations. Reuse generic direct-relation Delivery policies where they already fit. Starting points include R879, R796, R833, R806, M120, D268 and their actual current dependants.
3. [ ] Align the existing runtime registry, validator and affected callers with the accepted contracts. Add focused positive and negative tests for the new kinds, retained precise links, direct/inverse storage and the absence of automatic authority inheritance. Do not add a new rule engine or a parallel migration framework.
4. [ ] Migrate supported links in bounded batches. Preserve exact predecessors; increment Version once per real same-ID update and use the actual update time. Leave unrelated content unchanged. Keep ambiguous links explicitly queued instead of forcing a mapping, deleting their meaning or declaring their migration complete. Current means non-archived, not only Status Active.
5. [ ] Rebuild the affected derived views and verify the actual source links. Finish retirement of child_of / parent_of only after their Current uses and required consumers are resolved. Keep archived history readable and unchanged.

### Known review cases

- M297 currently carries both child_of and method_for to R1487: distinguish the two facts before replacing either.
- R951 to R933 is a candidate for same-rule refinement, subject to current source review.
- R796 to R1174 needs its exact constraint or Goal-contribution meaning established; a specification link is not proof that a Goal was achieved.
- E207 to R815, D250 to M261 and M160 to M110 need their current endpoints or governing propositions resolved before mapping.

These are review leads, not a complete migration map or permission to reuse old Version/hash pins. Reopen the current sources before execution. General unrelated content migration remains [CA-P-1970](19-CA-P-1970-EPIC--align-atom-content-after-subject-migration.md).

### Definition of Done

The two precise kinds and their required source/runtime contracts agree. Every old Current parentage link has a supported disposition and verified effect; unresolved cases keep this Epic incomplete. Required consumers no longer depend on the retired pair. Focused tests and rebuilt views reflect the actual result, direct relations have no authored inverse duplicates, and exact predecessor history is preserved. No hidden inheritance, guessed mapping, unrelated content migration or deployment is included.

Resolve Candidate #10 review findings

## Objective

After the FPF review, resolve its findings with the Operator and refine the proposal and Drafts. Ask one context-rich question at a time for unresolved choices. Promotion and migration require a later explicit step.

## Details

Candidate: [A1218](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1218-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--subject-model-candidate-10.md). The proposal holds the structure and definitions; this Task holds work, progress and links to decision proposals.

Latest Operator decisions supersede incompatible earlier messages. Scope: main Subjects and their definitions, without instances or property enumeration.

## Definition of Done

The stated deliverable is present and checked. Draft preparation, review, adoption and graph rebuild remain separate outcomes.

## Review decisions

Review: [Candidate10 FPF design challenge](../../../../fpf-reports/20261027T134959Z-fpf-design-challenge-subject-model-candidate-10-review.md).

### C10-I01 / C10-F01 — resolved; clarification Drafted

Decision: [A1219 — Clarify mixed Subject targets](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1219-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--clarify-mixed-subject-targets.md). Operator-accepted; reflected in R1994@11-draft, R2209@1-draft and Candidate #10. No Current RMED promotion.

### C10-I02 — resolved; C10-F02 superseded; replacement clarification Drafted

Decision: [A1220 — Define Project as a whole entity](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1220-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--define-project-as-a-whole-entity.md). Operator-defined meaning is reflected in R2220@1-draft and Candidate #10. C10-F02 was not adopted as written. No Current RMED promotion.

## Decision storage

Save each accepted review decision as one Analysis Atom of Type Specification Proposal, in its own file. This Task tracks its status and links to it; it does not duplicate the decision text. An unanswered question is not an accepted decision.

## Resolution state

Both review findings have Operator dispositions, each in its own Specification Proposal file. The corresponding Definition Drafts and Candidate are refined. The saved FPF report remains the historical review; its original OPEN states are not rewritten. Adoption and migration remain separate.

## Completion

Both FPF findings have Operator decisions recorded separately in A1219 and A1220. R1994, R2209 and R2220 Drafts match those decisions. Candidate #10 and its source links are checked. Current RMED is not promoted; source adoption and migration remain outside this Task.

# Summary

Map Candidate #10 Governs Subjects

## Objective

Map the selected Current RMEDO Atoms’ Governs Subjects to the accepted Candidate #10 structure before mapping dependencies.

## Details

Start with a fresh inventory of the Current Requirement, Method, Evaluation, Delivery and Operations source set used by the Subject Graph. Record the actual source boundary and counts; do not assume the earlier snapshot count remains current. Treat the prepared 42 Drafts as a separate proposed input, not Current sources.

Continue the existing thin change table in P2675 as the single live inventory. Keep four columns: Atom ID | old Subject | new Subject | status. Use a Governs section first; link real Drafts from the Atom IDs. Do not create a second map with copied Claims, hashes or extended analyses.

Map by meaning, using A1218 and the accepted A1219/A1220 decisions. Shared concepts use the CAPRMEDIO namespace; project-specific concepts use the project namespace. Owning Scope Unit does not select the Subject namespace. Do not copy Tool or Scope Unit names into topic branches.

Create or refine only the necessary source-update Drafts as mappings become supported. Reuse the prepared next-version Draft instead of creating another successor for the same source. Keep unrelated content unchanged. Mark unsupported mappings explicitly; ask the Operator one concrete question at a time below 90% confidence and save each accepted decision in its own Specification Proposal.

## Definition of Done

Every selected Current Governs Subject has an evidenced proposed target, unchanged disposition or explicit unresolved question. The thin inventory and actual Drafts agree; no source promotion or migration has run.


## References

- [A1218 — Candidate #10](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1218-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--subject-model-candidate-10.md).
- [A1219 — Mixed Subject targets](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1219-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--clarify-mixed-subject-targets.md).
- [A1220 — Project as a whole entity](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1220-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--define-project-as-a-whole-entity.md).
- [P2675 — Existing thin Draft/change inventory](02-CA-P-2675-TASK--draft-main-subject-definitions.md).

## Progress

Fresh inventory: 2,258 Current RMEDO Atoms. The first 803 Engineering, UX and Documentation Governs changes are Drafted; Current sources remain unchanged. Remaining source groups are being resolved before dependency mapping.


### Retained temporal classifications

Decision: [A1221](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1221-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--retain-continuant-and-occurrent-subjects.md). R1967 and R1972 are Subject-mapping Drafts; their meanings are unchanged.

### Formal references and generic Type rules

- [CA-A-1222](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1222-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--update-formal-subject-references.md).
- [CA-A-1223](../../../02_analysis/done/CA-A-1223-SPECIFICATION_PROPOSAL--govern-nodes-with-generic-type-rules.md).

## Result

All 2,258 Current RMEDO Atoms have a recorded Governs disposition in P2675. 2,240 successor Drafts are staged; 12 have unchanged Governs and six have no Governs to change. Fifteen new definition Drafts are tracked separately. No Current RMEDO source changed. Generic Type rules use Graph/Node; D393 uses Atom.Type. Existing Term paths move under Project Model/Term; Terms Graph work stays deferred.

Try R/Scope Definition in place of Goal: the Scope is the Scope Unit's purpose, responsibility, expected results and boundary, not merely a container address. ## Concrete writer defect — CA #3

The release copy phase reads Authority paths, drops each declared Delivery path, and builds the target from `source.name`. It would recreate the three ID-prefixed directories after the verified physical rename.

Required behavior:

1. Read source bytes from the declared Authority paths.
2. Write each copied subtree to its declared Delivery path, using the existing layout resolver where applicable.
3. Preserve copied file bytes and canonical Authority sources.
4. Verify that the next copy produces `LAYER_1_CORE_META_MODEL`, `LAYER_2_INSTALLED_EXTENSIONS` and `LAYER_3_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION`, without recreating their ID-prefixed siblings.

The static trace is in `coverage/folder-derivation-live-check-20261105/writer-static-audit.json` in the completion packet. CA #3 owns the implementation and focused writer verification, followed by the existing final integration gates. The source lane has made no implementation change.

## Root ID and bootstrap cutover — CA #3

The accepted Project root ID is `CA-SU-00`. `CA-SU--1` identifies the predefined Scope Unit named `world`, without a Declaration. The root Declaration Atom uses `container.scope_unit: CA-SU--1`; the Project Scope Unit itself keeps no formal parent.

The current reader accepts only the root Name statement and identifies the root by an absent ID. Its model/validator rejects a root ID. Before promotion:

1. Accept the root Declaration's ID and preserve both zeroes in `CA-SU-00` as text. Root identity follows the Project kind, not an absent ID. Shared rules support other Project ID namespaces.
2. Resolve `CA-SU--1` to predefined world without requiring or creating a World Declaration, Carrier or folder. Reject a supplied Declaration reusing that reserved ID.
3. Include the Project root in declared-ID uniqueness checks. Keep world separate from the Declaration count: the current baseline is 46 Declarations plus predefined world.
4. Read the one-key `Header.Container` mapping. Resolve base Atom IDs to Current and Scope Unit IDs to the declared or predefined Scope Unit. Apply the omitted-root-Declaration default mapping to world. Store no duplicate containment fact in Relations.
5. Preserve unordered/no-number/no-parent Project behavior and `.caprmedio_<project name>` root naming. Verify the bootstrap Declaration's adapter admission and placement before carrier migration.
6. Keep the source Current until the compatible reader, model, validator and adapter are ready. Verify the coordinated candidate through the existing admission and integration gates below.

The pinned static evidence is `coverage/project-root-id-20261105/static-impact/report.json` in the completion packet. Source Draft writes are not reader acceptance or runtime evidence.

## CFEL and single-person source cutover — CA #3

The reviewed candidate is `coverage/value-relations-20261105/final-live-cohort.json` in the completion packet. Its 49 Drafts are not Current syntax. The Operator requires source-first sequencing: complete and review CFEL, migrate Current and Draft Atoms in place, check that migration, then send CA #3 the implementation handoff. After that handoff, the required compatibility work is:

1. Distinguish HAS_ALLOWED_VALUE (`:=`, OR across applicable and inherited admissions) from HAS_VALUE_CONSTRAINT (`::`, AND across applicable and inherited constraints). With no admissions, omit that group. Preserve qualified-Subject `:=` and `{::n}` allowed cardinalities.
2. Support the accepted typed logical participants, `//` narrowing, `/` containment, scoped IF/THEN and FOR EACH groups, explicit bindings, and `# model` / `# instances`. Remove modeled CFEL Operator descriptor dependencies while preserving Actor/Operator.
3. Implement the final reviewed canonical-Relation and inverse-alias contract. Preserve model references such as Relation//CONTAINS and the declared IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR binding. Keep literal/constraint endpoint domains and zero-default bounds; do not restore separate inverse facts or infer reverse permissions.
4. Implement Atom-owned storage: Header.Relations is the default for outgoing canonical facts about the Atom; IS_CONTAINED_BY uses Header.Container. Header.Relations is optional and stores no inverse alias or duplicate containment. Coordinate the single-person schema/registry changes. Current R1559@28 and E440@38 already govern threshold-and-permission approval; the other attribution and root-ID changes remain staged. Preserve accepted historical records.
5. Use the existing Project-global identity boundary for allocation and application. The repaired value Relation IDs are R2826–R2829; retained history and all statuses reserve IDs. Keep other owners' Workbench sources intact.
6. Record semantic/parser/admission and integration results on one stable candidate through the five checks below. Source receipts and refreshed projections alone do not satisfy them.

## Remaining checks

1. The source lane verifies final Declaration counts, identities, derived paths and source hashes. Explain every digest change from preserved source evidence. CA #3 fixes and verifies the concrete Delivery writer defect above before the final stable-candidate checks.
2. Reconcile the legacy scope-field disposition from Current authority and identify a valid Current execution binding for every required operation. CA #3 owns matching implementation, registry/fixture changes and tests; a retired or archived carrier is not a Current replacement. The missing actual CA-O-104 Review Workflow remains a distinct source-authority issue and cannot be filled by a projection or installed copy.
3. CA #3 verifies live Project admission and fresh Docker query/status and lifecycle checks, including the W10 result/timestamp comparison, on the stable candidate.
4. CA #3 runs the complete current-source suite and launcher on that same stable candidate. Record exact implementation, source and image identities, results and cleanup. These checks remain pending until an actual terminal result is recorded; focused or mixed-state runs do not satisfy them.
5. Preserve the explicit O016 expected-failure disposition under P2708. It does not waive unrelated failures. Actual Workflow-instance migration remains separately deferred; do not conflate it with the missing CA-O-104 source or with the settled Occurrent kind decisions.

## Status

Active. Focused tests and source adoption receipts do not close this gate. No release is required.

- Keep Atom.Header and Atom.Content, an empty Claim container with one or two Formal Claim / Prose Claim children, declared heading interpretation, one canonical Relation Declaration with inverse aliases, and the removal of the @ reference operator.
- Atom.Header.Container is one mapping with exactly one key: scope_unit for a stable Scope Unit ID, or atom for an Atom ID. Store no Scope Unit name, name suffix or path. Resolve current names and physical destinations from the referenced identity. The root Project Declaration Atom uses scope_unit: CA-SU--1. This resolves to predefined world; it is not an unlinked scalar literal. Header.Relations stays optional and carries no duplicate containment fact. Formal Scope Unit parentage remains in its Declaration.

Keep formal containment only: a Step Run has one Workflow Run or Step Run parent; an Action Run launched by a Step Run belongs to that Step Run. Add explicit directional permissions without a general Run root or child-execution-count rule.

- P2695–P2706 and P2709 have recorded completed, bounded results. Preserve their history. P2708 owns the separately deferred O016 desired-behavior item.
- The Scope Unit source cutover, TOML retirement, Header/Claim/alias migration, Subject-root migration and CFEL grouping migration have application and preservation evidence.
- The earlier seven-view MODEL projection baseline used 1,159 pinned Current suppliers and Project root ownership. The graph reader passed 426 tests; the projection generator passed ten tests. Current admission passed 588 tests. These are focused results, not the final integration gate.

One original Declaration is archived and three Workbench Declarations were added; all 43 surviving original Claims and metadata match after the reviewed namespace and Formal Claim wrapping changes. This bounded source snapshot does not close stable-candidate integration.
- The previous Epic version preserves the detailed checkpoint history. The acceptance matrix retains all 23 requirement groups and their evidence. These baselines do not close the remaining gates.

- The Goal/Tier batch has 15 verified source contributions and exact predecessors. Seventeen reviewed Settings contributions merge logical ownership under Project.Settings; 25 ambiguous Settings sources remain held. R2747 and R2748 use fresh IDs because their Summaries changed.
- Source checkpoint a02ac7b83bf4561c7ad18b69ce9b6436dcbb02bf is reported pushed to amm/dev. It includes Goal/Tier, Settings, capability-deferral, containment-permission and refreshed-view source batches. Later code/runtime and fixture repairs remain uncommitted; this checkpoint is not final integration evidence.

- The capability deferral batch preserves confidence constraints in two revised Declarations and retires three redundant Tool/Extension Settings sources. Exact archives and frozen references remain. That earlier refreshed audit reported 56 missing and 23 unresolved Declaration-coverage cases.

## Responsibility and external dependencies

This Epic's source lane owns MODEL, CFEL, Declaration and Atom source decisions, edits, preservation and source-level review. CA #3 owns implementation and runtime changes, fixtures, regression work, and execution of the test and integration gates named below. Those are mandatory external dependencies for closure: do not count source receipts, focused source checks or unrun tests as completed gates, and do not remove them from the Definition of Done. Root coordinates source adoption, projection refresh and acceptance evidence. This plan authorizes no implementation or test execution in the source lane.

The current 11 Occurrent Declaration proposals reflect the settled Operator decisions: retain Execution, Workflow Run, Step Run, Action Run, Runtime, Session and Event; Runtime's four Internal/External Local/Remote variants are relative to the CAPRMEDIO application, and Local means on the Operator's machine; Session is narrower than External Remote Runtime; no Substep Run is added. The remaining source gates are Current pin and consumer reconciliation, endpoint/inverse-permission review, source adoption and faithful projections. Event Record direction and cardinality choices are already recorded; preserve those decisions. Runtime candidates remain unpromoted until those gates pass.


IS_BLOCKED_BY is canonical from the dependent Plan to its prerequisite; BLOCKS is its inverse alias. Store one canonical fact. The six-Atom source batch includes endpoint permissions, Delivery, authoring and Evaluation. Source migration preserves the meaning of prerequisite-side facts when normalizing their direction; CA #3 receives the checked source handoff for implementation and runtime conformance.

The Operator excludes Workbench and Workflows from this source lane: their agents own that work. Keep their required Epic gates as external dependencies. Core Occurrent and Relation Declaration sources remain this lane’s responsibility; their prepared Drafts are unpromoted pending source review. Actual Workflow definitions, execution instances and runtime behavior remain with their owners.

Term Definition is now an admitted Method Form under R2765. M450 is the sole Current ID Term meaning owner; exact R2275@2 is retired. Ten of the twelve Entity/Property Drafts remain held for Subject and scope repairs. R1318 is promoted with Term Property-bearing permissions. M451 defines Entity as anything represented in the Subject graph. Relation and Term remain separate from Node and declare their own Property-bearing rules; narrower entities inherit those rules.

## CFEL specification audit

1. Every admitted operator, Relation and expression construct has defining authority.
2. Each Atom governs one actual active Subject; its normative Claims stay within that Subject.
3. Vocabulary and notation are coherent. Keep necessary meaning, constraints and brief Relation Semantics; remove staging notes and redundant rules.
4. Use simple explicit syntax. Resolve ambiguity with the Operator before admission.
5. HAS_ALLOWED_VALUE uses `:=`; applicable and inherited admissions combine with OR. HAS_VALUE_CONSTRAINT uses `::`; applicable and inherited constraints combine with AND. Omit an absent allowed-value group. Combine the present groups with AND. Qualified Subjects retain `:=`; allowed cardinalities use `{::n}`. Review the staged successors and migrate by context before activating the new syntax. `?==` defines a missing effective Property value, `=` tests a condition, and `==` states a required or derived value. The Project confidence default is 90 in the integer range 0..100. Do not infer a Property rename.
6. IF bindings last through the condition and matching THEN group; standalone typed bindings last through the CFEL block. A new binding uses another name.
7. Mixed AND/OR uses parentheses. Quote text when needed; use escaped double quotes and backslashes.
8. Review the full Current CFEL specification census semantically; operator-use scans and hash checks alone do not prove this audit complete.

Workbench and Workflow definitions remain owned by other agents. Their illustrative use in a CFEL example does not exclude the CFEL specification itself from this audit.

## Declarative notation proposal

CA-A-1321@1-draft records the settled design and the 49 live successor Drafts. Keep Current syntax until coordinated source adoption and migration are ready.

- CFEL states constraints, relationships and required values; Workflows perform changes.
- The Operator accepted `<Node>` for a Model-defined object kind used as a Format.
- The proposed instance forms are anonymous `$<Node>` and named `$x[<Node>]`.
- The proposed `/` means containment and `//` means narrowing. Preserve relationship direction, inherited rules and endpoint count meaning during review.

# Summary

Unify installation **and** local/public release cycles

## Objective

The caprmedio Project provides simple, tested Local and Public release workflows and a reusable Framework package with an isolated runtime for each Project.

## Details

### Current Operator-approved scope

This direct happy path replaces the earlier release-sealing design. Release hashes, snapshots, admission records, package selectors, rollback, compatibility migration and recovery machinery are not prerequisites for these workflows. Preserve existing historical records; do not replay their Runs.

There are two Operator-invoked workflows. Neither runs automatically.

### Local release

Commit **everything** in Git before **every** step below, and once more at the end. Respect Git ignore rules and secret exclusions. Stop on a failed commit or step and write an issue report for manual handling; do not continue or roll back automatically.

1. Test the tools used by this release path.
2. Clear the product contents in `101_FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY`, preserving configuration, then copy the active Methodology-source Atoms from the Project's declared source folders. Exclude drafts and archives; ignore `.DS_Store`. Copy the supporting files needed by the compiler.
3. Compile Applicable Methodology in the product directory.
4. Replace the installed Methodology at `.caprmedio_caprmedio/000_CAPRMEDIO_framework` with the product as-is, preserving existing configuration.
5. Copy the Engine, delivered Methodology, locked dependencies and `ca` Skill into the reusable `.caprmedio_install` package; install that package into this Project's `.caprmedio_runtime` and install the project-local `ca` Skill. Preserve runtime configuration and existing Project records.
6. Build and start the Docker runtime; verify the actual returned MCP endpoint.
7. Remove only superseded images proven to belong to this Project. Retain current, unrelated and in-use images; report anything that cannot safely be removed.

The Project's editable Atoms remain in `.caprmedio_caprmedio`; `101_FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY` is the product; `000_CAPRMEDIO_framework` is the installed version. Project settings, structure, Operator registry and existing runtime configuration are not replaced. Other Projects and their runtimes remain separate.

### Public release

Test the intended release tools. Use one prompt for the full PR description, including What's new and What's fixed, and its concise bullet summary for Version History. Update README as needed. Version History contains only the summary and the actual PR link. Commit everything before each step and at the end, push to `amm/dev`, and create or update the PR to `main`; do not merge.

Local numbering adds/increments the fourth numeric component. Public numbering increments the third component and removes the fourth. Neither has a digit rollover.

### Implementation and work organization

- Keep both workflows available through Project MCP.
- Local release is programmatic; Public release has one content prompt.
- Concrete release Operations are Project-local. Their helper specifications and implementation belong to PROJECT_TOOLS; do not ship Project release procedures as general Methodology.
- Reuse existing compiler, installer and startup code only where it does not reintroduce the removed release prerequisites.
- Refactor the existing release entrypoints rather than adding parallel functions or capabilities. Disable release behavior outside the steps listed here.
- Journal actual workflow/action outcomes and keep a readable report. A queued Run, mock test or historical pass is not completed live execution.
- The existing decomposing Plans retain useful implementation responsibilities. Their snapshot, admission, recovery and complete-corpus test obligations are superseded by this current scope.
- Git and live effects have one owner; independent code, tests and documentation can be delegated.
- A workflow failure records its step and error. Further handling is manual.

- Completion evidence: Both direct workflows are implemented and their intended tests passed (16 tests, 19.160 seconds). Local Run epic1848-direct-local-20261012-001 copied and compiled active Methodology, preserved configuration, installed the package/runtime/ca Skill and demonstrated Docker MCP; see .caprmedio_runtime/simple_local_release/reports/epic1848-direct-local-20261012-001.md and .caprmedio_tmp/epic1848/direct-local-completion.md. Public Run epic1848-direct-public-20261012-001 completed for version 0.4.3, pushed to amm/dev and created PR 27 with complete notes and the actual Version History link. Final authority review resolved R-1922/R-1924 and retired O-198; unused legacy release code remains deferred outside this direct path.
- Public evidence: Run epic1848-direct-public-20261012-001 completed for 0.4.3; PR https://github.com/anatoly-m-maslennikov/caprmedio-graph-driven-framework/pull/27. Journal started Event 803fbb4b-8b3a-4a2a-9839-a65251d46e02; completed Event 8bdb213a-13be-4f26-9c87-0a44dfc30b34.

- Public completion receipt: .caprmedio_tmp/epic1848/direct-public-completion.md.

- No-merge correction verified: new Public PRs are created Draft and an existing open PR is converted to Draft before editing. Five focused Public tests passed; PR 27's earlier external bot merge remains recorded rather than rolled back.

## Definition of Done

The Epic is Done only when both updated workflow implementations and their intended tests are complete, the Local release has actually copied and compiled active Methodology, preserved configuration, installed the reusable package and Project runtime/Skill, and demonstrated Docker MCP operation. Public release must produce the requested description/history format, push to amm/dev and create or update its PR to main without merging. Before marking completion, record actual evidence for each in-scope decomposing Plan and report remaining manual issues. Do not claim a release or PR that was not executed.

# Summary

Align Subject and Subject-link definitions

## Objective

Align the governing Subject definitions with Operator decision D01:
Subject names the thing or topic an Atom governs or depends on.
Define GOVERNS / DEPENDS_ON separately as the special relations from an Atom
to nodes in the Subject graph; their defining Atoms depend_on the Subject
definition.

## Details

handles the accepted open categories of Graph Nodes. Estimated own work: up to 15 minutes.

  definitions. The review observed R1275@24 and R2006@7; those are evidence
  references, not fixed execution pins.
- Keep the Subject definition to the Operator's exact sentence above; remove
  its old relation-only meaning. Do not fold relation definitions into it.
- Define GOVERNS / DEPENDS_ON in their own Atoms. Reuse existing definitions
  where their identities and meaning fit; add the typed depends_on relation
  from each defining Atom to the Subject-definition Atom.
- The set of Subjects forms a graph. The Atom is the source of GOVERNS /
  DEPENDS_ON, and the addressed Subject graph node is the target. A path
  names the target, not the relation itself.
- Preserve the distinction between an object and its description. Do not mint
  another intermediate Subject object, new Domain entity, relation kind,
  authority precedence rule or generic named Selection.
- Keep role, Type and Local Scope Unit independent from Subject. Coordinate
  with P2641's open Continuant/Occurrent/Aspect categories; no new taxonomy
  or bulk remapping is part of this Task.
- Use normal predecessor history for changed Current definitions; leave
  existing Drafts, Archives and unrelated sources unchanged.

  conflict. Split further work into a separate Task rather than expanding this
  one beyond its own-work estimate.

  be named without inventing a new identity or temporal classification.
- No touched definition still calls Subject itself the Atom-to-target link.

  not report a projection rebuild or complete I01 closure that did not occur.

# Summary

Subject graph FPF refinement

## Objective

Resolve the Subject Graph content review with the Operator, one question at a
time. Turn accepted decisions into bounded child Tasks, then correct the source
Atoms and rebuild the affected Subject views.

## Details

### Starting point

The FPF alignment audit of 2026-10-26 found eight open issues in the Current
RMEDO Subject Graph and its governing sources. The reviewed projection is
[CA-PROJ-009](../../_projection/CA-PROJ-009-CAPRMEDIO--Subject-Graph--Current-RMEDO.md),
recorded rebuild 2026-10-26 02:53:08 +0400, with 2,238 sources.

The audit inspected selected source bodies, not every source body. Its findings
and suggested repairs are not approved model changes. Current sources must be
read again before a Task changes them. Latest explicit Operator decisions win.

### Findings to resolve

| ID | Issue and source leads | State |
|---|---|---|
| I01 | R1994@8 limits Graph Nodes to Continuant/Occurrent, while R2006@7 admits abstract topics. R1275@24 defines Subject as the link rather than its target. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I02 | D651@5/D652@7 use Carrier/Filename/Atom.Tier; D525@11 places persistent-state Carrier under Runtime. Check kind, property and representation meanings. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I03 | R2001@9/R1269@23 exclude Claim for Graph Rules, while R2150@4/M232@24 describe additive inheritance without the applicability exception. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I04 | R2003@7/R2149@7 operative Graph Rule YAML and R1997@10/D637@17 examples retain retired root paths. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I05 | D478@20/D480@15/D485@14 still govern Atom.Property; R1454@22 references Atom.Substance; O045@15 retains Atom.Atom/Tier. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I06 | R1617@13 treats derivation-evidence classification as a Relation Type; R1653@24 admits imprecise related_to. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I07 | R1989@9 and R868@25 disagree about archived Status, Version and Updated At. Distinguish an update predecessor from standalone archival. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |
| I08 | R1564@17/R1565@14 retain Actor as an Operations Type alongside Workflow, Step and Action. Preserve real participation policies when resolving it. | Applied; source checks PASS; bounded FPF alignment PASS |

D01–D08 supplied the accepted repair authority. The original no-Claim and
parallel-derivation-class proposals were rejected by later Operator decisions;
they were not implemented. Optional new design improvements remain proposals.

### Decision process

1. Ask one question with the conflicting source meanings, a proposed resolution,
   and its blast radius. Start with I01, because it affects every later mapping.
2. Record the Operator's answer here. Do not ask again where the latest answer
   already resolves a later issue.
3. Create child Task Atoms from accepted decisions. Each has a bounded source
   set, preserved obligations, dependencies and a checkable completion condition.
   Split own work into at most 15-minute Tasks where practical.
4. Track each issue as decided, tasked, applied and verified. A decision or
   Draft alone is not an applied correction.
5. After the accepted source corrections, rebuild affected views and check the
   specific findings and affected neighbors. Do not restart a general audit.

### Open questions and evidence gaps

- Q01 / G01: Subject/link distinction decided below; implementation tracked by
  P2640, applied and independently verified.
- Q02 / I01: decided by D02. Continuant, Occurrent and Aspect are permitted,
  and the category list is open. P2641 records applied and independently verified source alignment.
- Q03 / I03 and Q04: resolved for this refinement by D04. Every RMED Atom has
  a logical Claim; its representation is not fixed universally. Formal Claims
  may be carried by an Atom or Governing Configuration. No forced conversion
  or test based on the presence of a Semantics section is authorized.
- Q05 / G02: resolved by D05. Standalone archival preserves the existing
  Version; do not create a new Version merely to archive it. P2644 tracks
  alignment with the already-agreed update-predecessor behavior.
- Q06 / I06: resolved by D06/D07. Use explicit derivation between Relation
  Types and retire the old Relation Derivation Class definition. P2645/P2646
  track the accepted work. The prior typed-only decision already supplies the
  direction for related_to; do not ask for that policy again. P2648 tracks its
  bounded retirement and Current consumer correction.
- Q07 / I08: resolved by D08. Actor, Operator and AI Agent definitions belong
  in R, not O. P2647 tracks the source disposition and O catalogue correction.
- I02/I04/I05: the existing decisions already settle the direction: D governs
  the represented thing/property, paths use the accepted canonical root and
  operators, and retired generic fields are not revived. P2649–P2651 perform
  the source-specific mapping and ask only for concrete unsupported cases.
- G03: bounded consumer lookup and source correction are complete for the
  accepted repair. Global semantic coverage remains unclaimed: 137 proposals
  were not authored and 69 pre-existing unmapped Subject occurrences remain.
- I10–I12 / F10–F12: optional design-challenge opportunities concern one
  equal-name inheritance example, guidance for actual category additions, and
  a few authoring examples. None was adopted or implemented by this Epic.

### Accepted decisions

D01 — Subject definition, accepted and clarified 2026-10-26:

Subject names the thing or topic an Atom governs or depends on.

That sentence is the definition. GOVERNS / DEPENDS_ON are connected relations,
not part of the Subject definition. Define those relations in separate Atoms
that depend_on the Subject-definition Atom. The whole set of Subjects forms
another graph; those special relations connect Atoms to its nodes.

D02 — Open Graph Node categories, accepted 2026-10-26:

A Graph Node can be Continuant, Occurrent or Aspect. This list is open under
the framework's expandability principle; it is not an exhaustive three-value
enumeration. Do not force every Subject into Continuant or Occurrent, invent
new categories for existing topics, or remap all topics under a new Aspect
path merely from this decision.

D03 — Graph Rule Claim, accepted 2026-10-26:

Graph Rules have a Claim, carried in the YAML part. Absence of a Markdown
Claim section does not mean the logical Claim is absent. This supersedes the
review's proposed no-Claim inheritance exception. D04 below supplies the accepted representation choices; no migration of
existing formal rules into configuration is authorized. Do not silently
duplicate the same operative rule in both forms.

D04 — Claim meaning and representation, accepted 2026-10-26:

  location for Claim. This decision does not require a Claim on C, A, P or O.

The tree shows the changed branches and representative children. Existing Domain descendants, Product instances, UX topics and Documentation topics remain unless an approved decision changes their meaning. It is not an exhaustive enumeration.

#### Meaning and boundaries

- Engineering names aspects and practices: architecture, authoring, verification, delivery, storage, data handling, execution control, traceability and observability. Its old Continuant/Occurrent branches move to the appropriate new branches. Flatten Engineering/Aspect to Engineering.
- Implementation names the actual logical realization: Code, Prompts, Documentation and Resources. Content Role I and Subject classification remain independent.
- Code has logical units such as Function, Class, Module and Package. A physical folder is a Directory Carrier; a logical package groups code units.
- Documentation has logical content units. Document, Section, Paragraph, Sentence, List, Table, Code Block and Diagram are kinds; use containment for their actual whole/part structure, not subtype nesting. One file can represent many content units.
- JSON, TOML, Markdown and Mermaid describe format or syntax, not a new logical resource kind. Mermaid is a diagram syntax.
- Runtime names actual technical executions, including sessions and tool/app/service, process and container runs. Modeled business Action, Step and Workflow Runs stay in Domain/Occurrent.
- Carrier names representation and storage. For this model, Docker Image is a Carrier of packaged Implementation; container execution belongs to Runtime. Files, directories and databases remain Carriers. Git Commit, Git Branch and Pull Request are Carriers under the latest Operator decision.
- A Git Index represents the staged-file snapshot. A remote GitHub repository or branch is another Carrier; the legacy Git Remote Subject names the Git Repository Carrier, while connection details remain in Content Scope.
- Git Repository > Git Branch means containment: a remote repository contains remote branches. Repository and Branch remain distinct Carrier kinds; / must not encode this whole/part link.
- Release belongs to Domain/Continuant/History/Release. Its ID is called Version. Release identifies what was delivered; a Journal entry records that a release happened. Do not merge the delivered version with the event record about it.
- Local Release and Public Release remain named Workflows. Their definitions and workflow-specific RMED belong in PROJECT_CONFIGURATION.
- API-specific transport contracts use Engineering/Architecture/Communication/API. This Subject decision does not remove runtime Host/Origin checks.
- Subject, Content Role, Type, Tier and Local Scope Unit remain independent. A moved Subject does not by itself change an Atom's ownership, role or meaning. Do not copy Scope Unit or Tool identities into topic branches.
- Existing notation remains: / broader-to-narrower kind; . bearer-to-dependent property; : allowed value; // named instance; > whole-to-part using containment. Keep full canonical Subject paths in source data.
- Do not invent a new Domain kind to force a mapping. Classify remaining technical kinds from their source meaning; ask the Operator when confidence is below 90%.

2. Record Governs changes first, then Depends On, in one thin table: Atom ID | old Subject | new Subject | status.
3. Preserve prior supported Draft corrections and unrelated work. Create or refine the next-version Draft of each affected Atom.
4. Reuse existing R/Definition Atoms with the same meaning. Create missing Definition Drafts. Keep technology-specific definitions in PROJECT_CONFIGURATION; update shared Core model rules in their existing Core scope.
5. Review the exact Draft batch. Apply accepted successors with normal predecessor archives; preserve identity unless Summary or Content Role changes.
6. Rebuild the Current Subject views from applied sources. Drafted and Applied are separate states; list unresolved mappings explicitly.

No code, Tool, runtime, release execution or general Scope Unit reorganization is part of this migration.


The thin progress table is [Candidate #9 Subject changes](../../../../_projection/core-entity-review/presentation/candidate-9.subjects.md).

Refine Engineering Subject branch

## Objective

Apply the latest approved Subject model, preserving source meaning and normal version history, then rebuild the Current Subject views.

## Details

### Decision authority

[Task P2667](CA-P-2665-EPIC--refine-engineering-subject-branch/done/02-CA-P-2667-TASK--settle-engineering-subject-structure.md) contains Candidate #9. Its latest Operator decisions supersede incompatible earlier candidates and placements. Keep the candidate in that Task rather than maintaining a second decision document.

Engineering becomes aspects-only. Implementation, Runtime and Carrier are direct Graph Node branches. Release belongs to Domain/Continuant/History. Git Commit, Git Branch, Pull Request, Git Index and the remote Git repository are Carriers. The full meaning and boundaries are recorded in P2667.

### Work order

1. Review Governs before Depends On, using Current sources and the supported corrections already prepared in Drafts.
2. Maintain one thin table: [Candidate #9 Subject changes](../../_projection/core-entity-review/presentation/candidate-9.subjects.md). Columns: Atom ID | old Subject | new Subject | status. Do not copy bodies, hashes or analysis reports into it.

4. Review and apply the supported batch. Archive each Current predecessor and promote its accepted successor. Keep identity unless Summary or Content Role changes. Stop on failure and record actual progress.
5. Rebuild Core, Project Methodology, Engine and Full Current Subject views from the resulting source heads.

Ask one context-rich question when confidence is below 90%. Do not invent a new Domain kind to force a mapping. Preserve unrelated work and existing historical Drafts/Archives.

### Retained scope decisions

- Subject, Content Role and Local Scope Unit are independent. Topics do not copy Scope Unit or Tool identities.
- Workflow-specific Local Release/Public Release definitions and RMED belong in PROJECT_CONFIGURATION.
- R1752, R1753 and M260 govern Applicable Methodology Compilation; their Drafts belong in PROJECT_CONFIGURATION. R1754 Extension promotion remains deferred.
- Current source application, Draft preparation and projection generation are distinct states.
- No code, Tools, runtime, release execution, general Scope Unit reorganization or Terms Graph implementation is included. Broader content migration remains separate except for definitions required by Candidate #9.

### Projection

Keep the four sections: primary Subjects; properties with inheritance; instances; dependency-only Subjects. Dependency-only means exact values in Depends On absent from Governs within that view's own Current source set. List referring Atom IDs. Rooting alone does not prove semantic correctness.

### Applied result

Candidate #9 is applied: 1,350 existing Atoms updated and 35 new Definition Atoms. Two of those existing Atoms received final Definition-text corrections during completion audit, for 1,352 update events and 1,352 predecessor archives in total. The batch includes 20 ownership/carrier relocations. All 873 unselected Current source files remain byte-identical. All 1,387 actual source changes were appended to the Journal without invented Workflow Runs or earlier history.

The four regenerated views use 2,258 Current RMEDO sources: Core 819, Project Methodology 413 and Engine 1,026. Each view has primary Subjects, properties with inheritance, instances and exact dependency-only Subjects. No unmapped occurrences remain in these selected views. The broad inventory's 15 non-rooted occurrences are outside the selected RMEDO view and were not silently remapped.

Git Repository > Git Branch means containment. Both remain Carrier kinds. Engineering is aspects-only; Implementation, Runtime and Carrier are direct Graph Node branches. Release belongs to Domain/Continuant/History, and Version is Release.ID.

The thin table records Applied source changes. R1754's Extension-promotion feature remains deferred; this batch only normalizes its Subject classification. No production Tool, runtime or release execution is claimed. General content migration and wider Engine restructuring remain outside this completed batch.

Final completion audit corrected CA-R-2150@7 to describe the approved branches and removed the duplicate Semantics block in CA-R-1971@9. The final four views include those versions. Source identity/version/hash checks, predecessor reconstruction, release Workflow ownership and closure, thin-table application, exact dependency-only sets, and projection layout all passed. The thin table has 2,408 Applied rows and no pending Drafted rows. Generic Engineering-topic glossary Definitions were not added: the approved namespace Rule and existing source Semantics remain sufficient. No unresolved decision remains within this Epic's scope.

P2639 remains Done for its earlier bounded FPF work. P2637 consumes this accepted model in the wider Engine work.

## Definition of Done

- Candidate #9 and its missing definitions are represented by accepted source Atoms.
- Affected Subjects are migrated or have explicit unresolved Operator decisions; no unsupported mapping is silently applied.
- Current successors and predecessor archives match the reviewed batch; unrelated work is preserved.
- Four rebuilt views cite actual Current sources and versions and retain the dependency-only section.
- No code, runtime or broader migration completion is inferred from these methodology changes.

# Summary

Stage candidate runtime package and Skill

## Action

Stage candidate runtime package and Skill **means** the Action that prepares the one private `stage_candidate` package, runtime, and Skill payload from the frozen active source boundary without selecting it as the active runtime or project Skill.

## Scope

`stage_candidate` prepares the complete declared Framework package only under `.caprmedio_tmp/release_candidates/<run_id>/package/`, including the private active-source copy, compiled Methodology, Engine, complete `ca` Skill/default payload, dependency-lock identity, runtime input, and matching image context. It stages the `ca` payload for its Project target without replacing an active Skill or writing `LAYER_1_FRAMEWORK_METHODOLOGY/` or the installed Framework.

## Details

The phase requires CA-O-165's exact boundary and records the package digests used by CA-O-176, CA-O-185, and CA-O-169. A missing member, unbound target, incomplete Skill directory, digest mismatch, hook, partial staging, unavailable permission, or failed postcondition stops before image build, tests, or installation. This Action does not select a runtime or Skill, alter settings, register MCP, install, publish, or retry. Every actual invocation is journaled once.

# Summary

Verify candidate release package and image

## Action

Verify candidate release package and image **means** the Action that performs one bound `closed_unit_gate`, `candidate_image_build`, or `candidate_image_canary` phase for the frozen local boundary.

# Summary

Reconcile the uncertain CA-P-1959 update outcome

## Concern

A historical selected update_atom preview for CA-P-1959 returned a transport/implementation failure with outcome uncertain. It was not an authorized mutation execution: the retained preparation history records no execute, enqueue, dispatch or replay after that preview. Active tracks the unexplained historical preview failure; current reproducibility and root cause remain unknown.

## Evidences

Native call exec-3e8e0c9e-b687-43de-95fd-1d57dbe926f6 completed at 2026-10-17T22:06:53.476Z with failed transport/error result and diagnostic `Implementation call failed; no automatic replay`. Its target was CA-P-1959. Exact source: /Users/am/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-2026-10-16T13-51-07-01a1441f-5891-7372-8202-7b2cd4db8ea5.jsonl:3912.

The frozen observed row and request/result hashes are retained in .caprmedio_tmp/mcp-audit-20261020/corpus-v2/release-v2/; the bounded ledger is semantic/update-first/outcomes.jsonl under the same audit root. Adjacent retry previews and queue admissions are not terminal effect receipts. The exact request was candidate6-epic-update-001-af4eb31631564f62 with mode=preview; its request wrapper is truncated. Original and separate v2 execution plans both bind the pre-target to version90 SHA256709fffed7ad79bef99718597c6888a6b1d5115c9059107ce3af55f8eb606bb35. The v2 archived@90 readback retains that hash and unchanged_prior_body=true. Therefore no lasting source change is observed at that retained v90 boundary. This is not a terminal no-op receipt or proof against all unobserved side effects. The separate v2 update's successful terminal receipts do not establish success of the failed preview. Reconciled evidence: .caprmedio_tmp/mcp-audit-20261020/continuation/update-history/report.md and exactpins.json. It was not replayed. Source hashes are scan-time observations; 4 KiB header pins do not prove full-session immutability, and some update requests elsewhere are truncated. No common cause with C221/C439/C444/C521 was inferred.

## Blast radius

Callers cannot treat a failed preview as publication success or equate its uncertainty wrapper with an executed mutation. The observed unchanged v90 boundary narrows the source-effect concern, but does not explain the preview failure. Check any current reproduction using a distinct nonproduction project, port and state. Do not replay the historical request or treat a later preview, successful unrelated update or current MCP context read as resolution of this execution. The production MCP and its lifecycle remain outside test scope.

# Summary

Align edit-draft markers with no-ID Draft identity

## Concern

The source correction is implemented and verified, but installed runtime adoption remains outside this increment. The published Draft forms are: optional `atom_id` and ID-free empty-number Drafts, `CA-R-draft`/role-draft markers for new Atoms, version-qualified `<canonical-ID>@<proposed-version>-draft` edit markers, and legacy `<canonical-ID>@draft` compatibility. A marker is Draft-only proposal metadata, not a canonical identity. Existing-marker promotion must update the same canonical Atom at the explicit carried/requested Version, archive the exact current predecessor, and refuse stale target/version/digest bindings.

## Evidences

The six original Core deliveries and Engine RMEDO now agree on Draft-only markers and no retained-history/Journal admission gate. Independent frozen checks passed validator 542, CLI E2E 28, native promotion 8, marker formats 6, model lifecycle 20, exact pins 1 and full promotion 22. Staging passed focused 16, contract 5 and workflow 10. Same-path concurrent-edit preservation, exact predecessor bytes, Done-to-Active child bundles, strict Version bindings and mutation-free no-op were independently reviewed. The older parser cohort was corrected as a fixture/obsolete expectation issue and passed all 30; no production guard was weakened.

These are source/host proofs only. No release, deployment, installed mirror refresh, migration or held-Draft publication occurred. The installed 0.4.4.8 runtime has not been activated with this increment, so this Problem remains Active for separately authorized runtime adoption and reconciliation of held carriers CA-R-1016@draft, CA-R-1017@draft, CA-R-1019@draft, CA-R-1021@draft and CA-R-1472@draft. Preserve their captured evidence and the stopped batch; do not replay or reset it.

This is a separate bounded source-and-implementation follow-up, not authority to replay, delete, reset or publish the held drafts. Preserve their captured evidence and the stopped batch. The approved runtime release does not claim this Problem is repaired.

# Summary

Compose mandatory container lifecycle Runs

## Concern

The always-recursive container lifecycle rule is source-defined but lacks an implemented calling Workflow that composes the independently admitted single-Atom Runs. Archive must include all contained latest Atoms, including Done descendants; requesting Done must leave contained latest Plans already Done unchanged and request Canceled for every other contained latest Plan. There is no optional descendant mode.

## Evidences

Independent read-only call-path inspection found contained_atom_targets.py discovery unconnected to lifecycle execution. selected_execution.py freezes one Workflow Run, and change_status_atom_action must remain single-Atom. run_visit_limits repeats frozen Step inputs rather than freshly binding each target; the Subjects-only batch is a different expressly scoped exception. Current singleton publication can move matching bundles without performing descendant Status Actions; P2485 adds a guard against silently moving independent current children, not the missing recursive composition. This is source evidence, not a production MCP probe or deployed incident.

### Implementation review checkpoint

P2497 pure planner is reviewed and accepted, but the first P2499 mocked composition pass was rejected. Real-boundary gaps include original root authorization validation, ordinary fresh member receipts, canonical requested-Run IDs, parent descriptor shape, member frontier/effect bindings, canonical terminal evidence and request-bound uncertain progress. P2503 repairs these before acceptance; no recursive caller completion is claimed. P2500 preview sealing, P2501 actual entrypoint/status wiring and P2502 functional test preparation remain independently owned. C553/P2504 separately repair the frozen fixture and full source-context admission.

## Blast radius

P2494 owns a narrow O127-specific calling-Workflow composition above SelectedExecution.freeze/dispatch; P2495 owns frozen functional acceptance. Reuse governed containment discovery, process descendants before parent relocation, freshly bind each target after prior effects, stop on first failure and retain earlier successes. Preserve exact old history and external references. Do not add a mode, per-child human confirmation, hidden multi-target Action, generic orchestrator or cross-Atom rollback. Installed-runtime adoption, migration, replay and Stage 2 Scope Unit operations remain separately scoped.

Name CAPRMEDIO images with verified version and build date

Read-only Docker inventory on desktop-linux found29images with org.caprmedio.runtime.schema=1, all RepoTags empty. Eleven historical/current images currently have version proof via their source-head label and exact version.toml; eighteen lack verified version evidence. Docker Created is descriptive timestamp evidence, not proof that every source/checkout byte was included.

Native create was attempted once and stopped before publication at its final Project-boundary recheck because the read-I/O timeout budget expired. Exact target absence and unused identity were checked before this Operator-authorized manual save. This is not a passed native admission receipt; the separate bounded admission-performance Problem is C561.

P2518–P2521 own the Operator-prioritized fix, consistent regression coverage, additive exact-image maintenance and acceptance before recursive-container continuation. Preserve immutable SHA/fingerprint/platform/Project admission, occupied tags, existing containers and unknown historical version evidence. Approved18unknown-versionimages+6stoppedtestcontainers removed, then separately approved696-byte image27b9017daa69 removed non-force after fresh metadata/no-reference checks. Final fresh readback:12CAPRMEDIO images, allnamed, no unnamed; original e812container/08fimage unchangedhealthy. No version/date guessed; no release/deployment/restart. ExactIDs/actualreceipts retained in Journal event4ad64079-e23e-431b-93c5-02063dae88c7; final additional deletion recorded separately. C561/C562/C555/C545 remain independent open issues; this bounded naming defect is resolved, not all runtime issues.

# Summary

Warn and skip individual schema-invalid Atoms during scans

## Concern

Native ATOM_SEARCH observation surfaced 25 `schema_invalid` diagnostics with no
effects. The Operator now requires an isolated schema-invalid Atom to be omitted
with a technical warning carrying its path and reason, while the bounded scan may
continue with `complete: false`. This is a warning disposition for an individual
invalid carrier, not permission to hide an incomplete source frontier or to repair
the source.

## Required disposition

The implementation and acceptance evidence must distinguish an isolated
schema-invalid Atom from fatal I/O, security, duplicate-identity, stale, ambiguous,
or otherwise incomplete-frontier conditions. The former is skipped with valid
matches retained and `complete: false`; the latter remains a refusal/error with no
partial successful result. Technical warnings use Docker `stderr` as structured
records, carry the validated Project prefix from Project settings plus path and
reason, and are retained by Docker local rotation `max-size=10m` and
`max-file=3`, with `mode=non-blocking` and a `max-buffer-size=1m`; new technical
messages may be dropped when that buffer is full so the primary scan cannot stall.
The prefix uses the existing bound Project selection and canonical prefix-field
validation. This uses the selected immutable settings view and does not claim full
SettingsReader conformance or add another settings carrier. Docker logs are
removed with the container. They are not business Journal records, must not create
a fake Run, must not create a local log directory, and must not rewrite historical
Journal records. A missing or failed logging stream remains observable without
breaking the primary scan.

## Evidence boundary

The current AtomSearch suite passed 94 tests with no skips. Ten MCP protocol tests
passed in 3.990 seconds after warning-path and malformed-warning-skip updates;
four Docker logging checks and 21 related checks also passed. An isolated Docker
probe against the existing version 0.4.4.10 image, with read-only new source and
version mounts, verified two Project prefixes (CHECK_A and CHECK_B), the Docker
environment, token redaction, and Docker local logging inspection for
`max-size=10m`, `max-file=3`, `mode=non-blocking`, and `max-buffer-size=1m`; it
exited 0. This is source-mounted configuration evidence, not acceptance of a new
image. Production remained unchanged and healthy. CA-R-863, CA-M-370 and CA-E-301
carry the explicit scan disposition; CA-M-414 preserves the technical-diagnostic
versus Journal boundary. Existing query-Journal authorities CA-R-1865, CA-R-1867,
CA-M-337, CA-E-577 and CA-E-580 remain the route for truthful actual-query
evidence and do not authorize a competing log. The selected Docker `stderr`
stream and bounded local rotation are now the sink policy; this Problem does not
add a local log directory or turn technical warnings into business Journal
records. It remains Active pending new-image/deployment acceptance and the
pre-existing full SettingsReader/M284 conformance gap.

## Blast radius

ATOM_SEARCH and related bounded scans, their diagnostic result envelopes, runtime
logging, and the distinction between technical diagnostics and business Journal
history. Preserve all historical Journal bytes, no-effect behavior, fatal guards,
and the complete-suite/public-release gate. No Stage 2 Scope Unit operation,
release, deployment, migration, or whole-Epic closure is implied.

# Summary

Current native Workflow dispatch lacks Integrated continuation

## Concern

Current source R1527@7 defines Integrated execution as the current participating session receiving the bound Action inputs and instructions, performing the Action and returning its result to the executor. O016@17 binds all eight current Steps as Integrated. The current native implementation path instead invokes a separate ephemeral Codex CLI callback synchronously. Retaining prior-result data does not make that separate Agent the current participating session.

Read-only inspection found no public pending-prompt/result-submission path in the current enqueue, enqueue_selected and status operations. The native graph immediately transitions after a callback result and its execution session is in memory. A frozen current-graph check also observes O231 dispatching legacy O091. This is current source and isolated-fixture evidence, not an observation of a deployed current Workflow or a production incident.

## Required disposition

After the Operator-directed three-file legacy refactor is independently accepted, implement the existing Integrated context contract through a durable bound pending frontier, prompt/input return to the current session, admitted later result submission and continuation without replaying completed Actions or effects. Reuse the existing Project, request, Run, frozen source, candidate, packet, visit and retry fields. Validate stale, conflicting, repeated and cross-Project submissions and preserve partial evidence. Keep separate-Agent callbacks available only for explicitly Isolated invocations; do not silently substitute them for Integrated Steps.

# Summary

Preserve graph execution parity during decomposition

## Concern

Independent read-only review of the unaccepted four-module graph-loop extraction found a recovery regression: build_action_context checks membership in session.actual after start_run has inserted the new Action. A newly started change_atom_status Action during recovery is therefore incorrectly treated as restored and returns lifecycle-recovery-required rather than performing the admitted first execution. The predecessor snapshots actual Run identities before any starts. The current working-tree executor delegates to this extraction, so passing the one-Step happy-path smoke is not refactor acceptance.

The same review found execute_graph still owning visit control, dispatch, retained-state mutation and both completion paths in one oversized executable unit; retain_prior_result accepts an opaque nine-value Any varargs packet; and three exact writer diagnostics plus the non-string terminal error drifted from their predecessor. Source file-size, Ruff and Mypy successes do not discharge these behavioral and cohesion findings.

## Required disposition

Repair the extracted canonical owners without new business rules or an exception. Capture restored identities at entry, preserve genuine restored versus newly started recovery behavior, use explicit typed result-retention arguments, retain exact diagnostics and split the remaining oversized traversal unit by real responsibility. Add focused recovery, multi-Step/revisit and diagnostic parity checks. Re-run the related preserved legacy portfolio and independent review against exact current source bytes before CA-P-2590 and CA-P-2595 can complete.

Do not bypass the findings with class-wrapper result normalization, untyped self proxies, a generic registry, broader suppression, rewritten frozen source data or a claimed passing gate. Current shared-context features remain paused. CA-P-2589 owns the repair; the original executor and production caller integration remain under one writer.

## Resolution — 22 October 2026

The canonical extraction now snapshots restored Action identities before any starts, distinguishes new and genuinely restored Actions, retains exact creation/lifecycle/replacement writer and terminal diagnostics, and uses explicit typed prior-result arguments. Traversal responsibilities are cohesive and bounded. Independent review subsequently found and closed one further parity difference: graph projections again perform the unconditional final write after Step and Workflow terminal attempts, including unconfirmed receipts.

Four durable tests in test_selected_graph_recovery_parity.py cover recovery membership, frozen O016 revisit identities/order, exact diagnostics and the final projection write trace. Six related focused legacy checks, strict Mypy and pinned Ruff format/lint/C901 passed for the owned graph lane. Independent source/assertion review returned PASS. No source-size exception or current Workflow feature was introduced.

This resolves the identified graph extraction findings only. Public executor integration, manifest-fixture isolation and Subject-batch caller closure remain subject to CA-P-2590 and CA-P-2595; the separate Integrated continuation gap CA-C-576 remains Active.

## Evidence boundary

These findings concern unaccepted local refactoring, not a deployed incident or a new Workflow policy. Agent and selected-route refactors have separate reviewed acceptance. Current Integrated continuation remains a distinct implementation gap in CA-C-576. No full suite, production MCP traffic, release, deployment or uncertain replay was used to claim graph-loop acceptance.

# Summary

Read-only interrupted status requires recovery

## Concern

The strengthened isolated continuation run accepts a terminal submission with
the canonical terminal/interrupted_pending disposition and an
interrupted_pending graph result, but the final public status is blocked
with the message "selected checkpoint interruption requires explicit recovery".
The public read-only status therefore does not expose the accepted
interrupted state without a recovery action. This is a current status and
recovery-surface problem, not permission to replay a completed Action or to
change the business Journal.

## Evidences

The root-controlled isolated current-Workflow fixture reproduced the sequence
after the prior 4/4 journey result: terminal submission validation retained
the canonical terminal/interrupted_pending state and graph result, while the
public status path returned blocked and required explicit recovery. The
observation is bounded to the tested source-bound workflow and nonproduction
state; it does not establish current Project binding, runtime admission,
deployment or production MCP behavior.

## Required disposition

Add a bounded read-only status/recovery check under CA-P-2611. Preserve the
accepted terminal/interrupted_pending result, expose it consistently through
the public status read, and make recovery/replay behavior explicit. Verify
that a read-only status request does not mutate the Run, replay completed
Actions, or silently convert an interrupted result into a successful
completion. Keep the existing public API and business-only Journal boundary.

No production MCP call, Docker action, full-suite run, release, deployment,
uncertain replay or RMED promotion is authorized by this Problem.

## Blast radius

Public status, reconnect/recovery and retained partial-result visibility for
the selected Integrated Workflow Run. The issue may leave a valid interrupted
Run appearing blocked until recovery, while earlier accepted receipts remain
intact.

## Resolution

CA-P-2611 completed the bounded read-only status/recovery verification. The combined current-workflow portfolio passed 64/64 checks, six direct observation guards and seven checkpoint checks; the strict SDK journey passed 4/4 in 30.110s with exact terminal/interrupted_pending disposition, final public status and verified graph-result bytes. The final Docker-free stdio smoke passed with 23 tools, and Ruff/mypy passed. The public status now preserves terminal and run_disposition interrupted state without granting recovery permission or replaying completed Actions.

This Problem is Resolved for the observed status defect only. CA-C-576, the installed binding, current Project binding, runtime admission, handoff, release and deployment remain separate gates.

# Summary

Current Journal receipt gates need reconciliation with Core completion semantics

## Concern

The completed source review establishes definite current semantic conflicts, not
only a generic question. O130 line 44 treats an unconfirmed Workflow Journal
start as blocking dispatch. O131 line 55 applies a Journal-confirmation gate.
O133 and O136 line 39 make an absent receipt prevent a Run from completing.
O134 and O137 lines 40, 42 and 46-48 contain recording blockers or completion
gates. These are current declarations requiring reconciliation with the higher
Core authorities; they are not a claim that the deployed runtime is failing.

The compiler path has the same concrete boundary: compile_applicable_methodology.py
lines 1235-1275 constructs Approval from a Journal row and digest, while lines
1177-1180 and 1211-1232 use a failed Publication Journal record for recovery.
O007/O155/O156 provide affected approval-source context; their recorded decision
context must not be turned into a generic proof gate merely because logging is
mandatory. O029/O031 are declared helper contracts and do not prove that the
generic status implementation is actually blocked.

R1525@11, R1720@22 and D340@17 explicitly provide no Journal permission, proof,
recording, completion or recovery gate. The actual business Journal append
obligation remains valid, including the separate O051 obligation, which is not
included in this Problem's gate claims. Independently admitted Run-state and
Operator-Decision evidence can be legitimate evidence; it must remain distinct
from a Journal receipt.

## Required disposition

Apply the existing higher Core rule to these concrete current clauses; do not
invent a new authority choice or automatically rewrite a clause during this
review. Separate an actual business-lifecycle append obligation, an
independently admitted Run or Operator-Decision state, a technical
recording_error and a Journal receipt used as a recovery input. Do not treat a
missing Journal row as generic missing proof, and do not silently remove a
required append, add a universal completion gate or claim the declared helper
conditions are actual generic status blocking.

behavior and explicit failure reporting. Any source or implementation repair
requires a later bounded decision and validation; this Problem authorizes no
binding mutation.

authority-reconciliation record, not a runtime, release or deployment claim.

# Summary

Keep implementation policy in Active RMED

## Question

How can the general PROGRAMMATIC prompt prevent invented business logic without spreading feature-specific rules to unrelated implementations?

## Scope

General PROGRAMMATIC Methods, their selected implementation prompt, and the ownership of conditional Methods included in that prompt.

## Analysis

The Operator reports that AI-assisted implementation became overcomplicated: extra behavior cost time and tokens to implement, test and later remove. This is the Operator's assessment, not a measured cost estimate.

An implementation can accidentally become a second specification when an agent fills gaps with extra restrictions, approvals, history checks or workflow steps. Tests can then preserve the invented behavior instead of the intended behavior.

Active RMED should own business decisions. Implementation should realize those decisions. Ordinary technical choices remain the implementer's work; changing business meaning requires the Operator's decision. CA-M-384 records this boundary. It adds no runtime gate and does not authorize removing existing declared protections.

## Conditional Methods and descendant ownership

"Applicable to this task" describes when a Method is loaded; it does not decide which Scope Unit owns the Method.

- Keep shared implementation rules at PROGRAMMATIC: functional core, objects for owned lifecycle, small units, Python environment, file/subprocess safety (M161), structured diagnostics (M163), measurement before optimization (M165), and structured boundary validation (M286). Their conditions can apply across Tools and Apps.
- Keep the shared Settings-reader consumption rule (M284) at PROGRAMMATIC: several descendants use that same boundary. A reader's private implementation rules belong with the reader.
- Review M193, MCP Tool-frontier publication, for relocation to the Scope Unit that owns MCP exposure. Its current procedure governs one capability, not all PROGRAMMATIC implementations.
- Review M191, mutation Initiative propagation, for the appropriate common owner of the affected mutation Workflows. Do not move it to one Tool if several descendants depend on it.

These are ownership candidates from a bounded reading of M161, M163, M165, M191, M193, M284 and M286. The complete Method set and all consumers were not audited. No existing Method is moved or retired by this Analysis. Before relocation, confirm the actual owning Scope Unit and consumers, preserve IDs/history, and update the prompt's source locations.

## Result

Use CA-M-384 in the common implementation prompt. Load additional Methods only when their stated conditions apply. Separate shared conditional rules from descendant-specific rules; do not treat either as permission to invent business behavior.

## Sources

- Operator instructions in this Codex conversation, 2026-10-15: implement only business logic declared in Active RMED; ask about gaps; reconsider task-specific Method ownership.
- Current PROGRAMMATIC Methods M161, M163, M165, M191, M193, M284 and M286, and the compact PROGRAMMATIC Method projection.
