# Summary

Serialize review coverage and correction outcomes separately

## Scope

temporary JSON reports **and** progress records emitted by the RMED review prompt Implementation.

## Claim

the Implementation **must** serialize initial check evidence, applied corrections, **and** derived completion **in** separate fields within the report layout governed by CA-D-496-CORE_META_MODEL--store-one-review-report-per-source-atom.

## Details

| Record | Field | Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| report | `source` | object containing the checked path, Version, **and** SHA-256 digest |
| report | `atom_id` | checked Atom ID |
| report | `workflow_run_id` | the caller's Run ID, retained through checking, correction, **and** handoff |
| report | `criteria_sha256` | the supplied shared checking-packet digest, linked **to** its exact rule bindings; retain that digest rather than hashing a different subset |
| report | `checks` | object keyed by `properties`, `cce`, `scope`, `claim`, `details`, **and** `summary`; **every** entry carries `status` **and** evidence **or** a reason |
| report | `findings`, `blockers` | separate arrays of confirmed findings **and** incomplete check coverage |
| report | `corrections`, `rejected_findings`, `unresolved_findings` | separate arrays retaining the disposition of findings; a completed fix carries an explicit empty `unresolved_findings` array |
| report | `fix_blockers` | correction blockers, distinct from incomplete initial check coverage |
| report | `result` | recorded check **or** fix result |
| progress item | `reported_result` | retained report result |
| progress item | `check_complete` | Boolean for completion of **all** required initial checks |
| progress item | `complete` | Boolean for completion of this Atom's admitted work |
| progress item | `state` | derived state that retains `blocked` for unresolved coverage **or** findings |
| progress total | `total`, `reported`, `checked`, `completed`, `complete`, `states` | selection size, report count, complete-check count, completed-Atom count, aggregate Boolean, **and** state counts |

initial check outcomes remain preserved **after** correction. `fixed_not_rechecked` **or** an approved `replaced_not_rechecked` result does **not** overwrite blocked check evidence **or** independently set `complete` **to** true.

**every** finding has a stable per-report identifier **or** fixed array index. corrections, rejections, **and** unresolved dispositions reference those findings explicitly; a correction **may** address multiple identified findings. a finding omitted from **all** dispositions remains unresolved. retain correction blockers separately so that a fully performed check remains distinguishable from an unauthorized **or** unfinished fix.

# Summary

Deliver current Implementation Workflow prompt carriers

## Scope

the definition-only shared-context package at `LAYER_2_FRAMEWORK_ENGINE/FEATURE_AGENTIC/FEATURE_PROMPTS/ACTION_PROMPTS/IMPLEMENTATION_WORKFLOW/SHARED_CONTEXT/`.

## Claim

the package **must** contain only `CA-O-231`, `CA-O-232`, `CA-O-233`, `CA-O-094`, `CA-O-234`, `CA-O-096`, `CA-O-099`, and `CA-O-239` `.prompt.md` carriers, plus `README.md`, `definition_frontier.projection.json`, and `tests/`.

## Details

Each prompt header carries exact Step, Action, and context. This Delivery specifies definition-only carriers, not executable admission. Keep the existing native package, executable source_bindings, and frozen corpus unchanged until separately admitted runtime realization; do not dispatch these definitions through the old adapter.

Every invocation packet additionally carries exactly one `selected_project`
binding before a prompt can verify its governed sources or call an Agent:

| Field | Required value | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selected_project.kind` | `selected_project` | identifies the Project frozen by the selected Workflow; it is not an absolute host path, current directory, code-root copy, or mount grant |
| `selected_project.source_root` | `.caprmedio_caprmedio` | the only authority root for prompt-source resolution |
| `selected_project.source_references` | the exact current `source_bindings` rows, each with Atom ID, Version, project-relative `path`, and SHA-256 | every path is nonempty, relative, has no `..` segment, begins under `source_root`, and resolves only beneath the frozen selected Project |
| `requirements`, `methods`, `evaluations`, `delivery` | complete applicable direct source rows: `atom_id`, `version`, Project-relative `path`, `sha256`, and full `content` | independently verify the authorized initial selection, its declared universe and applicable governing parents against current Project authority; preserve R/D implementation targets separately from governing context |
| `method_projection` (optional) | a legacy source-bound derived view | it neither replaces direct source rows nor blocks a Run when absent; no compiled paragraph or projection file is required |
| `workspace` | the existing absolute, non-symlink disposable workspace supplied to the Agent | no source binding infers or substitutes this path |
| `permissions.implementation_workspace` | the existing exact `{kind: disposable_workspace, path: workspace, allow_write: true}` capability | it must match `workspace`; this Delivery adds no write grant |

The selected Workflow runtime resolves `selected_project` only from its frozen
Project context. Absent, stale, duplicate, mismatched, escaping, or
partially-readable source references, incomplete direct RMED inputs, or a
missing/mismatched workspace capability blocks before Agent launch or effects.
This binding exposes neither credentials nor an Agent endpoint and does not
authorize a hidden mount, arbitrary writer, or live-model execution. An
explicit executable mock remains `mock-not-live-llm` evidence only.

An Integrated prompt response carries the current Step's prompt, bound inputs,
output contract, and opaque continuation identity. Publishing it leaves the Step
pending. The controlling session may perform or delegate the admitted work and
submit its actual result through the same Workflow interface. Only the executor
validates that bound submission and chooses the next Step; a prompt alone is not
completion. Retain the persistent Plan, partial effects, candidate-specific
review/check evidence and finite retry state across requests. The implementation
instructions use CA-R-2117, CA-M-431, and CA-E-653 for narrowest-branch RMED
ownership comments; citations alone do not prove conformance.

- preserve the correspondence between the committed change set **and** its individual Journal Events; Git **must not** become another authoritative Journal.

# Encode exact Git references in release evidence

**when** the GIT Extension supplies the Git binding for a selected release candidate, its evidence references **must** identify the repository **and** the full immutable commit object ID representing the checked content.

- a branch name, HEAD, **or** a tag name alone is **not** an exact Revision reference. retain a selected tag as a label **only** alongside its resolved commit ID.
- a commit ID **must not** represent uncommitted content as evaluated committed content; material working-tree differences **must** remain explicit under the applicable candidate binding.
- a release manifest **must** bind the released candidate **to** that exact reference; a later branch movement does **not** rebind earlier evidence.
- use the existing proof-frontier **and** Journal Carriers. do **not** create a second authoritative release log **or** redefine the generic Journal schema.

this Git-specific encoding does **not** select a branch strategy, require Git outside the selected Extension capability, **or** authorize commit, merge, tag, push, **or** publication.

## Summary

Model concepts use their readable names in authored methodology.

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Model names in authored Methodology Sources, including their applicable child Scope Units.


**when** writing model concepts in Subjects, Formal claims **or** authored model text, the Author **must** use their governed readable model names. For example, name the applicable model concepts:

- Content Role;
- Local Scope Unit; **and**
- Updated At.

**when** explaining an encoding, show the exact technical spelling as a Carrier key **or** serialization example. Preserve each canonical model name **and** do **not** invent aliases through stylistic changes.

## Semantics

Readable model language includes technical Subjects. Technical key spelling belongs to the file-adapter Method; Carrier fields and encodings remain governed by Delivery authority. The choice of presentation does not change the identified concept or its permitted values.

# How many R and D Atoms may govern one Entity?

what limits, **if** **any**, should apply **to** the number of Requirement **and** Delivery Atoms that govern the same Entity while expressing distinct Claims?

## Context

the Operator can envisage cases requiring **`>1`** Requirement Atom for the same Entity because the Claims differ. the earlier proposed limit of **`<=1`** Requirement Atom **and** **`<=1`** Delivery Atom per Entity remains unresolved. distinct Claims **and** duplicated authority for the same Claim are different cases; correctly assigned Subjects, applicable Scope Units, **and** Local Tiers require consideration **before** choosing a rule.

## Disposition

deferred for later consideration at the Operator's request. this Concern records an open design question; it does **not** establish a cardinality rule **or** block the current migration.

## Summary

Should a future model support non-Property bearer dependence?

## Concern

Should a future model support an Entity whose identity depends on an immediate bearer but which is not a Property?

- If yes, define that future Entity and its bearer contract explicitly without treating it as a Property or restoring a superseded Relation merely by name.
- If no, continue to use the Property bearer and inverse contracts for the selected model.

The selected model currently treats a dependent Entity as a Property. The working choice is to adopt IS_PROPERTY_OF and HAS_PROPERTY, then retire the superseded IS_BORNE_BY and BEARS definitions and their inverse Rule. This future-extension question does not block that ordered change.

## Evidences

CA-R-1260 describes a Dependent Entity whose identity requires an immediate bearer. CA-R-1243 defines BEARS as the derived inverse. CA-R-1456 calls those names historical and superseded. The newer IS_PROPERTY_OF and HAS_PROPERTY Declarations describe Property bearing; the Node Declaration classifies Node dependents as Properties. The declared-entity universe also includes entities outside the Node branch, so that Node rule alone does not resolve the wider historical domain.

## Blast radius

A future non-Property dependent Entity would need an explicit bearer contract before it can be admitted. The selected Property contract and the historical predecessor sources remain available without adding an unsupported Relation to the current model.

## Question

Does `p.**[name format]{:n}` count all selected descendant Properties together across every depth?

## Details

- `p.**` selects all descendant Properties recursively.
- `p.*` selects immediate Properties.

The existing aggregate-count rule is confirmed. CA-R-2472 records selector composition.

How does a Step select its work and bind parameters?

## Summary

Declare Occurrent Nodes and execution-event Relations

## Proposal

Declare the Occurrent hierarchy and its execution-event Relations.

- Execution has Workflow Run, Step Run and Action Run kinds.
- Runtime has Internal Local, Internal Remote, External Local and External Remote Runtime kinds.
- Session is narrower than External Remote Runtime.
- Local means on the Operator's machine.
- Internal means part of the CAPRMEDIO application.
- Each Event Record records one Event. Its other retained recording fields remain in place.
- Event author attribution is not included in the staged Event Record declaration. Retirement of R2582, R2583 and R2622 is planned as part of coordinated adoption; they remain Current until then.
- Executions produce Events and run in Runtimes.
- Step is recursive. Each Step uses exactly one execution form: RUNS one Action, RUNS one Workflow, or CONTAINS one or more Steps.
- Retire the separate Substep kind. Step Run executes Step at any nesting level. Actual Workflow instances remain with their owners.

## Run Properties

Runs are not Atoms. Run Properties are deferred, including Header, Container and ID. Atom.Header.Container is unchanged. Formal Run parentage is retained. A Step Run has one Workflow Run or Step Run parent. An Action Run launched by a Step Run belongs to that Step Run. R2750@1, R2751@1 and R2752@1 are rebased with explicit directional permissions and Container classifications. No Run Property Draft is created.

Declarations define the model kinds and their permitted Relations. Occurrences and their records have distinct identities. Reusable definitions admit actual Runs. ## Summary

Consolidate CFEL syntax and precise Relations

## Proposal

1. Define every CFEL operator, Relation and expression construct.
2. Keep each Atom's normative Claim about its active Subject.
3. Use short statements and coherent names. Remove staging notes and repeated rules.
4. Preserve exact predecessors and frozen references.

## Syntax decisions

- `=` tests a condition. `==` states a required or derived value. `?==` supplies an effective default when the Property is missing. These statements perform no business mutation.
- Default resolution preserves valid explicit values and rejects invalid supplied values.
- Numeric ranges are inclusive. Format constraints separated by commas all apply.
- Project Settings AI Agent Confidence Threshold defaults to integer 90 in 0..100. The Plan override uses the same numeric domain.
- A standalone typed instance binding lasts through its CFEL block.
- An IF binding lasts through its condition and matching THEN group. A new binding uses a different name from a bound outer variable.
- Mixed AND/OR expressions use parentheses.
- Text stays bare when unambiguous. Double quotes protect text containing syntax. Inside quotes, only escaped quote and escaped backslash are valid escapes.
- Model names and Property paths remain references.

## Precise Relations

- SPECIALIZES is Direct from a specific Atom to a general Atom. Its Claim is more specific or stricter in the same or narrower applicability, while preserving applicable parent constraints.
- IS_SPECIALIZED_BY is the Derived inverse.
- Classify each existing child_of link by its actual Claims. Evaluation, implementation and dependency use their own precise Relations.
- Endpoint domains and outgoing permissions are separate. Each direction has its own applicable permission.

## Focused source cleanup

- Keep Relation Name and Meaning Claims about those Properties.
- Put the existing edge-identity rule in Relation, preserving it during Name cleanup.
- Preserve endpoint restrictions across the combined Formal Claim and Prose Claim.

## Model scope

- Entity means anything represented in the Subject graph.
- Relation, Term and Node keep their separate branches.
- Relation and Term each declare Property-bearing permissions. Narrower entities inherit the applicable rules.

## Rationale

Distinct symbols separate conditions, required values and defaults. Explicit scopes preserve variable identity. Parentheses and quoting resolve syntax without implicit precedence. Separate LOOKUP authority keeps default assignment focused. Precise Relations describe what each contribution does.

## Summary

Move Atom containment into Header.Container

## Decisions

- Header.Container is one mapping with exactly one key.
- `scope_unit` stores the containing Scope Unit ID.
- `atom` stores the containing Atom's base ID; it selects Current by default.
- Names, name suffixes and paths are resolved from the ID.
- The CAPRMEDIO Project Scope Unit has ID `CA-SU-00`.
- `CA-SU--1` is the predefined Scope Unit named `world`, without a Declaration.
- The root Project Declaration Atom uses `scope_unit: CA-SU--1`. If omitted, that mapping is its effective default.
- The Project Scope Unit itself stays unordered, without order.number or a formal parent.
- Header.Relations is optional and carries no duplicate containment fact.
- D264 and D266 remain. The declared Container and placement readback identify the same fact.
- Runs use formal containment Relations. Run Properties remain deferred.

## Rationale

IDs preserve references through Scope Unit renames and moves. The Project and its Declaration Atom are different objects. Predefined world supplies the Declaration Atom's bootstrap Container without another Declaration or a scalar exception.

## Source changes

1. Require stable IDs on declared Scope Units; assign the root ID in its specific Declaration.
2. Exempt predefined world from Declaration coverage and the ordinary non-Project parent requirement.
3. Declare the Container mapping and its two ID-valued leaf Properties.
4. Reconcile Header, Relation serialization, placement and validation consumers.
5. Adopt the reviewed source/schema packet with compatible readers, then migrate carriers and refresh the seven MODEL views.

## Summary

Unify declarative CFEL paths and instance Formats

## Proposal

CFEL is declarative: Claims state participants, scope, constraints and required values; they do not perform I/O or business actions. A Formal Claim is self-contained. `topics.main_subject` identifies the one declared Subject and is not an implicit operand or binding.

- `X//Y` selects a narrower kind with inheritance; `Whole/Part` expresses immediate containment. The coordinated source and consumer migration is not yet adopted.
- `<Kind>` identifies a Model kind used as an object Format. `$x[<Kind>, (conditions)]` selects a named participant, and `$<Kind>` an anonymous instance; selection creates nothing.
- `$x[<KindA> OR <KindB>]` binds one participant drawn from either kind; a following count applies to the combined selection. Kind alternatives remain Formats, not new graph Nodes.
- `VALUES(p)` selects the actual direct Property value occurrences, preserving duplicates without traversing nested Properties or treating constraints as stored values. CA-R-2904@1-draft declares this construct.
- `FOR EACH $x[<Kind>, (conditions)]: ( ... )` expresses universal quantification. The body contains semicolon-separated expressions; no `WITH` or `IN` header keyword is used. Existing bounded IF binding and no-shadowing remain.
- Formal Claims use `# model` before `# instances` when both groups occur. `=` tests a condition, `==` states a required or derived value, and `?==` supplies a default under its own rule.
- HAS_ALLOWED_VALUE (`:=`, CA-R-2826) supplies allowed literal alternatives; applicable local and inherited alternatives combine by OR. HAS_VALUE_CONSTRAINT (`::`, CA-R-2828) supplies applicable local and inherited constraints combined by AND. Final admissibility is the allowed-value OR group AND the constraint AND group. When no allowed-value group exists, omit it (true): there is no enumeration restriction. Qualified Subjects retain `:=`.
- The staged CA-R-2827@1 and CA-R-2829@1 pure-inverse Declarations are superseded for coordinated withdrawal; their Draft files remain until migration and are not proposed for adoption. Literal values remain values, not newly invented Nodes.
- An inverse alias is a phantom reverse-view name of its canonical Relation, not a literal or a separate Alias kind. Fixed Model Relation references require no `$` binding: `Relation//CONTAINS ((IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR)) Relation//IS_CONTAINED_BY;`. `IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR` is declared in staged Draft CA-R-2951@1. The distinction between GOVERNS and HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT remains an open question.
- Atom Header storage concerns the Atom itself: outgoing Relation facts default to `Atom.Header.Relations`, while `IS_CONTAINED_BY` is stored only in `Atom.Header.Container`. This Atom schema rule does not add storage Properties to Relation.
- CFEL has no modeled Operator descriptor catalog in this proposal. Actor Operator and AI Agent remain distinct Actor kinds.

## CFEL vocabulary and dependency order

CFEL operators and constructs include grouping `()`, `FOR EACH`, `==`, `=`, and `IF`/`THEN`. `ELSE` is a proposed construct whose definition and binding scope remain open; it is not adopted.

Canonical Relation names, their inverse aliases, and their short notation form the Relation vocabulary. Examples of short notation include `:=`, `::`, `.`, `/`, `//`, `+>`, and `>|`; the governing Relation declarations determine their direction and meaning.

`VALUES`, `COUNT`, `MAX`, `LOOKUP`, `FENCED_LABELS`, and `alias` are pure functions. `UNIQUE` and `DETERMINES` are Boolean predicates; `DISTINCT` is a modifier. The semicolon and `#` group comments are punctuation, not Relation names or graph entities.

The planned definition sequence is `[]` Format, then `<>` Model reference, then `INSTANCE_OF`. A Format can contain a reference to a declared Model kind, and `INSTANCE_OF` relates an admitted instance to its declared kind. For example, `$a[<Atom>] ((INSTANCE_OF)) Atom` uses a bound Atom instance and a bare Model kind where the Relation endpoints admit them. These three integrated definitions are prospective and remain subject to review; this sequence does not rename the canonical Relation.

## Topic fields

- `topics.main_subject` replaces `subjects.active`.
- `topics.dependencies` replaces `subjects.passive`.
- The model paths are `Atom.Header.Topics.Main Subject` and `Atom.Header.Topics.Dependencies`.
- Each Atom has exactly one Main Subject. Dependencies retain their existing direct contextual meaning and cardinality.
- Topic and Subject have similar everyday meanings. Main distinguishes the one selected Subject from the other dependency Topics.
- Mentioning a Topic alone does not make it a dependency. This naming change does not add a mentions collection or a Topic model kind.

## Rationale

One declarative notation separates value admission, value constraints and required results while retaining source identity and inherited meaning. Model kinds, instances and Relation facts remain distinct.

## Staged Draft cohort

The following **51 actual Draft Atoms** are the pinned language and value-Relation cohort. They are staged evidence, not Current authority or implementation.

CA-R-2951@1 declares IS_INVERSE_ALIAS_FOR. Canonical Relation Drafts CA-R-2478@6, CA-R-2762@3, and CA-R-2766@3 adopt the inverse-alias approach; CA-R-2817@1 and CA-R-2247@12 are rebased grammar Drafts. These six Drafts do not constitute a complete canonical Relation inventory and are not Current authority.

Complete and review the CFEL source cohort first, including the pending candidate 55-authority review manifest; this is not Current authority or proof of complete language coverage. Then migrate applicable Current and Draft sources in place mechanically, preserving their content and identity under the reviewed migration. After that source migration, hand off implementation, adapters, data conversion, fixtures and tests to CA #3. Preserve Current grammar until coordinated adoption. Rebuild affected MODEL projections after source acceptance.

# Summary

Establish explicit Term Definitions and staged CCE consistency checks

## Question

How were the seventeen-RMED CCE packet and its necessary consumers reconciled with the Current subject system and promoted?

## Scope

Source adoption of the original seventeen-RMED packet in CORE_META_MODEL, including the three previously promoted Methods, plus narrow compatibility updates to optional terminology consumers. This Analysis remains a provisional tracking Draft. Runtime, parser, generated-view publication, project-wide vocabulary migration and complete occurrence review are outside these source effects.

## Approach

Apply the Operator's latest decisions over older Draft text. Verify Current authority from Project Structure, rebase stale candidates without losing adopted metadata or formal constraints, independently review the new Subject bindings and semantic boundaries, allocate fresh identities under the canonical Project lock, archive actual Current predecessors and consume only the fourteen remaining packet Drafts. Record actual source effects independently in the Journal.

## Results

### Accepted model

Each reusable Term has one explicit authoritative R/Term Definition. M explains writing its content; E checks well-formedness and consistent use in stages: entity names, Claim, Claim Scope, Semantics, Details and remaining authored fields. D carries content and review evidence through existing carriers. No dictionary Projection or lookup service is a prerequisite.

Complete canonical entity names retain one-to-one bindings and exact authored usage. `atom.id` and `projection.id` are distinct complete qualified property names using the same ID meaning; their terminal component need not be globally unique. # Summary

Move Terms to the Entity root and Method definitions

## Question

Which source changes implement the Operator-confirmed direct Term branch, Method-owned lexical definitions and Empty meaning without silently changing Current authority or unrelated identities?

## Scope

CORE_META_MODEL Term placement and meaning ownership: direct `Entity/Term`, initially flat named Term instances, Method Type Term Definition, the explicit Empty, ID, Entity, Term and Property lexical definitions, the direct `Entity/Property` kind and the approved IS_PROPERTY_OF / derived HAS_PROPERTY Relation pair, structural and ownership Requirements, and source consumers of the old path or Requirement-qualified Type. This packet prepares Drafts only. Current adoption, identity repair, numeric allocation, archival, runtime, generated graphs, release and a complete terminology-coverage claim are outside these effects.

## Approach

Use the latest human decisions over earlier R classification and Continuant placement. Pin exact Current source paths, versions and hashes. Keep structural Requirements separate from lexical Methods, prepare coordinated N+1 consumer successors, and preserve existing Claims except the approved role/path changes. Review the primary Drafts independently and verify both mechanical successors and the later semantic corrections against their sources. Do not use an ambiguous canonical ID as a source selector.

### Rationale from the Operator's input

This rationale follows the Operator's messages in this conversation. The latest explicit correction controls earlier wording. The points below connect those inputs to the Drafts; source-governed compatibility work is identified separately.

1. **Precise vocabulary must preserve entity identity.** The Operator asked for a “precise dictionary” and “no synonyms”, then corrected the initial Term/entity equivalence: “it's not Terms, it's entities.” The resulting constraint applies to complete canonical entity names: one complete name identifies one entity, and references to that entity retain that name. This motivates the canonical-name Rule, CCE authoring Methods and naming Evaluations. It does not require a different Term for every entity.

2. **Terms are reusable components; full expressions identify entities.** The Operator used Package in Package, Eval Package and Runtime Package, and Unit in Scope Unit and Code Unit to explain reuse. The later correction requires the full expression when naming an entity. Those short lexical forms illustrate components, not complete canonical entity names outside the Term branch. The supplied `Atom/Content Role: X/Type: X` shows why repeated X components can be valid within different qualifications. The accepted `atom.id` and `projection.id` likewise reuse ID while identifying distinct qualified properties. These inputs motivate the Term-kind, subject-expression, component-reuse and full-name Drafts and their evaluation fixtures. Existing value-admission rules still apply independently in each qualified context.

3. **Structural definition and lexical definition have different targets.** The Operator distinguished an Entity with Subject `Entity` and Type R / Entity Definition from its reusable Term. The final correction makes Entity the sole exception outside the Term branch whose complete canonical name can also be one Term, “because it's our subject root.” Thus the structural definition governs `Entity`; the lexical definition governs `Entity/Term//Entity`. The earlier general permission for any outside entity to have a complete name equal to a Term is superseded. The Project and Project Implementation root examples do not extend this naming exception. The separate request “also we need Term Term” supplies the lexical target `Entity/Term//Term`, alongside the structural kind `Entity/Term`. Reusing Term in its own definition requires no further lexical instance.

4. **Terms need an explicit branch and dedicated meaning owners.** The Operator placed Terms in a “different root branch”, supplied `Entity/Term//Empty`, and deferred grouping: “maybe we'll group them later.” The Operator also settled “Term Definition is M”. Accordingly, the root and Term-kind Drafts establish the initially flat Term branch; the new Method Type declaration admits the intended specialized Type; M / Term Definition Drafts supply lexical meanings. R / Entity Definition continues to define model entities and their structure. The separate authoring Method explains how to write definition content. Changing the path alone would leave old Role/Type references and consumers inconsistent, which explains the coordinated successor Drafts.

5. **Checks should follow the authored source in stages.** The Operator found the proposed projection too complex and requested explicit definitions followed by occurrence review: entity names, Claim, Claim Scope, Semantics, Details and remaining fields. This motivates the authoring, Evaluation and evidence-carrier Drafts. They check declared meaning, ownership, complete names and consistent occurrences directly in the sources. A generated dictionary or Terms Graph is not a prerequisite for that review.

6. **The concrete Term definitions retain the Operator's boundaries.** For ID, the Operator supplied a unique identifier used to find an entity instance across Continuant and Occurrent instances, then bounded uniqueness by matching prefixes. The spelling examples do not decide version identity or lifecycle semantics. For Empty, the Operator supplied null, the empty string and omitted input, clarifying undefined as omission. The Empty Method gives the Create Draft discussion a precise input condition without broadening it to general truthiness. These are the reasons for the ID replacement and new Empty Draft; this proposal does not implement Workflow execution.

7. **Property is the one canonical concept and Term.** The Operator first grounded dependence in a Relation and permitted `Entity/Dependent Entity`, then explicitly selected Property as the single Term. The later decision supersedes that separate kind and lexical name. The structural target is `Entity/Property`, with lexical owner `Entity/Term//Property`. The Operator approved `IS_PROPERTY_OF` with strictly derived inverse `HAS_PROPERTY`; no old-name aliases are introduced. The direct Relation runs from Property to immediate bearer; dot notation runs from bearer to Property. The Operator places no separate Carrier and applicable direct-value Format/cardinality in Claim, exactly one outgoing Relation in the Formal claim, and Property-as-bearer nesting in Semantics. The latest two-sided notation places `{1}` before the token: `Property {1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Bearer` counts outgoing Relation instances per Property, independently of value cardinality and of a Relation's two endpoints. The extra generic identity/lifecycle clauses were rejected. The Operator subsequently approved prohibiting IS_PROPERTY_OF cycles, including self-loops. This applies only to Property bearer Relations.
8. **Drafts record decisions before adoption.** The Operator repeatedly requested Draft updates, asked for the proper format, and stated that the latest input beats previous input. The packet therefore corrects superseded interpretations in Drafts and keeps Current adoption separate. Root structure, kind definitions, Method Type, lexical owners, naming rules, authoring Methods, Evaluations and consumers must agree before promotion. N+1 versions, exact source pins and replacement identities are governed compatibility requirements supporting that agreement. The five original Property/Type/Artifact target cases now have Draft dispositions; the Draft count does not establish that their logic is settled. The Operator also specified that the Workflow work belongs in another A/Spec Proposal with its own Drafts.

## Results

### Confirmed decisions

- Terms form a direct branch `Entity/Term`, alongside the existing root branches. Do not retain the earlier narrower placement under `Entity/Object/Continuant/Term` or infer inherited Continuant classification from that former path.
- Begin with flat named instances, including `Entity/Term//Empty`, `Entity/Term//ID` and `Entity/Term//Property`. No intermediate Term groups or categories are introduced. Grouping may be considered later.
- Type and Content Role are Properties, including when used for classification. `X.Y` addresses Property Y; generic `X: Y` means Y is an allowed value of X; `X/(.Y: Z)` qualifies the whole X by its relative Property and admitted value, retaining inheritance from X. Existing YAML keys represent these same Properties. Syntax alone establishes no Entity or value admission.
- **M / Term Definition** supplies one Term's authoritative lexical meaning as an authoring and interpretation convention. This supersedes the earlier R/Term Definition classification.
- **R / Entity Definition** continues to define the Term kind and its inherited structure. M lexical definitions supply instance-specific meaning, not duplicate structural Requirements. A separate Method explains how to write definition content; E checks well-formedness and consistent occurrences.
- **Empty means an omitted input, null, or the empty string `""`.** `undefined` denotes omitted input; it is not the literal string `"undefined"` or a general truthiness test. Whitespace-only strings, `0`, `false`, `[]` and `{}` are outside this exact set.
- ID keeps the approved meaning of a unique identifier used to find one Continuant or Occurrent entity instance, with uniqueness bounded by matching prefixes. Moving its definition to M or its target to `Entity/Term//ID` adds no lifecycle equivalence, case-folding, parser or ID-allocation semantics.

The R Entity-root successor adds direct Term and Property branches; moving reference strings alone would not establish the new hierarchy. `Entity/Property` is an entity kind and `Entity/Term//Property` its lexical Term instance. Property is the sole canonical name for the former Property/Dependent Entity distinction. Its direct Relation is `IS_PROPERTY_OF`, with strictly derived `HAS_PROPERTY`. No pairwise disjointness, new Primary Entity branch or lifecycle restriction is inferred. The separately approved Property bearer-cycle prohibition is recorded below. The Term-kind successor preserves `Name[string]{1}`. The Governed Term successor is based on Current CA-R-1319@25, Type Rule, and requires exactly one active Method Term Definition owner.

```text
Source {forward-count}RELATION{reverse-count} Target
Step {1}+>{1+} Workflow

The count before the token constrains links in the written Source-to-Target direction per Source; the count after it constrains the reverse count per Target. # Summary

Move Terms to the Entity root and Method definitions

## Question

Which source changes implement the Operator-confirmed direct Term branch, Method-owned lexical definitions and Empty meaning without silently changing Current authority or unrelated identities?

## Scope

CORE_META_MODEL Term placement and meaning ownership: direct `Entity/Term`, initially flat named Term instances, Method Type Term Definition, the explicit Empty, ID, Entity, Term and Property lexical definitions, the direct `Entity/Property` kind and the approved IS_PROPERTY_OF / derived HAS_PROPERTY Relation pair, structural and ownership Requirements, and source consumers of the old path or Requirement-qualified Type. This packet prepares Drafts only. Current adoption, identity repair, numeric allocation, archival, runtime, generated graphs, release and a complete terminology-coverage claim are outside these effects.

## Approach

Use the latest human decisions over earlier R classification and Continuant placement. Pin exact Current source paths, versions and hashes. Keep structural Requirements separate from lexical Methods, prepare coordinated N+1 consumer successors, and preserve existing Claims except the approved role/path changes. Review the primary Drafts independently and verify both mechanical successors and the later semantic corrections against their sources. Do not use an ambiguous canonical ID as a source selector.

### Rationale from the Operator's input

This rationale follows the Operator's messages in this conversation. The latest explicit correction controls earlier wording. The points below connect those inputs to the Drafts; source-governed compatibility work is identified separately.

1. **Precise vocabulary must preserve entity identity.** The Operator asked for a “precise dictionary” and “no synonyms”, then corrected the initial Term/entity equivalence: “it's not Terms, it's entities.” The resulting constraint applies to complete canonical entity names: one complete name identifies one entity, and references to that entity retain that name. This motivates the canonical-name Rule, CCE authoring Methods and naming Evaluations. It does not require a different Term for every entity.

2. **Terms are reusable components; full expressions identify entities.** The Operator used Package in Package, Eval Package and Runtime Package, and Unit in Scope Unit and Code Unit to explain reuse. The later correction requires the full expression when naming an entity. Those short lexical forms illustrate components, not complete canonical entity names outside the Term branch. The supplied `Atom/Content Role: X/Type: X` shows why repeated X components can be valid within different qualifications. The accepted `atom.id` and `projection.id` likewise reuse ID while identifying distinct qualified properties. These inputs motivate the Term-kind, subject-expression, component-reuse and full-name Drafts and their evaluation fixtures. Existing value-admission rules still apply independently in each qualified context.

3. **Structural definition and lexical definition have different targets.** The Operator distinguished an Entity with Subject `Entity` and Type R / Entity Definition from its reusable Term. The final correction makes Entity the sole exception outside the Term branch whose complete canonical name can also be one Term, “because it's our subject root.” Thus the structural definition governs `Entity`; the lexical definition governs `Entity/Term//Entity`. The earlier general permission for any outside entity to have a complete name equal to a Term is superseded. The Project and Project Implementation root examples do not extend this naming exception. The separate request “also we need Term Term” supplies the lexical target `Entity/Term//Term`, alongside the structural kind `Entity/Term`. Reusing Term in its own definition requires no further lexical instance.

4. **Terms need an explicit branch and dedicated meaning owners.** The Operator placed Terms in a “different root branch”, supplied `Entity/Term//Empty`, and deferred grouping: “maybe we'll group them later.” The Operator also settled “Term Definition is M”. Accordingly, the root and Term-kind Drafts establish the initially flat Term branch; the new Method Type declaration admits the intended specialized Type; M / Term Definition Drafts supply lexical meanings. R / Entity Definition continues to define model entities and their structure. The separate authoring Method explains how to write definition content. Changing the path alone would leave old Role/Type references and consumers inconsistent, which explains the coordinated successor Drafts.

5. **Checks should follow the authored source in stages.** The Operator found the proposed projection too complex and requested explicit definitions followed by occurrence review: entity names, Claim, Claim Scope, Semantics, Details and remaining fields. This motivates the authoring, Evaluation and evidence-carrier Drafts. They check declared meaning, ownership, complete names and consistent occurrences directly in the sources. A generated dictionary or Terms Graph is not a prerequisite for that review.

6. **The concrete Term definitions retain the Operator's boundaries.** For ID, the Operator supplied a unique identifier used to find an entity instance across Continuant and Occurrent instances, then bounded uniqueness by matching prefixes. The spelling examples do not decide version identity or lifecycle semantics. For Empty, the Operator supplied null, the empty string and omitted input, clarifying undefined as omission. The Empty Method gives the Create Draft discussion a precise input condition without broadening it to general truthiness. These are the reasons for the ID replacement and new Empty Draft; this proposal does not implement Workflow execution.

7. **Property is the one canonical concept and Term.** The Operator first grounded dependence in a Relation and permitted `Entity/Dependent Entity`, then explicitly selected Property as the single Term. The later decision supersedes that separate kind and lexical name. The structural target is `Entity/Property`, with lexical owner `Entity/Term//Property`. The Operator approved `IS_PROPERTY_OF` with strictly derived inverse `HAS_PROPERTY`; no old-name aliases are introduced. The direct Relation runs from Property to immediate bearer; dot notation runs from bearer to Property. The Operator places no separate Carrier and applicable direct-value Format/cardinality in Claim, exactly one outgoing Relation in the Formal claim, and Property-as-bearer nesting in Semantics. The latest two-sided notation places `{1}` before the token: `Property {1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Bearer` counts outgoing Relation instances per Property, independently of value cardinality and of a Relation's two endpoints. The extra generic identity/lifecycle clauses were rejected. The Operator subsequently approved prohibiting IS_PROPERTY_OF cycles, including self-loops. This applies only to Property bearer Relations.
8. **Drafts record decisions before adoption.** The Operator repeatedly requested Draft updates, asked for the proper format, and stated that the latest input beats previous input. The packet therefore corrects superseded interpretations in Drafts and keeps Current adoption separate. Root structure, kind definitions, Method Type, lexical owners, naming rules, authoring Methods, Evaluations and consumers must agree before promotion. N+1 versions, exact source pins and replacement identities are governed compatibility requirements supporting that agreement. The five original Property/Type/Artifact target cases now have Draft dispositions; the Draft count does not establish that their logic is settled. The Operator also specified that the Workflow work belongs in another A/Spec Proposal with its own Drafts.

## Results

### Confirmed decisions

- Terms form a direct branch `Entity/Term`, alongside the existing root branches. Do not retain the earlier narrower placement under `Entity/Object/Continuant/Term` or infer inherited Continuant classification from that former path.
- Begin with flat named instances, including `Entity/Term//Empty`, `Entity/Term//ID` and `Entity/Term//Property`. No intermediate Term groups or categories are introduced. Grouping may be considered later.
- Type and Content Role are Properties, including when used for classification. `X.Y` addresses Property Y; generic `X: Y` means Y is an allowed value of X; `X/(.Y: Z)` qualifies the whole X by its relative Property and admitted value, retaining inheritance from X. Existing YAML keys represent these same Properties. Syntax alone establishes no Entity or value admission.
- **M / Term Definition** supplies one Term's authoritative lexical meaning as an authoring and interpretation convention. This supersedes the earlier R/Term Definition classification.
- **R / Entity Definition** continues to define the Term kind and its inherited structure. M lexical definitions supply instance-specific meaning, not duplicate structural Requirements. A separate Method explains how to write definition content; E checks well-formedness and consistent occurrences.
- **Empty means an omitted input, null, or the empty string `""`.** `undefined` denotes omitted input; it is not the literal string `"undefined"` or a general truthiness test. Whitespace-only strings, `0`, `false`, `[]` and `{}` are outside this exact set.
- ID keeps the approved meaning of a unique identifier used to find one Continuant or Occurrent entity instance, with uniqueness bounded by matching prefixes. Moving its definition to M or its target to `Entity/Term//ID` adds no lifecycle equivalence, case-folding, parser or ID-allocation semantics.

The R Entity-root successor adds direct Term and Property branches; moving reference strings alone would not establish the new hierarchy. `Entity/Property` is an entity kind and `Entity/Term//Property` its lexical Term instance. Property is the sole canonical name for the former Property/Dependent Entity distinction. Its direct Relation is `IS_PROPERTY_OF`, with strictly derived `HAS_PROPERTY`. No pairwise disjointness, new Primary Entity branch or lifecycle restriction is inferred. The separately approved Property bearer-cycle prohibition is recorded below. The Term-kind successor preserves `Name[string]{1}`. The Governed Term successor is based on Current CA-R-1319@25, Type Rule, and requires exactly one active Method Term Definition owner.

## Summary

Notation baseline for intuitive symbol review

## Question

Which short keyboard notations make these meanings easiest to read correctly?

## Scope

Latest Operator-agreed meanings, including Draft changes. Latest human input
supersedes earlier wording. This is review input, not Current adoption or
evidence of parser support.

## Approach

Use this baseline explicitly; do not infer meanings from other languages.
The Astra-max comparison is complete. The Operator then selected the
Composition and Classification spellings below and clarified two-sided
Relation cardinality. Use compact English-keyboard symbols while balancing
visual readability and intuitive understanding. No qualification replacement
has been selected; `/`, `()` and `.` retain their meanings.

## Results

### Meaning baseline

| Notation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X/Y` | Y is narrower than X and inherits X's applicable features and constraints. |
| `Part +> Whole` | Part is part of Whole. The pointer faces the Whole; containment supplies no inheritance. |
| `Whole <+ Part` | Whole has Part: the reverse written view of the same containment fact. The pointer still faces the Whole. |
| `X >\| Y` | X has Classification Y. The pointer faces the Classification endpoint, marked by the bar. This is axis applicability, not membership in a particular group. |
| `Y \|< X` | Y is the Classification applicable to X: the reverse written view of the same fact. |
| `X.Y` | Y is a Property borne by X. |
| `X: Y` | Y is an allowed value of X, regardless of X's kind or preceding path. This is not assignment and does not imply that X is a Property. |
| `X/(.Y: Z)` | An X qualified by its own Property Y and allowed value Z. The qualified X inherits from X; Y does not become a subtype of X. |
| `K//Name` | The named instance Name of kind K, not a narrower kind. |
| `[format]` | Declared Format of a Property's direct values. |
| `x.y[format]{cardinality}` | Format and count of the Property's direct values: `{n}` exactly n, `{n+}` at least n, `{n..m}` inclusive range. |
| `Source {f}RELATION{r} Target` | Two independent directional counts: f constrains links from each Source toward Target; r constrains reverse links from each Target toward Source. An omitted side is unspecified. These do not count Relation arity. |
| `@` | Call/reference to an already declared Entity; it does not declare a new Entity. |
| `()` | Logical grouping of the enclosed expression, including relative Property qualification. |
| `Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` | A named Relation with its declared direction and endpoints. The double-parenthesis form is a distinct compound notation. |

### Examples and boundaries

```text
Atom.Status >| Status Group: Draft <+ Draft
Atom.Status >| Status Group: Archived <+ Archived
Atom.Status >| Status Group: Current <+ * not in (Draft, Archived)

Step {1}+>{1+} Workflow
Workflow {1+}<+{1} Step
```

Status Group classifies Atom Status values. Each group contains the Status
values shown on its right. `*` ranges only over admitted Atom Status values.
These three groups are mutually exclusive and exhaustive within that domain.
The wildcard mapping is Formal claim text; it does not introduce an executable
Boolean or query grammar for Subjects.

The last two lines are equivalent: each Step belongs to exactly one Workflow,
and each Workflow has one or more Steps. Reversing the written direction
swaps the two count positions. Missing counts remain unspecified; property
value counts remain separate. This supersedes the former Relation convention
where a single postfix count always counted outgoing links from the left.

`Atom/(.Type: Method)` denotes the whole qualified Atom, which inherits from
Atom. This notation example alone does not admit Method as a Type value;
the admitted Content Role example is `Atom/(.Content Role: Method)`.

Containment retains direct IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS.
`>|` retains HAS_CLASSIFICATION, and `|<` is its selected reverse view.
Choosing that view introduces no separately authored reverse fact or new
canonical inverse Relation Type name. The selected spellings replace bare
`>` / `<` containment and the earlier `::` axis spelling. The selected
Composition pointer faces the Whole, superseding the opposite direction in
the FPF report's earlier conditional `+>` candidate; that report stays unchanged.

### Authorized adoption and migration

The Operator requests: update/review/fix the full Term/Property proposal,
promote the reviewed closed batch to Active, then migrate Current notation.
The scope includes the 125-Draft packet and required notation owners; it
preserves the accepted Property relation and Method-owned Term definitions.

Classification is not a new Entity kind. HAS_CLASSIFICATION and
IS_CLASSIFIED_BY are named Relation instances under Graph Syntax; a generic
Classification word definition, if needed, belongs to Terms. No inverse pair
is inferred merely from listing those two Relation names.

Review and repair stale successors from their live Current owners before
promotion. Use the admitted lifecycle/identity-allocation path, preserve
archived/history bytes, migrate only reviewed expressions, update parser and
consumers together, and rebuild derived projections. A source/promotion
record alone does not establish implementation or migration success.

### Source alignment

The table incorporates generic `:`, `@` for an already declared Entity,
logical grouping `()`, the selected symbol pairs and two-sided Relation
cardinality. The repaired full proposal now has a 130-Draft adoption closure,
including the 125-Draft register and five required notation owners. Older
Current wording remains migration work; it does not override the latest human
decisions. Draft preparation does not establish Current adoption.

Approved AST support and its graph, lookup and validator callers are prepared
in source. Ten focused parser tests pass. Installed runtime activation,
Current publication and migration have not occurred. Broader test runs have
separate filesystem limits; they are not an all-green certification.

Supporting Drafts: [notation](../../04_requirement/draft/CA-R-1931@17-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-RULE--use-subject-path-separators-for-broader-to-narrower-and-bearer-to-dependent.md),
[HAS_CLASSIFICATION](../../04_requirement/draft/classification-and-status-groups/CA-R-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-RELATION_DEFINITION--define-has-classification.md),
and [Format/cardinality](../../04_requirement/draft/CA-R-2243@3-draft-CORE_META_MODEL-ENTITY_DEFINITION--define-cardinality-notation.md).

## TLDR

The selected pairs are `Part +> Whole / Whole <+ Part` and
`X >| Y / Y |< X`. Relation counts constrain both directions independently;
Property value counts stay postfix. Source parser checks pass; adoption and
Current notation migration remain pending actual lifecycle execution.

# Summary

Declare the Node branch and derive the graph from Formal Claims

## Question

How should the graph model, Declaration Forms and notation change so that one coherent source declares each Node without repeated inherited definitions or ambiguous constraints?

## Scope

This proposal covers governing Drafts for the Node branch, graph Relations and notation, Role/Form naming, carrier mappings and formal Scope. It records the latest human decisions; earlier conflicting alternatives are superseded. The [Epic successor Draft](../../../../../03_plan/draft/CA-P-2694@39-draft-EPIC--entity-graph-refactor-stage-4-polishing.md) tracks adoption and implementation dependencies.

Actual Workflow, Step, Substep and Action instance review/migration is deferred by the latest Operator instruction. This pass reviews their model declarations and constraints; model-level examples do not perform instance review.

## Approach

Write the governing Drafts directly, keep the design rationale here, and review the packet before adoption. Preserve Current sources and completed publication history. Resolve exact source-to-Node mappings before replacing Definitions; never replace all `/` edges with composition.

## Results

### What changes

- **Carrier placement is explicit.** Use `@Carrier//Markdown file`. Deliver non-Content Objects into frontmatter. Deliver Content descendants into Markdown. Frontmatter is delimited YAML at the beginning of the file. Carrier filename/location are properties; location is repository-relative.
- **Node scope is explicit.** `Node/**, .**` selects narrower entities plus their Properties. Add `Node` when a rule also covers the root.

- **Names and values use separate expressions.** `p{:0..1}: [format]{:1}` separates occurrence from values. `p.*[...]` constrains immediate names. `p.**[...]` constrains names recursively. Expressions use semicolons.
- **Claim is one Property.** Keep `Atom.Content.Claim`. Formal content is an optional CFEL fence inside its Markdown value. No separate Formal Claim Property is retained. RMED Claim is required. Claim Scope, Semantics and Details are optional.
- **Delivery specifies representation.** `>>` delivers Objects to a referenced Carrier or its parts. Object means Node instance. Filename/location formula details remain separate until expressible.

- **Analysis is freeform.** `Atom.Content.**[string]{:0+}: [markdown]{:1}` constrains each dependent Property recursively. Sibling names are unique. `x.y.z` differs from `x.z`. Shared Atom constraints remain inherited.

- **Graph Syntax becomes CFEL — CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language.** CFEL covers expression syntax and meaning for Subject addresses and Formal Claims. Graph, CFEL and Carrier remain distinct model components. This names the existing language; it does not add notation.

- **Declaration is a Form of Requirement.** Use `Role: Requirement / Form: Declaration` and the existing R prefix. Within each selected effective MODEL, each declared member selected by `(Node, Node/**, .**)`, including Properties, has one effective Current Declaration with one matching active Subject. Count only those Declarations; other RMED may address the same Node. Use CFEL Formal Claims where possible. Use Claim prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express. Keep brief Semantics for Primary Nodes only. Each Property Declaration specifies two contracts: direct-value format/cardinality; dependent-entity format/cardinality. Unchanged inherited Properties reuse their original Declaration; explicit MODEL overrides select their local replacement. CFEL entities retain a Claim and may have Semantics.
- **Use Role and Form.** Rename Content Role to Role and the Role-specific Type to Form. These names express different purposes. Naming Methods prefer words that convey the actual distinction and reuse canonical expressions consistently; they do not impose a blanket word ban on useful contextual uses of `content`, `entity` or `type`.
- **Use two root kinds.** MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE are Primary Node kinds declared in CAPRMEDIO's self-describing MODEL. Their instance roots are `MODEL//CAPRMEDIO`, `PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO`, and the corresponding consumer Project roots. The consumer MODEL is optional. PROJECT STRUCTURE describes Scope Structure, Aspects and other declared components. Core Meta-Model contains the Atoms defining CAPRMEDIO's MODEL. Extensible axis configuration stays deferred.
- **Declare Scope outside the constrained Unit.** State permitted active/passive Subjects and Relation endpoints/cardinalities. ENGINE's proposed Scope permits allowed instances and implementation RMED; model definitions use their declared model-defining Scope. A local MODEL does not automatically widen ENGINE's Scope. Target Scope never grants wider authority.
- **Keep graph meanings distinct.** `/` narrows Primary Nodes with inheritance, `//` names their instances, `.` addresses Properties, `+>`/`<+` expresses composition, and `>|`/`|<` expresses classification. Composition uses canonical IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS; Container has yes/no value cases. `(Node, Node/**, .**)` includes the root, its recursive narrower branch and their recursive Properties. `@` references an existing target, parentheses group, and `in (...)` states membership. `:` denotes an allowed value, `=` tests, and `==` establishes a required/derived conclusion. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, as in `Atom/(.Role := Method)`. It does not write an instance value or exclude other allowed values from Atom.Role. Formal Claims keep `:` and `=` separate. Full Formal Claims stay out of Subjects; `..` and an invented `::` meaning are excluded.
- **Keep both counts.** Relation cardinality constrains both written directions; reversal swaps the counts. Property syntax uses separate expressions for occurrence, direct values and immediate dependent names: `p{:occurrence count}; p: [value format]{:value count}; p.*[name format]{:child count}`. YAML and Markdown mappings preserve that distinction, including mixed section content and nested headings.
- **Derive Primary Node versus Property.** The Node branch permits zero or one IS_PROPERTY_OF bearer. Zero derives Primary Node and no direct value; one derives Property and forbids narrowing and instantiation. Property-bearing must be acyclic. HAS_VALUE binds a Property on an instance to a literal, such as CA-P-123.version = 1; literals do not become declared graph Nodes.
- **Inheritance supplies effective rules.** Narrower instances receive applicable Relation cardinalities and declared Property constraints. Do not redeclare an inherited Property or create a new Declaration merely for an inherited lookup. Each Node's single effective Declaration in the selected MODEL resolves its Relation whitelist, endpoint constraints and counts. MODEL inheritance may replace any inherited rule through an explicit local override; unchanged Declarations are reused. Inheritance neither copies instance facts nor gives a Property a second bearer.
- **Operations use siblings and explicit composition.** Workflow, Step, Substep and Action narrow Operations. Each Workflow has one or more Steps, each Step one Workflow. A Step exclusively runs one Action or contains one or more Substeps. Each Substep has one Step and runs one Action. Actions may have zero or more callers. RUN bindings do not establish execution evidence.
- **Store authored instance Relations once.** Rename Subject links to active/passive; store modeled authored Node-instance links under `relations`, with typed containment references. Derive HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT from the dedicated Subject field and derive inverse views. The exact Assignee/Target reference migration remains open.

Relation Definitions now state allowed Host/Target signatures and reuse `Direct ((HAS_INVERSE)) Derived`. Inverse views have no separate Definition Atom. Repeated migration commentary is removed from the governing Drafts.

### Why these changes

The human rationale is to remove words that add no useful distinction, keep each complete expression precise, and avoid defining inherited material repeatedly. Primary Nodes, Properties, narrowing, composition and classification need different meanings so the graph can express constraints faithfully. A formal Scope outside its Unit makes the Unit's permitted authority explicit. One Declaration gathers a Node's structure and permissions; formal rules support graph reconstruction without turning an address into a second programming language. Syntax explanations remain useful where symbols are not self-explanatory.

### MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE — latest architecture

The two kinds are declared in MODEL//CAPRMEDIO itself. The named Subject roots are their instances:

```text
MODEL//CAPRMEDIO
PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects

MODEL//<PROJECT NAME>              (optional)
PROJECT STRUCTURE//<PROJECT NAME>
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects
```

The Project name above is a placeholder. A Project uses MODEL//CAPRMEDIO. It may define a local MODEL. A local MODEL inherits MODEL//CAPRMEDIO and may override any inherited rule. No inherited rule requires an overridable marker.

One Current authoritative Declaration per Node means one effective Declaration within the selected MODEL. Unchanged inherited Declarations are reused. A local replacement and its base source can coexist without becoming two effective owners in that MODEL. This selection context is distinct from the Project-wide instance context used by UNIQUE.

Core Meta-Model is a Scope Unit in CAPRMEDIO's Scope Structure. It contains the governing Atoms defining MODEL//CAPRMEDIO, including the two root kinds. This self-description does not identify the MODEL instance with its Scope Unit or PROJECT STRUCTURE instance. Existing ordered Scope Unit proposals remain subject to exact registration and mapping.

Model inheritance connects MODEL instances. It is separate from `/` Node narrowing and `<+` containment. The inheritance Relation name and exact Model-selection/override binding still need specification; this pass adds no invented notation or runtime behavior.

This replaces the earlier owner-wrapper layout and the MODEL-versus-PROJECT root split. The rationale is to distinguish reusable declarations from each Project's actual structure, reuse inherited material, and let each local MODEL control all of its effective rules.

### Adopted Atom register

The 139 registered Atoms are Current. The inventory includes 30 Primary Node and 60 Property Declarations. Each row links to its adopted Atom Version. The [migration record](node-declaration-20261031/migration-20261101/README.md) records predecessor archives, direct fixes, graph rebuilding and verification limits. Earlier preparation counts below are historical.

| `CA-R-2462@2` | Requirement / Declaration | [Declare Node](../../04_requirement/CA-R-2462-CORE_META_MODEL-DECLARATION--declare-node.md) |

# Summary

Declare the Node branch and derive the graph from Formal Claims

## Question

How should the graph model, Declaration Forms and notation change so that one coherent source declares each Node without repeated inherited definitions or ambiguous constraints?

## Scope

This proposal covers governing Drafts for the Node branch, graph Relations and notation, Role/Form naming, carrier mappings and formal Scope. It records the latest human decisions; earlier conflicting alternatives are superseded. The [Epic successor Draft](../../../../../03_plan/draft/CA-P-2694@39-draft-EPIC--entity-graph-refactor-stage-4-polishing.md) tracks adoption and implementation dependencies.

Actual Workflow, Step, Substep and Action instance review/migration is deferred by the latest Operator instruction. This pass reviews their model declarations and constraints; model-level examples do not perform instance review.

## Approach

Write the governing Drafts directly, keep the design rationale here, and review the packet before adoption. Preserve Current sources and completed publication history. Resolve exact source-to-Node mappings before replacing Definitions; never replace all `/` edges with composition.

## Results

### What changes

- **Carrier placement is explicit.** Use `@Carrier//Markdown file`. Deliver non-Content Objects into frontmatter. Deliver Content descendants into Markdown. Frontmatter is delimited YAML at the beginning of the file. Carrier filename/location are properties; location is repository-relative.
- **Node scope is explicit.** `Node/**, .**` selects narrower entities plus their Properties. Add `Node` when a rule also covers the root.

- **Names and values use separate expressions.** `p{:0..1}: [format]{:1}` separates occurrence from values. `p.*[...]` constrains immediate names. `p.**[...]` constrains names recursively. Expressions use semicolons.
- **Claim is one Property.** Keep `Atom.Content.Claim`. Formal content is an optional CFEL fence inside its Markdown value. No separate Formal Claim Property is retained. RMED Claim is required. Claim Scope, Semantics and Details are optional.
- **Delivery specifies representation.** `>>` delivers Objects to a referenced Carrier or its parts. Object means Node instance. Filename/location formula details remain separate until expressible.

- **Analysis is freeform.** `Atom.Content.**[string]{:0+}: [markdown]{:1}` constrains each dependent Property recursively. Sibling names are unique. `x.y.z` differs from `x.z`. Shared Atom constraints remain inherited.

- **Graph Syntax becomes CFEL — CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language.** CFEL covers expression syntax and meaning for Subject addresses and Formal Claims. Graph, CFEL and Carrier remain distinct model components. This names the existing language; it does not add notation.

- **Declaration is a Form of Requirement.** Use `Role: Requirement / Form: Declaration` and the existing R prefix. Within each selected effective MODEL, each declared member selected by `(Node, Node/**, .**)`, including Properties, has one effective Current Declaration with one matching active Subject. Count only those Declarations; other RMED may address the same Node. Use CFEL Formal Claims where possible. Use Claim prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express. Keep brief Semantics for Primary Nodes only. Each Property Declaration specifies two contracts: direct-value format/cardinality; dependent-entity format/cardinality. Unchanged inherited Properties reuse their original Declaration; explicit MODEL overrides select their local replacement. CFEL entities retain a Claim and may have Semantics.
- **Use Role and Form.** Rename Content Role to Role and the Role-specific Type to Form. These names express different purposes. Naming Methods prefer words that convey the actual distinction and reuse canonical expressions consistently; they do not impose a blanket word ban on useful contextual uses of `content`, `entity` or `type`.
- **Use two root kinds.** MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE are Primary Node kinds declared in CAPRMEDIO's self-describing MODEL. Their instance roots are `MODEL//CAPRMEDIO`, `PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO`, and the corresponding consumer Project roots. The consumer MODEL is optional. PROJECT STRUCTURE describes Scope Structure, Aspects and other declared components. Core Meta-Model contains the Atoms defining CAPRMEDIO's MODEL. Extensible axis configuration stays deferred.
- **Declare Scope outside the constrained Unit.** State permitted active/passive Subjects and Relation endpoints/cardinalities. ENGINE's proposed Scope permits allowed instances and implementation RMED; model definitions use their declared model-defining Scope. A local MODEL does not automatically widen ENGINE's Scope. Target Scope never grants wider authority.
- **Keep graph meanings distinct.** `/` narrows Primary Nodes with inheritance, `//` names their instances, `.` addresses Properties, `+>`/`<+` expresses composition, and `>|`/`|<` expresses classification. Composition uses canonical IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS; Container has yes/no value cases. `(Node, Node/**, .**)` includes the root, its recursive narrower branch and their recursive Properties. `@` references an existing target, parentheses group, and `in (...)` states membership. `:` denotes an allowed value, `=` tests, and `==` establishes a required/derived conclusion. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, as in `Atom/(.Role := Method)`. It does not write an instance value or exclude other allowed values from Atom.Role. Formal Claims keep `:` and `=` separate. Full Formal Claims stay out of Subjects; `..` and an invented `::` meaning are excluded.
- **Keep both counts.** Relation cardinality constrains both written directions; reversal swaps the counts. Property syntax uses separate expressions for occurrence, direct values and immediate dependent names: `p{:occurrence count}; p: [value format]{:value count}; p.*[name format]{:child count}`. YAML and Markdown mappings preserve that distinction, including mixed section content and nested headings.
- **Derive Primary Node versus Property.** The Node branch permits zero or one IS_PROPERTY_OF bearer. Zero derives Primary Node and no direct value; one derives Property and forbids narrowing and instantiation. Property-bearing must be acyclic. HAS_VALUE binds a Property on an instance to a literal, such as CA-P-123.version = 1; literals do not become declared graph Nodes.
- **Inheritance supplies effective rules.** Narrower instances receive applicable Relation cardinalities and declared Property constraints. Do not redeclare an inherited Property or create a new Declaration merely for an inherited lookup. Each Node's single effective Declaration in the selected MODEL resolves its Relation whitelist, endpoint constraints and counts. MODEL inheritance may replace any inherited rule through an explicit local override; unchanged Declarations are reused. Inheritance neither copies instance facts nor gives a Property a second bearer.
- **Operations use siblings and explicit composition.** Workflow, Step, Substep and Action narrow Operations. Each Workflow has one or more Steps, each Step one Workflow. A Step exclusively runs one Action or contains one or more Substeps. Each Substep has one Step and runs one Action. Actions may have zero or more callers. RUN bindings do not establish execution evidence.
- **Store authored instance Relations once.** Rename Subject links to active/passive; store modeled authored Node-instance links under `relations`, with typed containment references. Derive HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT from the dedicated Subject field and derive inverse views. The exact Assignee/Target reference migration remains open.

Relation Definitions now state allowed Host/Target signatures and reuse `Direct ((HAS_INVERSE)) Derived`. Inverse views have no separate Definition Atom. Repeated migration commentary is removed from the governing Drafts.

### Why these changes

The human rationale is to remove words that add no useful distinction, keep each complete expression precise, and avoid defining inherited material repeatedly. Primary Nodes, Properties, narrowing, composition and classification need different meanings so the graph can express constraints faithfully. A formal Scope outside its Unit makes the Unit's permitted authority explicit. One Declaration gathers a Node's structure and permissions; formal rules support graph reconstruction without turning an address into a second programming language. Syntax explanations remain useful where symbols are not self-explanatory.

### MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE — latest architecture

The two kinds are declared in MODEL//CAPRMEDIO itself. The named Subject roots are their instances:

```text
MODEL//CAPRMEDIO
PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects

MODEL//<PROJECT NAME>              (optional)
PROJECT STRUCTURE//<PROJECT NAME>
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects
```

The Project name above is a placeholder. A Project uses MODEL//CAPRMEDIO. It may define a local MODEL. A local MODEL inherits MODEL//CAPRMEDIO and may override any inherited rule. No inherited rule requires an overridable marker.

One Current authoritative Declaration per Node means one effective Declaration within the selected MODEL. Unchanged inherited Declarations are reused. A local replacement and its base source can coexist without becoming two effective owners in that MODEL. This selection context is distinct from the Project-wide instance context used by UNIQUE.

Core Meta-Model is a Scope Unit in CAPRMEDIO's Scope Structure. It contains the governing Atoms defining MODEL//CAPRMEDIO, including the two root kinds. This self-description does not identify the MODEL instance with its Scope Unit or PROJECT STRUCTURE instance. Existing ordered Scope Unit proposals remain subject to exact registration and mapping.

Model inheritance connects MODEL instances. It is separate from `/` Node narrowing and `<+` containment. The inheritance Relation name and exact Model-selection/override binding still need specification; this pass adds no invented notation or runtime behavior.

This replaces the earlier owner-wrapper layout and the MODEL-versus-PROJECT root split. The rationale is to distinguish reusable declarations from each Project's actual structure, reuse inherited material, and let each local MODEL control all of its effective rules.

## Summary

Register depends_on and required_by relation pair

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//depends_on ((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//required_by;

Relation//depends_on ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct;

# instances
$dependent ((depends_on)) $prerequisite
```

### Prose Claim

#### Claim scope
the `depends_on` **and** `required_by` relation pair.

`depends_on` **means** a direct dependency-ordering relation from a dependent Artifact **to** its prerequisite Artifact, with `required_by` as its inverse-derived view. Plan start dependencies use the Plan Graph's `BLOCKS` under CA-R-1580 instead; this Relation Kind **must not** duplicate that scheduling fact.

Both endpoints are Artifacts: the Host is dependent and the Target is its prerequisite.
Forward `Host ((depends_on)) Target` and reverse `Target <((depends_on)) Host` are views of the same Relation fact.
depends_on relates dependent Artifact to prerequisite Artifact.

## Summary

Reject authored inverse relations

## Claim

### Prose Claim


authored inverse typed relations.


validators **must** reject **every** inverse typed relation authored **in** an Atom Carrier.

## Details

Inverse means the derived direction declared by the governing Relation Kind definition, not a direction guessed from its name. In the containment pair, IS_CONTAINED_BY is direct from child to parent and is the only permitted authoritative direction when Atom containment is authored; CONTAINS is the inverse and must not be separately authored. This clarification does not admit a new runtime relation key or waive endpoint Entity Definition constraints.

## Summary

Define Subject Path

## Claim

### Prose Claim


A canonical Subject path identifying a governed or dependency target.




The following interpretation is required when this governed concept is used:

A Subject Path is a full canonical expression identifying one thing or topic addressed by GOVERNS or DEPENDS_ON. Entity is the canonical expression root under CA-R-2462; this Definition does not enumerate a closed root-branch set. A source path retains the declared operators and full qualification; a short display label is not another identity or alias.

The target is selected by the meaning addressed, not by the Atom's Local Scope Unit, Content Role, folder or Carrier. The path names a target; it is not itself the Subject Relation. A defining Atom may introduce that target, so format checks do not require prior target existence.

## Semantics

A path may address classification without declaring an Entity kind. `Atom.Header.Role` addresses the relative Property, while `Atom/(.Header.Role: Plan)` identifies a qualified Atom inheriting applicable Atom features and constraints. Neither form invents an intermediate Entity kind. The root and operators follow the adopted Entity syntax under CA-R-1931; no Project-name namespace layer is introduced.

## Summary

Keep relation vocabularies graph-specific

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Relation Types, their shared Project identities, and any applicable Entity Definition constraints in CAPRMEDIO Graphs.


Relation Type names are shared across CAPRMEDIO Graphs and unique within the Project. A Relation Type is not owned by a graph kind. Existing Entity Definition constraints, where applicable, supply graph-specific endpoint classes, endpoint graph contexts, cardinality, permissions, and prohibitions for that shared Type. They do not create graph-owned Type copies or impose a new per-Type/per-graph admission registry; this contract chooses neither default allow nor default deny.
