## Summary

Use distinct graph notation for Node relations

## Claim

### Prose Claim

In Subject addresses and Formal Claims, `X/Y` selects a narrower declared kind and `X//Name` an instance of a declared kind. A Property cannot narrow; it can have instances borne by corresponding data bearers. `X.p` addresses a Property borne by X; an unchanged inherited Property is resolved to its existing declaration rather than redeclared or given another bearer. In Subject addresses and filtered Node expressions in Formal Claims, `X/(.p := V)` admits V as a Property value and selects the whole Primary Node X where p equals V. The case does not exclude other allowed values from X.p. `(Node, Node.**)` selects Node and its recursive dependent Properties; it is not a narrowing assertion. Shared Node rules are declared once and inherited by applicable narrower Nodes.

`Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one composition fact, not narrowing. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite views of one classification fact. `:` marks an allowed value. `=` tests a condition; `==` sets a value. Parentheses group expressions; `in (a, b)` expresses membership. A bare Entity name refers to the existing target without copying or reparenting it.

For `Source {:left}((NAME)){:right} Target`, each optional bound constrains Relation instances at its written endpoint. Reversing the written view swaps the bounds. A Node-specific Claim addresses its active Node and its own bound; a Relation Declaration can state both intrinsic endpoint bounds. The opposite view requires its own applicable permission; a reverse written view does not grant permission. `{:n}` states an allowed cardinality. The same notation can constrain Properties, instances and Relations. Repeated references in a rule, including its conditions and conclusions, bind the same selected member. An omitted named Property occurrence cardinality does not require presence; applicable value constraints determine presence. Other omitted cardinalities are undefined, not implicit zero or permission.

`(Node, Node.**)` selects model Entities in the Node branch; it does not limit other declared Entities. `(Node//, (Node//).**)` is the instance-layer selector. `Node//` selects Node instances including instances of narrower kinds. `(Node//).**` selects recursive Property instances borne by a Node instance. Each is an instance of its corresponding model Property and has no independent Carrier. The two layers have separate permissions. Repeated instance matches count once by identity.

Subjects remain addresses and do not contain complete Formal Claims. In Subjects and filtered Node expressions in Formal Claims, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, including `Atom/(.Header.Role := Method)` and `Workflow/(.Purpose := Runtime)`; it does not write an instance value. Outside these selections, `:` and `=` retain their separate allowed-value and condition meanings. The withdrawn `..` form is not adopted; `::` has no assigned meaning here.

## Dependent selection

- `x.*`: immediate dependents.
- `x.**`: all dependents recursively.

A Property's full path determines its identity. Sibling names must be unique.

## Expression lists

Separate complete expressions with `;`. A line break is layout. Boolean groups remain one expression.

## RMED

RMED names these Roles:

- Requirement.
- Method.
- Evaluation.
- Delivery.

## Formal content

A Formal Claim is a declared child of an ordinary RMED Claim and contains formal content in a fenced block labelled CFEL. Formal content in an ordinary RMED Claim belongs in Formal Claim. Prose Claim contains ordinary Markdown. A heading in a Markdown value does not declare a Property by itself. Unknown headings, including `##` headings, within Prose Claim remain part of that value and do not terminate it.

## Inherited Node selection

- `Node.**` selects recursive dependent Properties.
- `(Node//).**` selects their occurrences on a Node instance.
- Node rules are inherited by applicable narrower Nodes.
- Commas combine selectors within one expression.
- Semicolons separate expressions.

## Summary

Separate Property names and values

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- `p{:occurrence}` constrains occurrences of the named Property.
- `p{:occurrence}: [value format]{:value count}` constrains its direct values.
- `p.*[name format]{:child count}` constrains immediate dependent names.
- `p.**[name format]{:recursive count}` constrains recursive dependent names
  across every descendant depth.
- `p.*[name format]{:child count}: [value format]{:value count}` also
  constrains each selected immediate dependent Property's direct values.
- The name count and value count are different counts. Separate complete
  expressions use `;`.

Property selectors compose from left to right:
- `p.*.*` selects Properties exactly two levels below p.
- `p.*.**` selects Properties two or more levels below p.

Names are unique within one bearer. `x.y.z` differs from `x.z`. Resolve local
declarations first and inherited declarations next. If neither declares
dependents for p, the effective immediate-child constraint is `p.*[]{:0}`:
undeclared dependent entities are forbidden. An explicit applicable child-name
selector, including an explicit wildcard selector, is the stated exception;
it permits only the names and counts that it declares.

Each applicable named Property occurs at most once per corresponding bearer. A leaf with a positive applicable value minimum is required; a zero minimum by itself does not require presence. Explicit occurrence and other applicable constraints still apply. A present Property has a value; nonempty child structure can provide a structural parent value when direct-value count is zero. `p: {:0..1}` specifies direct-value count while using the applicable inherited format. Missing direct-value, Format, and other count annotations remain unspecified. For `p.**`, the recursive count aggregates the selected
distinct descendant Property identities below p within each selected bearer.
It counts each selected descendant once regardless of depth; it neither counts
direct values nor combines descendants from different bearers. Sibling names
remain unique within that bearer.

## Details

```CFEL
# model
Atom.Content.**[string]{:0+}: [markdown]{:1}
```

## Summary

Define Property bearing and its inverse

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
$property ((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) $bearer;

Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF ((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//HAS_PROPERTY;

alias(Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF) == ".";

Relation//IS_PROPERTY_OF ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

IS_PROPERTY_OF directs a Property to exactly one immediate bearer. HAS_PROPERTY is its derived inverse. The bearer relation is acyclic. `Bearer.Property` addresses the Property.

A Property has exactly one immediate bearer; the bearer may be any applicable declared model Entity or instance.

Forward `Host ((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Target` and reverse `Target <((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Host` are views of the same Relation fact.
In `X.Y`, Y IS_PROPERTY_OF X; traversal runs from bearer to Property.
IS_PROPERTY_OF relates Property to immediate bearer.

## Summary

Bind direct Property values on instances

## Claim

### Prose Claim


HAS_VALUE binds a Property on an instance to its admitted literal value. For example, the version Property of Atom instance CA-P-123 has value 1. The Property declaration supplies its value format, admitted domain and cardinality; the literal 1 is not a separately declared graph Node and requires no Declaration Atom.

HAS_VALUE is a value binding rather than an ordinary Node-to-Node graph Relation. It must not create graph endpoints or independently authored inverse facts for literals. A Primary Node has no direct value. A Property instance may hold direct values where its effective declaration permits them, including inherited Property declarations. A Property occurrence on an instance is an instance of its effective declared Property and is borne by its data bearer. The declaration remains borne by its original model bearer. HAS_VALUE binds its admitted literal values and does not create an independent Carrier or graph endpoint for a value.

## Summary

Separate the CAPRMEDIO model from Project structure

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Aspects <+ Product
```

### Prose Claim


CAPRMEDIO's PROJECT STRUCTURE has:

- Scope Structure.
- Aspect instances, including Product.
- Other declared components.


Its Scope Structure retains the proposed ordered Units:

1. META_MODEL.
2. ENGINE.
3. CORE EXTENSIONS.
4. DOCUMENTATION.

Its Core Meta-Model Unit contains the Atoms defining MODEL//CAPRMEDIO, including the Declarations for MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE. The MODEL and its defining Scope Unit have separate identities.

Each constrained Unit's formal Scope is declared outside that Unit. It states permitted active and passive Subjects, Relations, endpoints and cardinalities.

CAPRMEDIO's PROJECT STRUCTURE records ENGINE's base formal Scope:

- Implementation RMED uses ENGINE's declared implementation Subjects.
- Instance creation follows that Scope's permissions.
- ENGINE references metamodel Declarations only through passive Subjects.
- Active metamodel definitions use the declared model-defining Scope.
- A local MODEL changes ENGINE's Scope only through an explicit Scope-contract replacement.

Declared Unit order governs this Scope Structure.

## Details

The two root kinds are MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE. Their CAPRMEDIO instance roots are MODEL//CAPRMEDIO and PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO. A consumer Project has its own PROJECT STRUCTURE instance root and may have a local MODEL instance root.

This Draft does not move directories. Exact instance registration and mapping from existing Scope Units remain adoption work. The earlier PROJECT//CAPRMEDIO Framework wrapper is superseded by the separate typed roots. CAPRMEDIO's actual Unit names are not universal values.

## Summary

Classify permission to have parts as Container

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Node >| Container: yes;

Node >| Container: no
```

### Prose Claim


Container is a classification whose admitted value cases are yes and no:


The yes case permits the Node to be the whole endpoint of CONTAINS, subject to its effective Relation whitelist and cardinalities. It does not by itself require a part. The no case forbids that endpoint role. Whether a part may belong to a whole is distinct from whether that part may itself have parts.

Use `Node// >| Container = yes` when selecting eligible whole instances. Container is not a required Boolean Property authored on every instance. This Draft does not assign an implicit default or require a classification annotation for every Node.

## Details

The Operator chose IS_CONTAINED_BY / CONTAINS and Container: yes/no. Current CA-R-1945@13 distinguishes permission from a requirement to have children; retain that distinction while replacing the old Atom.Enabled Relations.Contains Property representation. Its default-False mechanism is not silently imported into the new general classification. Explicit CONTAINS cardinalities can require parts for a particular Node, such as Workflow.

## Summary

Define HAS_INVERSE

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//$relation ((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//$relation_2;

alias(Relation//HAS_INVERSE) == "<-->";

Relation//HAS_INVERSE ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

HAS_INVERSE binds a direct graph Relation to its derived inverse graph Relation. The Host is Direct and the Target is Derived. The inverse swaps Host and Target for each admitted direct fact. The two Relation identities remain distinct. The direct Declaration owns the shared meaning, endpoint signature, endpoint conditions and this binding; the derived Declaration supplies the reverse written counterpart binding and its own lexical alias when one exists. A bound inverse is inferred from the direct fact and is not authored separately. The inferred IS_DERIVED_RELATION_OF metadata is not repeated in the minimal derived Declaration. A qualified derived counterpart requires its qualification at the direct Declaration and is not an unconditional inverse.

`<-->` is the Subject notation alias for this binding. ## Summary

Define CFEL

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p{:occurrence}:: [value format]{:value count};

p.*[name format]{:immediate name count};

p.**[name format]{:recursive name count};

p.*[name format]{:immediate name count}:: [value format]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

CFEL (CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language) is the formal notation for
Subject addresses and fenced Formal Claims. CFEL is a model component beside
Graph and Carrier: Graph contains Nodes and Relations; CFEL addresses and
constrains them. CFEL syntax neither creates a Node, Relation, Property,
Carrier fact, Workflow step, nor evaluator result.

An `IF` membership condition can bind an unbound variable to each matching member of its declared selection; a variable already bound in the surrounding scope is tested against membership without rebinding. A parenthesized multi-line `THEN` body uses the same binding in each complete expression. This does not introduce a `FOR` primitive.

In a Formal Claim, `#model` and `#instances` are ordering comments for the model and instance expressions that follow; they do not assert graph facts. A `$variable` explicitly binds an anonymous selected Entity or instance; repeated occurrences in its scope select the same identity. A typed selector supplies its universe; use model variables where model entities are intended. These bindings introduce no new binding operator.

CFEL uses these graph-address forms:

- `X/Y` selects a narrower Primary Node; `X//Name` selects an existing
  instance of a declared kind, including a Property instance borne by its data bearer.
- `X.p` addresses Property p borne by X. A Subject selection may appear in an address or inside a filtered Node
  expression in a Formal Claim: `X/(.p := V)` combines an admitted Property
  value with selection of X. `:=` belongs to this Subject-selection syntax; it
  is not a free-standing Formal-Claim value assignment.
- `Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite written views of one
  containment fact. `X >| Axis` and `Axis |< X` are opposite written views
  of one classification fact. A bare qualified address references its declared entity or instance. No `@` reference operator is required; `@N` identity/version tags retain their separate meaning.
- Parentheses group one expression. `;` separates complete expressions;
  a line break has no conjunction or disjunction meaning.

Text values use double quotes when needed to distinguish literal text from CFEL syntax; otherwise an unambiguous value may remain bare, including a multiword value such as `Scope Contract`. For example, `"A/B"` is text containing a slash. A name or path used as a reference retains its declared identity; a text value does not become a model reference. Within double-quoted text, `\"` represents a literal double quote and `\\` represents a literal backslash. Reject every other escape and any incomplete trailing backslash; JSON escape rules are not imported. This applies to values in Formal Claims and Subject selectors.

In Formal Claims, `X: Y` admits Y as an allowed value of X regardless of X's
kind or preceding path; it is not assignment. `=` and `!=` test conditions,
and `==` states a required or derived conclusion. `in` and `not in` are the
admitted membership tests. Numeric comparison and addition use the separately
defined `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` and `+`; they are distinct from Relation
operators. Property occurrence, direct-value, immediate-name
and recursive-name counts are distinct:

`{:n}`, `{:n+}` and `{:n..m}` state allowed cardinality bounds on their
qualified selection; `{=n}` tests a count condition, `{>n}` tests whether the
actual count is greater than n using the existing numeric `>`, and `{==n}`
concludes a required or derived count. These test/conclusion forms are not
allowed bounds. A Relation has independent outgoing and
reverse cardinalities: `Source {:forward}((RELATION)){:reverse} Target`.
A named Property has at most one occurrence per corresponding bearer; its applicable value constraints determine whether it is required. A present Property has a value, including nonempty child structure for a structural parent. `p: {:0..1}` specifies a direct-value count with its applicable inherited format. Other omitted annotations are unspecified, not zero. `[format]` applies to direct
values; a name selector is not a value selector. A `p.**` count aggregates
selected distinct descendant Property identities below p within each selected
bearer, independently of direct values and other bearers.

The named constructs `IF`/`THEN`, `UNIQUE`, `DETERMINES`, `COUNT`, `MAX`,
and `FENCED_LABELS` are admitted with the semantics in their own CFEL Rules.
`LOOKUP(R, q)` and `?==` are admitted CFEL operators with their own operator
Declarations; the `?==` ordered-assignment Rule supplies its chain semantics.
Boolean `AND` and `OR` combine conditions; parenthesize mixed AND/OR
expressions to state their grouping explicitly. `>>` is delivery notation with the
semantics of the delivery Rule; `!(selectors)` excludes branches from a
delivery selection. `Kind//$x` binds an existing selected instance and `$x.p`
reads its Property. Each non-graph CFEL operator has its own Declaration;
an operator is not a binary Node Relation. A Requirement/Declaration describes
a canonical or derived Relation direction; it does not authorize a second
stored inverse fact.

The reusable metadata family `Operator//Name == "notation literal"` binds a
declared operator descriptor to its token or bounded construct spelling. Its
quoted right side is metadata, not an executed CFEL expression, value assignment,
state creation, or a new model entity.

A direct Relation Declaration owns shared meaning and endpoints. A derived inverse Declaration retains the reverse HAS_INVERSE binding and its own alias, when present. A qualified or other non-inverse derived view retains its source, endpoint transformation and qualification; derivation alone does not imply unconditional endpoint reversal. `alias(Relation//NAME) == "token"` binds exact Relation names to lexical notation. `Relation//DIRECT <--> Relation//DERIVED` binds distinct inverse Relations in the direct Declaration. It never equates their identities. These metadata forms do not create literal-to-Node graph links.

A graph Relation connects declared model entities or declared instances,
including Carrier and CFEL; it is not limited to `Node/**`. A literal remains a
Property or allowed value, not a graph endpoint. A non-graph CFEL operator is
not itself a graph Relation, but its declared operator descriptor is a model
entity that may be a graph endpoint; an operator glyph or literal operand does
not create another model entity. Each direct Relation Declaration supplies shared meaning and a
formal Host/Target signature with typed selectors whose universe is known, or
with declared variables bound to that universe. Within a Relation Declaration
Formal Claim only, `$host ((RELATION)) $target` is the reusable generic
signature: its untyped variables range over that declared entity-or-instance
universe and exclude literals. It declares neither a Relation fact nor instance
data. Known endpoint kinds remain typed selectors. This generic Relation signature binding applies within Relation Declarations; typed bindings can also select model entities where their universe is declared.

Concrete directional alternatives describe the same canonical Relation fact:
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` and
`Workflow <((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Step`. The bare forward form
`Step ((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) Workflow` remains valid. In reverse writing,
normalization swaps canonical Source/Target and the two written endpoint count
slots. This syntax does not grant an inverse Relation permission. The Relation Declaration states the Host, Target and applicable counterpart direction. `HAS_INVERSE` applies to inverse Relations; a qualified non-inverse derived view retains its source, transformation and qualification.

In RMED Claims, all formal content is a fenced block labelled `CFEL`. CFEL
body syntax and Markdown-fence-label parsing are separate concerns. This Definition
describes the admitted language contract; it does not claim a complete parser
or evaluator. An unimplemented construct remains an adoption and conformance
gap, not evidence that the construct has different semantics.

This Definition does not convert a Format, Bool value, or any other value
into an instance selected by `//`. Such an instance selection requires the
existing source binding that declares it. No value-format-to-instance rewrite
is implied by the CFEL overview.

`Relation//IS_DECLARED_BY` is the qualified derived view of a GOVERNS fact whose source is a Requirement/Form Declaration; it reverses that selected fact while retaining the qualification. It is not a general inverse of GOVERNS or a permission for every Relation.

## Summary

Compare and add numeric values in CFEL

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- `x > y`: x is greater than y.
- `x >= y`: x is greater than or equal to y.
- `x < y`: x is less than y.
- `x <= y`: x is less than or equal to y.
- `x + y` returns the numeric sum of two numeric operands. If both operands are integers, the result is an exact integer.
- Each operand resolves to one numeric value. No string coercion is allowed.
- Evaluate `+` before `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<` and `<=`. Parentheses override this order.
- `=` tests equality, including in a Claim invariant; it does not assign a value.
- A missing or multi-valued operand makes an evaluated comparison invalid.
- Guard optional Properties by their occurrence before comparing their values.
- A comparison in Claim must hold. In an IF condition, it tests the values.
- An IF conclusion is evaluated only when its condition holds.
- A Declaration applies the comparison to each matching instance.
- Comparisons do not assign values or change occurrence counts.
- `+>`, `<+`, `>|` and `|<` remain distinct Relation operators.

## Details

```CFEL
# model
Atom.Header.Version >= 1;

Atom.Header.Tier >= -1;

# instances
Atom/(.Header.Role: Plan)//$atom;

IF ($atom.Header.Work Sequence Number{=1})
THEN ($atom.Header.Work Sequence Number > 0);
```

Without a condition, evaluate the complete selected population regardless of Status Group or containment, including selected Drafts and Archived instances. An incomplete or unresolved population is an error. A known empty population satisfies uniqueness.
- Evaluate a condition on each candidate instance before resolving tuple Properties. Relative Properties bind to that same instance. False excludes it; unresolved, invalid or ambiguous conditions are errors. Use the existing Boolean grouping and AND/OR syntax.

- Two distinct selected logical instances must not have equal value tuples. Repeated references or Carrier representations of the same logical instance do not create additional instances. Do not infer that two instances are one merely because their key tuples match.

- Optional Properties require an explicitly resolved subset whose members carry the required values; do not silently skip missing rows.

---
## Summary

Bind instance variables

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- `Kind//` selects existing instances of Kind and its narrower kinds.
- `Kind//{:n}` applies the existing cardinality to the selected logical instances within the Project context, except for the per-bearer Property selection below. Resolve the complete selection and count each instance once across repeated references or Carrier representations. An unresolved population is an error.
- For `Node.**//`, `{:n}`, `{:n+}` and `{:n..m}` count instances separately for each effective applicable model Property and actual corresponding bearer instance. CA-R-2462 uses `{:0..1}`.
- Each instance is `INSTANCE_OF` its model Property and `IS_PROPERTY_OF` its data bearer. The rule also applies when that bearer is a Property instance. Inherited Properties retain their original schema identity and model bearer. Mismatched pairs are invalid; unresolved applicability or population is an error. These constraints do not create Cartesian links.
- A leaf with a positive direct-value minimum requires an instance; zero alone does not require one. Explicit occurrence and other constraints still apply. A present Property has a value; for a structural parent, nonempty child structure can be that value even when its direct-value count is zero.
- `Kind//$x` ranges over the selected instances. Each non-aggregate per-binding constraint must hold for every matching binding. Repeated `$x` references in one Claim block identify the same instance within each binding; an enclosing aggregate retains its selected population.
- `in` and `not in` test an instance's identity against a selected instance set. `=` and `!=` compare bound instance references by identity; they do not test kind membership or broadcast a scalar comparison over a set.
- `Kind//$x.p` selects and binds an instance and reads its Property `p`. `$x.p` reads that same bound instance's Property.
- In an IF condition, `Kind//$c ((R)) Kind//$p` tests a link that already exists, including a legitimately derived inverse. It is not an endpoint signature and does not create a link.
- Evaluate the condition for candidate bindings. Its THEN conclusion applies only to bindings for which that link exists; it does not require links between every candidate pair.
- Endpoint counts aggregate matching links per endpoint; they do not require a link between every pair of bindings.
- Binding selects existing instances. It does not create an instance named `$x` or assign a value imperatively. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target.

In one CFEL Formal Claim fence, the full-line comments `# model` and `# instances` distinguish MODEL constraints from instance constraints. When both are present, write `# model` first. These comments are not operators, Properties, or values. Named MODEL addresses such as `Relation//NAME` and `Operator//NAME` retain their declared identity; a Relation descriptor variable in the MODEL group does not make it a runtime instance constraint.

In the MODEL group, `IF $x in (selection) THEN (conclusion)` binds an unbound `$x` over the selected MODEL entities. If `$x` is already bound, the membership test filters that same binding. References to `$x` throughout the parenthesized conclusion use the same binding; the conclusion may contain nested conditions and semicolon-separated statements. This does not create a MODEL entity or introduce a FOR operator.

`KindSelection//$x` binds existing members of the selected logical instance population. The receiver may be a named Kind or a union Kind selection: `(in (Action, Workflow))//$selected` keeps the Action-or-Workflow population and binds its matching members. An existing filter follows the explicit binder without changing its matching population, as in `Event Record//$event_record(.object_output{=1}, .object_output.id = $projection.ID)`. In an aggregate such as `MAX(Event Record//$event_record(.object_output{=1}).happened_at)`, the argument remains the complete filtered population; inserting the binder does not turn the aggregate into one calculation per selected row.

`Kind//$x{:n}` constrains the count of the entire selected logical population in its Project context, not a count of one already-bound row. The existing `Kind//{:n}` population rule remains readable for historical sources, subject to the per-bearer Property selection above. Neither a binder nor a named reference creates an instance, Property, Relation fact or imperative assignment. Binding alone does not grant an inverse permission or change endpoint counts.

## Details

```CFEL
# instances
Kind//$x
```

This binds one existing selected instance.

## Summary

Require scalar Property immutability

## Claim

### Prose Claim


`IMMUTABLE(p)` requires the same valid scalar Property value for one logical bearer from the first point when the surrounding scope selects that Property onward.

- At first applicability, bind the one existing valid scalar value. Existing occurrence, Format and value-cardinality constraints still apply. Guard an optional Property before applying `IMMUTABLE`.
- Bind later versions to the same logical bearer using supplied lineage, not by matching the mutable Property value. A new Version or Carrier representation does not create a new bearer for this check.
- If an IF guard activates `IMMUTABLE`, the constraint remains active for that bearer after the first true condition, including when later versions no longer satisfy the guard.
- Use the first applicable value, not the latest observed value. Missing or invalid required values, unresolved bearer lineage, or incomplete history needed to establish the first applicable value are errors; none proves immutability.
- After activation, every later version of that bearer must still provide exactly one valid scalar value matching the bound value. A later false guard or removal of an optional Property does not suspend the constraint. Compare using the declared scalar Format, without implicit normalization or coercion.

`IMMUTABLE` is a declarative invariant. It does not write, allocate or lock a value, or perform a Workflow step.

## Summary

Require functional dependencies between Property tuples

## Claim

### Prose Claim


`DETERMINES(selector, (.key, ...), (.dependent, ...))` requires equal ordered key tuples to have equal ordered dependent tuples. An optional fourth argument, `condition`, restricts the state population: `DETERMINES(selector, (.key, ...), (.dependent, ...), condition)`.

- Use one explicit Project evaluation context. Resolve the complete relevant state history selected by Kind, including versions and rebuild states, rather than only the latest Current snapshot.
- The context supplies the historical population, Property-value resolution and declared reference-identity bindings. These are evaluation inputs, not new Artifact fields.
- Evaluate an optional condition separately on each candidate historical state before resolving tuple Properties. Relative or selected-Kind Property references in that condition bind to that same state. A false condition excludes the state. An unresolved, invalid or ambiguous condition is an error. Without a condition, use all selected states. Do not select by only the latest state and then include its excluded historical states.
- Bind every tuple Property to the same selected state. Each must resolve to exactly one valid scalar value. Missing, invalid or multiple values are errors; do not skip rows.
- Compare tuple positions in order. Compare scalar values using their declared Format without implicit normalization or coercion. A declared reference compares by its resolved target identity. Missing or ambiguous reference bindings are errors; raw text or Carrier locators are not fallback identities.
- For every pair of selected states, equal keys require equal dependents. Repeated keys with equal dependents are allowed. Different keys may have equal dependents.
- An unresolved or incomplete required history is an error. A known complete empty selection satisfies the constraint.

`DETERMINES` does not assert key uniqueness, merge instances, allocate IDs, freeze inputs, assign values or execute a Workflow.

## Summary

Select fenced Markdown labels

## Claim

### Prose Claim


`FENCED_LABELS(p)` selects one label per fenced code-block occurrence in one scalar Markdown value.

- Evaluate p separately for each matching bearer. Do not pool values across Atoms.
- Use the complete recursive Markdown block parse. Exclude indented code blocks.
- Preserve duplicate labels as separate occurrences. An unlabelled fence contributes an empty label.
- `FENCED_LABELS(p): [format]{:n}` requires every selected label to match the Format. The count constrains selected occurrences, including duplicates.
- The finite literal Format `[in (CFEL)]` matches only CFEL. An empty selection satisfies the Format condition but must still satisfy the count.
- Bind parsed labels through the governing Markdown Format and the existing CFEL-labelled-fence rule. No whole-info-string, token or case-normalization policy is added here.
- Missing or multiple Markdown values, incomplete parsing and unresolved or ambiguous label bindings are evaluation errors. Never replace them with an empty selection.

Selection reads Markdown value structure, not Graph Nodes or dependent Properties. CFEL body syntax is validated separately.

## Summary

Filter instances and select maximum values

## Claim

### Prose Claim


`Kind//(c1, ...).p` selects p from matching instances of Kind and its narrower kinds in one explicit current-Project instance snapshot.

- Relative filter paths bind the same candidate instance. Outer variables retain their enclosing bindings; an unbound or ambiguous variable is an error.
- Every filter condition must hold. Commas inside filter parentheses mean AND. Outside them, selector commas retain their existing union meaning. Existing AND, OR and grouping remain available. Filter conditions and AND groups evaluate left-to-right with short-circuiting: a later field read is evaluated only after its earlier guard holds.
- A missing, invalid or unresolved evaluated filter is an error, not false. Short-circuiting excludes only an unevaluated later condition; it never turns an evaluated invalid value into a skipped record. Reference comparisons use resolved target identity, not raw identifiers or Carrier data.
- Each matching instance contributes exactly one valid scalar p. Selection does not implicitly expand lifecycle history.
- `MAX(selection)` returns the greatest selected scalar under its Format-defined ordering. Numeric and datetime values are orderable. Compare datetimes as instants, not lexical strings.
- Empty, incomplete, incompatible or non-orderable selections are errors.
- Equal greatest values return that scalar value. MAX does not select a record row.

Both operations are read-only. They create no record, Property, Relation, value or lifecycle transition.

## Summary

Record business Property changes in one update Event Record

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Event Records with action create or update describe accepted, completed business creations or updates. No-op, failed, unaccepted, archive and Carrier-only events do not use these actions.

One accepted business update has one update Event Record.

- Its change delta contains only changed logical Properties.
- Atom.Content and all its descendants are excluded from Event Records for now.
- Each recorded change identifies the Property by its complete path and records its old and new value or absence.
- Promotion is an update; Version and Status are included when they change.
- Updated At may be included when changed. Its new value follows the maximum of happened_at over accepted create and update Event Records for that object through this record’s happened_at.
- This recorded copy is audit evidence. It does not supply that maximum or constitute another business update.
- Carrier filename and directory changes are excluded from the delta.
- A Carrier-only rename or move creates no update Event Record.

## Summary

Distinguish event time from record insertion time

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- Event Record.happened_at is the time the recorded event happened.
- Event Record.inserted_at is the time the record was added to its Journal.
- Delayed insertion does not replace happened_at with inserted_at.

## Summary

Capture Atom input and output metadata

## Claim

### Prose Claim


An Event Record for Atom creation or update has object_output. An update record also has object_input; creation input is optional.

For each present Atom input or output, the Event Record captures:

- Atom.Header.ID.
- Atom.Header.Version.
- Atom.Header.Updated At.

object_input contains the values before the change. object_output contains the values after it. Their IDs may differ. The captured values remain as recorded.

Define HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR

```CFEL
# model
Relation//HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR ((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//IS_EVENT_AUTHOR_OF;

HAS_EVENT_AUTHOR relates Event Record instance to Actor instance.

## Summary

Capture Projection input and output metadata

## Claim

### Prose Claim


An Event Record for Projection creation or update has object_output. An update record also has object_input; creation input is optional.

For each present Projection input or output, the Event Record captures:

- Projection.ID.
- Projection.Updated At.

object_input contains the values before the change. object_output contains the values after it. Neither side contains a Version. The captured values remain as recorded.

## Summary

Count direct Property values and distinct values

## Claim

### Prose Claim


- Within `COUNT(...)`, `p: $` selects the direct value occurrences of Property p on the current bearer. `$` is anonymous and binds no new named variable. It does not select dependent Property names.
- Repeated equal values remain separate occurrences. A known absent optional p selects an empty selection of value occurrences. An unresolved or malformed bearer, Property population, or value is an error, not an empty set.
- `COUNT(p: $)` returns the nonnegative number of selected direct value occurrences. `COUNT(DISTINCT p: $)` returns the number of their unique values.
- DISTINCT equality is the declared Format equality: no implicit string trimming, case folding, coercion, or canonicalization. A reference Format compares resolved reference identity.
- Counts apply per current bearer, not across Atoms. Existing Property occurrence, value-format, value-count, and source constraints remain in force.
- Outside this COUNT selection, existing `p: literal` and `p: [format]{:n}` meanings are unchanged.

## Details

```CFEL
# instances
Atom//$atom;

COUNT($atom.Header.Subjects.Passive: $) = COUNT(DISTINCT $atom.Header.Subjects.Passive: $)
```

## Summary

Apply default Relation cardinalities

## Claim

### Prose Claim

## Summary

Declare HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct;

# instances
Atom//$atom ((HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT)) $active_subject
```

### Prose Claim

HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT links an Atom to the declared model entity or instance named by its active Subject. This includes a Requirement/Form Declaration's target and is not restricted to the Node branch. Carrier entities, CFEL operator descriptors, graph Relation types and their declared instances are admitted when selected by the active Subject. Literal values and operator glyphs are not endpoints.

The Host is an Atom and the Target is the entity or instance resolved from its dedicated active Subject field. The field's source supplies the canonical HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT fact; obtaining that value from the field does not make this Relation a derived view of another Relation. An unresolved Subject remains a diagnostic, not an empty or automatically valid target population.

Forward `Host ((HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT)) Target` and reverse `Target <((HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT)) Host` are written views of the same fact. Ownership cardinalities are supplied by their applicable rules; this endpoint signature does not itself create an ownership count.

## Summary

Require one Scope Unit Declaration

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Each Scope Unit, including Project.


Every specific Scope Unit, including Project, has exactly one external Requirement Atom with Form `Scope Unit Declaration` and an active Subject naming that Scope Unit. The Declaration is the sole structural authority for its declared values.

The Declaration carries the Scope Unit Name, ordered state, optional Label, conditional order.number and direct containment. A non-root Scope Unit also has a stable ID. Project is unordered and has neither Scope Unit ID nor order.number. A non-root Scope Unit has one direct Parent; Project has none.

Authority and Delivery folder names are derived from the Declaration. `project_structure.toml` is not a governing source.

## Details

The Project Declaration is externally Operator-owned. The Operator is an Actor, not a Scope Unit.

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
Atom/(.Header.Role: Operations)/Workflow/(.Purpose := Runtime)

## Semantics

A Runtime Workflow is a Workflow whose Purpose is Runtime: it provides behavior through a Project's delivered result during its operation. In CAPRMEDIO, examples include Create Draft, Promote Draft and Archive Atom.

It inherits Workflow's shared Step, Substep and Action model. Purpose describes use relative to a Project and does not change the canonical definition's owning Scope Unit.

## Summary

Assign a default when an Object Property is absent

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p ?== expression
```

### Prose Claim



- `p ?== e1 ?== e2` is one ordered conditional-assignment chain. Keep p when it has an authored value; when p is absent, use the first available valid expression from left to right and set that missing Object Property value in the Model. An authored invalid value is an error, not absence. Omission is Property absence, not null, an empty string, zero or false.

- Expressions may be literals, same-bearer Property paths, explicit bound Property reads, or `LOOKUP(R, q)`. An explicit foreign-bearer read must resolve one target in the declared evaluation context; zero or multiple targets are errors.

- `LOOKUP(R, q)` is an admitted fallback expression; its value and traversal semantics are defined by the Operator//Lookup Declaration.

- Evaluate fallback expressions lazily from left to right; stop at the first valid available value. Later branches are not evaluated. Missing final values, evaluated fallback-expression cycles, and more than one applicable fallback chain are errors. Independent Declaration constraints still apply.

- The conditional assignment sets the missing Object Property value in the Model and the result must satisfy p’s declared value Format and cardinality, including required effective cardinality. It does not itself write a Carrier, persist a file, or create an authored Carrier occurrence; Carrier I/O remains the responsibility of an adapter or Delivery rule. Property-declaration inheritance is unchanged; recursive instance-value lookup occurs only through explicit LOOKUP.
## Details

```CFEL
# model
Atom.Header.Label ?== Atom.Header.Form
```

## Summary

Declare CFEL operator LOOKUP(R, q)

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Operator//Lookup == "LOOKUP(R, q)"
```

### Prose Claim

`LOOKUP(R, q)` is an existing contextual value expression admitted in a `?==` fallback expression. Starting at the bearer of target Property `p`, follow one existing outgoing link of declared Relation `R` at each step, in R's declared direction. Exclude the starting bearer. Return the nearest authored value of `q` that is applicable to that bearer. Resolve `q` by full Property declaration identity and effective MODEL applicability; skip only an inapplicable Property or an absent authored occurrence. At a known end with no applicable authored value, return absence. Do not match by bare name or invent a Property slot.

A present invalid value, unresolved applicability or graph fact, multiple outgoing targets, or revisiting a bearer is an error. Follow only the Relation direction named by R.

## Semantics

`Operator//Lookup` identifies the declared CFEL value-expression operator. The traversal semantics above are its complete existing contract.

## Summary

CFEL numeric range constraint

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
p:: [0..100]{:value count}
```

### Prose Claim

Inside a square-bracket value Format annotation, `lower..upper` is a closed numeric interval: both endpoints are included. It constrains each direct Property value and does not state Property occurrence or value cardinality. This square-bracket value constraint is distinct from the existing curly-brace cardinality range `{:n..m}`.

CFEL Format constraint intersection

### Formal Claim

```CFEL

A comma inside one square-bracket value Format annotation combines constraints by intersection. Each direct value must satisfy every listed constraint. Existing curly-brace occurrence and value-cardinality annotations keep their current meanings and remain independent.

replacement **or** absorption history.

## Summary

Apply relation direction within its ordering domain

## Claim

### Prose Claim


declared relations.


**every** declared relation **must** satisfy the target position **and** ordering domain registered for its relation family. Stored governing RMED relation occurrences selected by CA-R-2148@10 **must** use the numeric Tier-and-Scope ordering in CA-R-2149: a same-Scope target **must** have a strictly lower numeric Tier, a target in a strict ancestor Scope Unit is accepted without Tier comparison, the exact one-way Project Configuration-to-Core Meta-Model logical-role prerequisite declared by CA-R-1218@31 is accepted without Tier comparison, and every other descendant **or** sibling target is forbidden. Temporal relations **must** use lifecycle succession, realization relations **must** use realization order, dependency relations **must** use dependency order, **and** **every** other admitted domain **must** use its own registered order. a universal upstream **or** downstream rule **must not** be inferred across different ordering domains, **and** an inverse-derived view **must not** create another declared edge.

## Details

For selected governing RMED occurrences, CA-R-2149 uses the Project Scope Unit resolved from the active Subject of an Atom with Form Goal as its ordering context. Ordinary endpoints still use their Local Scope Unit.

## Summary

Identify Dependent-Entity Occurrences by Complete Subject Path

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Model Property occurrences selected by `Node.**`, their immediate bearers, and their complete Subject Paths.


**every** model Property occurrence selected by `Node.**` **must** derive its
source-admitted bearer-qualified identity from its complete Subject Path
**without** imposing one global ordinal position on a reusable Term. Its
outgoing direct IS_PROPERTY_OF Relation identifies its immediate bearer. Distinct
model Property occurrences **must** use distinct complete canonical names, while repeated
references **to** the same occurrence **must** retain its same complete canonical
name.

## Details

The complete Subject Path preserves source-admitted bearer qualification.
Ordinal position and display placement do not create entity identity.
Qualification is part of the complete property name used for collision checks.
A repeated display or reference of one model Property remains the same Property, and
parsing a name does not introduce another graph entity.

`Node.**` selects Properties of Node and its narrower branch. Property instances are distinct from their model Properties; the applicable Declarations govern their HAS_INSTANCE links.
`Term//Property` is its reusable lexical Term; the Term is not the
selector or an occurrence. The direct IS_PROPERTY_OF Relation runs from the
Property occurrence to its bearer. The separate bearer-cardinality Rule owns
the exactly-one constraint; this Rule owns only the complete-path identity.


The contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` distinguish their respective ID Properties; they are not alternative complete canonical Subject names or case-folded aliases. Authored Subjects use their full admitted expressions. `ID` is reusable and the terminal label need not be globally unique. Shared `Unit` components remain permitted in `Scope Unit` and `Code Unit`. This preserves complete-path identity without imposing disjoint lexical components or a new global ordinal position.

## Summary

Define IS_BORNE_BY

## Claim scope

an IS_BORNE_BY Relation from Entity A **to** Entity B **in** the Entities Graph.

## Claim

an IS_BORNE_BY Relation from Entity A **to** Entity B **in** the Entities Graph **means** that A is a Dependent Entity whose identity requires B as its immediate bearer.

### Formal claim

```text
Entity/Graph Syntax > Relation//IS_BORNE_BY
Entity/Graph Syntax > Relation//BEARS
```

## Semantics

Primary means that identity does not require another Entity occurrence as bearer. Dependent means that identity requires an immediate bearer, as expressed by IS_BORNE_BY. The proposed kind `Entity/Dependent Entity` classifies entities with that identity dependence; `Entity/Term//Dependent Entity` names its separate lexical Term. An absent edge in an incomplete view does not establish independence or remove source-established dependence.

The direct Relation is `X IS_BORNE_BY Y`, from the dependent entity X to its immediate bearer Y. The qualified path is `Y.X`, read from bearer to dependent. `Y BEARS X` is the derived inverse under CA-R-2416, not an additional independently stored fact. The canonical Relation name remains `IS_BORNE_BY`; the earlier conversational spellings do not create aliases. Generic prerequisite dependence does not establish bearer-qualified identity.

## Notation for subject

```text
.
```

## Details

This Draft incorporates the Operator-confirmed relational meaning and direct `Entity/Dependent Entity` kind. The kind and its separate lexical Method definition remain pending Draft dependencies, not Current admission. No Primary Entity branch is introduced.

### Withdrawn preparation — Property consolidation

The Operator approved IS_PROPERTY_OF and derived HAS_PROPERTY. New unallocated Relation Definition Drafts replace this proposed old-name successor; Current R1260 is not renamed or retired by this marker. The prior preparation is retained as historical review evidence. Do not promote this Draft as written or treat this marker as Current-source retirement.

## Summary

Keep Entity and Artifact Distinct

## Claim scope

the Artifact Term and an Entity instance represented in a Carrier.

## Claim

Artifact **must not** be equivalent **to** the Entity category. Artifact is a Term for an Entity instance represented in a Carrier; it does not create a separate Artifact Entity identity or a disjoint Entity kind.

## Semantics

An Entity instance may be referred to as an Artifact when it is represented in a Carrier such as a file, folder, or database row. The represented Entity instance remains the same Entity; the Artifact Term does not add another identity, branch, or classification axis.

## Summary

Classify Dependent Entity as an Entity

## Claim scope

the `Entity/Dependent Entity` kind and its relation to Entity.

## Claim

`Entity/Dependent Entity` **must** be NARROWER_THAN `Entity`.

## Details

`Entity/Dependent Entity` names an Entity kind; its `/` path expresses
specialization. `Entity/Term//Dependent Entity` names the reusable lexical
Term used to write that kind and other qualified entity names. The Term is not
the kind, and mentioning or parsing the Term does not introduce an Entity
occurrence.

An `Entity/Dependent Entity` occurrence has an immediate bearer identified by
an outgoing direct IS_BORNE_BY Relation to that bearer. This Rule classifies
the kind; the Relation Definition supplies relation meaning and the separate
bearer-cardinality Rule supplies the occurrence constraint.

## Summary

Define Type

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Type Properties and their use in qualified Entity kinds. A Type Property is
optional generally; an applicable governing rule may require it in its context.


Type is a single-valued Property when an Entity admits that Property. It can
be used for classification: `X/(.Type: Z)` identifies a kind narrower than X,
qualified by the Type Property and its admitted value Z. The Type Property
and a Property addressed directly by `X.Y` share the same Property meaning;
classification use does not introduce another Property category.

The applicable allowed-value set is finite at an Applicable Methodology
Revision and expandable through governed Methodology Sources. Admission and
requiredness remain scoped to the qualified Property context.

## Semantics

`X.Y` addresses Property Y. `X.Y: Z` expresses that Z is an allowed value of
that Property. `X/(.Y: Z)` qualifies a narrower kind of X by its own Property Y
and admitted value Z. The leading dot addresses X.Y relative to X; the
qualified X inherits X's applicable features and constraints. Y does not
become a narrower kind of X, and no intermediate X/Y kind is declared. Neither form assigns a
value to an existing instance merely by appearing in an expression.

Atom Form is represented by the YAML `form` key; Atom Role is represented by `role`. Legacy `type` and `content_role` are readable only under the transition rules in CA-D-657. These encodings do not create separate Property kinds.
For example, `Atom/(.Header.Role: Method)` concerns Atoms classified by Content
Role Method; Method is not used as a Type value in this example.

## Details

The latest Operator clarification supersedes the earlier interim statement
that Type is not a Property. Both addressed and classification uses are
Properties. The selected relative Property qualification preserves that
Property meaning without another Property category or qualification operator.

The reviewed CA-D-478@29 says qualified classifications are ordinary
metadata Properties and maps them to `content_role` and `type`. CA-D-657@1
governs the YAML Frontmatter field encodings, with each field also subject
to its applicable Property and Delivery authority. Preserve declared keys,
locations and canonical values; an admitted Property with an unsettled
encoding is a schema gap, not permission to guess. Do not derive a new
YAML structure from a display path. No new
Property kind, intermediate classification object, Carrier per field or
YAML-versus-frontmatter ontology is created. Generic grouping/continuation
syntax and parser effects are not established by this interpretation.

## Summary

Define Subject Expression

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Subject Expressions formed from entity names, reusable Term components, and registered relation syntax.




The following interpretation is required when this governed concept is used:

a Subject Expression **means** a reference **to** **`=1`** canonical Subject Target formed from entity names and registered relation syntax. A qualified Atom expression uses the admitted Role and Form Properties, for example `Atom/(.Header.Role := Plan)/(.Header.Form := Epic)` when both values are admitted.

Outside the Term branch, an Entity reference **must** use its exact complete canonical expression with every source-established qualifier; a bare Term is not that expression. The sole one-Term exception is the Subject root `Entity`. Ordinary lexical components **may** reuse Terms with consistent approved meanings; an instance's name is **not** automatically a lexical Term. Inside `((...))`, a registered direct Relation token resolves to **`=1`** admitted Relation Type under the named-Relation notation. Its bare spelling is not that Relation Type entity's complete canonical expression; naming comparison uses the full qualified expression separately. A qualified Atom expression such as `Atom/(.Header.Role := <exact Role>)/(.Header.Form := <exact Form>)` is available only when both exact values have independent source admission; its segments do not become admitted merely by appearing in an expression.

`/`, `//`, `.`, `::`, `+>`, `<+`, `>|`, `|<`, parentheses, the named-relation form `Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target`, **and** cardinality follow CA-R-1931 **and** CA-R-2487. `//` is one separator token between a kind **and** a named instance; its right operand is the instance's name, **not** an Atom ID. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target; Atom version tags retain their separate meaning. Parentheses provide logical grouping. `Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are containment, not inheritance or sequence. `X >| Y` and `Y |< X` express the same HAS_CLASSIFICATION fact with Entity Y used as an applicable Classification axis, not membership or a new Entity kind. Relation counts use `Source {::forward}((RELATION)){::reverse} Target`; direct values use `Property{::occurrence}:: [format]{::value count}`. Operators, grouping, relation delimiters, Formats, **and** cardinality are **not** Terms.

The complete expression **must** resolve **to** **`=1`** canonical Subject Target that already exists **or** is explicitly introduced by applicable defining authority under CA-R-1194 **and** CA-R-1931. Syntax alone neither creates **nor** admits a target **or** native EntityGraph fact. The expression identifies the target, **not** the Atom's Subject Relation **to** it. An arbitrary composite expression is **not** one Term **or** automatically one entity name; an admitted qualified property name **may** identify **`=1`** entity.

## Details

Subjects do not carry Atom or Artifact IDs, whether bare, version-qualified, or embedded in an ID selector. Use typed Relations for links to those Atoms or Artifacts. The contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` distinguish their respective ID Properties, not particular identifier values. They are not alternative complete canonical Subject names or case-folded aliases; an authored Subject uses its full admitted expression. Their shared terminal label and reusable `ID` meaning do not collide. Dot remains an operator; these contextual spellings are not renamed to `atom.atom_id` or another invented spelling. Named-instance Subjects use names, not IDs. Source/provenance metadata outside Subjects is not prohibited.

`//` selects a named instance of a primary kind, not an instance of a dependent property. A following `.` can select that instance's property, including `Selection//Projection and Journal Authority Sources.updated_at`. Source-established kind or bearer qualification participates in the complete canonical name. Distinct modeled entities require distinct complete qualified names, while repeated references retain the same identity and name. Local instance labels may coincide across different kinds when their complete qualified names differ. Local names remain unique per entity kind within the project's Current source view across owning Scope Units under CA-R-2476. This grammar adds neither case folding nor a name registry. When `//` is mandatory remains deferred.

`Entity/Object/Continuant/Package`, `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module`, and `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module <+ Code Unit` identify three connected entities. The chain is not one Term or a fourth entity. `Package`, `Module`, and `Code Unit` are their reusable lexical components, not their complete Entity expressions. Likewise, `Package` and `Unit` are reusable Terms whose occurrence does not itself introduce an entity or Relation. The rule applies to exact full expressions in authored prose as well as Subjects. Literal source quotations and code identifiers remain distinguishable and are not automatically renamed. ## Summary

Define Subject Expression

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Subject Expressions formed from entity names, reusable Term components, and registered relation syntax.




The following interpretation is required when this governed concept is used:

a Subject Expression **means** a reference **to** **`=1`** canonical Subject Target formed from entity names and registered relation syntax. A qualified Atom expression uses the admitted Role and Form Properties, for example `Atom/(.Header.Role := Plan)/(.Header.Form := Epic)` when both values are admitted.

Outside the Term branch, an Entity reference **must** use its exact complete canonical expression with every source-established qualifier; a bare Term is not that expression. The sole one-Term exception is the Subject root `Entity`. Ordinary lexical components **may** reuse Terms with consistent approved meanings; an instance's name is **not** automatically a lexical Term. Inside `((...))`, a registered direct Relation token resolves to **`=1`** admitted Relation Type under the named-Relation notation. Its bare spelling is not that Relation Type entity's complete canonical expression; naming comparison uses the full qualified expression separately. A qualified Atom expression such as `Atom/(.Header.Role := <exact Role>)/(.Header.Form := <exact Form>)` is available only when both exact values have independent source admission; its segments do not become admitted merely by appearing in an expression.

`/`, `//`, `.`, `::`, `+>`, `<+`, `>|`, `|<`, parentheses, the named-relation form `Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target`, **and** cardinality follow CA-R-1931 **and** CA-R-2487. `//` is one separator token between a kind **and** a named instance; its right operand is the instance's name, **not** an Atom ID. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target; Atom version tags retain their separate meaning. Parentheses provide logical grouping. `Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are containment, not inheritance or sequence. `X >| Y` and `Y |< X` express the same HAS_CLASSIFICATION fact with Entity Y used as an applicable Classification axis, not membership or a new Entity kind. Relation counts use `Source {::forward}((RELATION)){::reverse} Target`; direct values use `Property{::occurrence}:: [format]{::value count}`. Operators, grouping, relation delimiters, Formats, **and** cardinality are **not** Terms.

The complete expression **must** resolve **to** **`=1`** canonical Subject Target that already exists **or** is explicitly introduced by applicable defining authority under CA-R-1194 **and** CA-R-1931. Syntax alone neither creates **nor** admits a target **or** native EntityGraph fact. The expression identifies the target, **not** the Atom's Subject Relation **to** it. An arbitrary composite expression is **not** one Term **or** automatically one entity name; an admitted qualified property name **may** identify **`=1`** entity.

## Details

Subjects do not carry Atom or Artifact IDs, whether bare, version-qualified, or embedded in an ID selector. Use typed Relations for links to those Atoms or Artifacts. The contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` distinguish their respective ID Properties, not particular identifier values. They are not alternative complete canonical Subject names or case-folded aliases; an authored Subject uses its full admitted expression. Their shared terminal label and reusable `ID` meaning do not collide. Dot remains an operator; these contextual spellings are not renamed to `atom.atom_id` or another invented spelling. Named-instance Subjects use names, not IDs. Source/provenance metadata outside Subjects is not prohibited.

`//` selects a named instance of a primary kind, not an instance of a dependent property. A following `.` can select that instance's property, including `Selection//Projection and Journal Authority Sources.updated_at`. Source-established kind or bearer qualification participates in the complete canonical name. Distinct modeled entities require distinct complete qualified names, while repeated references retain the same identity and name. Local instance labels may coincide across different kinds when their complete qualified names differ. Local names remain unique per entity kind within the project's Current source view across owning Scope Units under CA-R-2476. This grammar adds neither case folding nor a name registry. When `//` is mandatory remains deferred.

`Entity/Object/Continuant/Package`, `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module`, and `Entity/Object/Continuant/Package <+ Module <+ Code Unit` identify three connected entities. The chain is not one Term or a fourth entity. `Package`, `Module`, and `Code Unit` are their reusable lexical components, not their complete Entity expressions. Likewise, `Package` and `Unit` are reusable Terms whose occurrence does not itself introduce an entity or Relation. The rule applies to exact full expressions in authored prose as well as Subjects. Literal source quotations and code identifiers remain distinguishable and are not automatically renamed. Arbitrary instance names and identifiers outside this modeled-entity naming role are not automatically lexical definitions.

Entity is the canonical expression root under CA-R-1194. The registered operators retain their meanings and native-fact admission boundaries. No new alias, parser, resolver grammar, formula, or unadopted syntax is introduced by this definition.

## Summary

Permit reused Terms **in** qualified value domains

## Claim

### Prose Claim

A reusable Term **may** occur in literal allowed values in multiple qualified Property contexts when it retains the same approved meaning and governing authority admits the value separately in every context; distinct modeled entities **must** have distinct complete canonical names, and admission in one context does **not** admit the value in another. Reusing a Term in literal values does not create a value Node or make that Term another Entity’s complete canonical name.

## Details

Reusable lexical Terms and complete canonical names have distinct responsibilities. Shared `Package`, `Unit`, or `ID` components and repeated terminal labels do not collide when complete qualified expressions differ. The contextual topic/code spellings `atom.id` and `projection.id` distinguish their respective ID Properties; they are not alternative complete canonical Subject names or case-folded aliases. Authored Subjects use their full admitted expressions. `Atom/(.Header.Role := X)/(.Header.Form := X)` is a possible qualified expression: its two `X` components reuse the registered Term `X` in separately qualified value contexts, and governing authority must admit `X` in each context. The expression does not make `X` the complete canonical name of an entity outside `Term`, create an entity, or transfer value admission. Governing authority establishes the qualification and entity identity; path spelling alone does not invent them.

Repeated references to one source-admitted entity retain its complete canonical name and do not grant another value-domain admission. Component reuse does not introduce another entity or alter the approved meaning owned by its dedicated Term Definition. Complete-name uniqueness does not prohibit reusable Terms or require globally unique terminal labels.

## Summary

Record Tool calls within Step Runs

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Tool Calls that occur within Step Runs.


a Tool Call **means** an invocation of a Tool during execution; **when** it occurs within a Step Run, its execution evidence **must** remain associated with that parent Step Run **in** the canonical Project Journal.

## Details

- retain the invoked Tool, supplied inputs, actual result **or** error, **and** parent Step Run association. preserve call identity **and** timing sufficient **to** distinguish separate attempts; do **not** report an attempted **or** uncertain effect as confirmed completion.
- use authorized references **or** protected representations for secret **or** sensitive inputs under their governing rules; execution tracing does **not** authorize copying secrets into the Journal.
- a Step Run for a leaf Step that runs an Action executes its **`=1`** declared Action through its **`=1`** Action Run. a containing Step Run launches no own Action; its nested Step Runs retain their own Step execution. Tool calls remain execution details associated with their parent Step Run, **not** automatically new Steps, Action definitions, **or** Workflow nodes; this tracing rule does **not** grant Tool-call permission.
- a view **may** display Workflow Run, containing **and** leaf Step Runs, **and** Tool-call evidence as a nested trace; derive the view from the canonical records rather than creating another independently maintained execution history.
- preserve actual ordering **and** parentage **without** inferring concurrency permission, Workflow routing, **or** a new Step Run for **every** Tool call.

## Summary

Define the Content Role Property

## Claim scope

The Content Role classification of Atoms.

## Claim

Content Role is the classification parameter of an Atom that identifies the primary contribution of its Claim. The parameter has an allowed value, such as Requirement or Plan; it is not a separate entity kind.

Within `Entity/Object/Continuant/Governing Objects`, `Atom.Content Role` names the Atom's Content Role Property. `Atom/(.Content Role: Requirement)` names the narrower Atom kind qualified by that Property and its independently admitted value. That narrower kind inherits Atom's applicable features and constraints. The full canonical Subject uses the Entity root and complete path.

### Formal claim

```text
Atom.Content Role[string]{1}
```

## Semantics

A Subject may name a thing or a topic. Having a Subject does not make the named topic a separate entity kind. Defining Content Role therefore does not introduce an intermediate Entity kind between Atom and its role-qualified kinds; the Property remains directly addressable.

The stored Content Role value classifies a particular Atom. The Subject notation describes the classification axis or a role-qualified Atom kind; it does not assign a value to a particular Atom instance.

## Details

The allowed values and the requirement for one value per Atom remain governed by CA-R-1283 and CA-R-740. This definition does not change those rules.

## Summary

Use Subject Path Separators for Broader-to-Narrower and Bearer-to-Dependent

## Claim

### Prose Claim


a Entity Path.


In an Entity Path, `/` separates a broader kind from its narrower kind; `//`
separates an Entity kind from a named instance; `.` separates a bearer from a
dependent Property; and `::` separates any `X` from its allowed literal value
`Y`, irrespective of X's kind or path. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target and declares no target. Parentheses provide logical
grouping.

`Part +> Whole` and `Whole <+ Part` are opposite writings of the same
containment fact. Its direct fact is Part IS_CONTAINED_BY Whole, and CONTAINS
is derived. `X >| Y` and `Y |< X` are opposite writings of the same
HAS_CLASSIFICATION fact, with Entity Y used as an applicable Classification
axis rather than belonging to a separate Classification Entity kind. This Rule does not
invent an inverse canonical Relation Type for HAS_CLASSIFICATION.

`X/(.Y := Z)` denotes a narrower kind of X qualified by its own Property Y
and value Z. The leading dot inside parentheses is relative to X: `.Y`
addresses `X.Y`. The qualified X inherits X's applicable features and
constraints. The Property is the qualification condition; it does not become
a narrower kind of its bearer. This form replaces the proposed classification
Property category and the earlier bare `X/Y: Z` qualification spelling.

`Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target` expresses a defined named Relation. Persist
the direct fact once and show its declared derived inverse only as a derived
view. Entity syntax neither creates target identities nor admits native facts
without defining authority. A defining Atom may introduce its governed Entity.

Cardinality uses `{::n}`, `{::n+}`, and `{::n..m}`. Direct Property values use
their post-Property notation, for example `X.Y:: [format]{::n}`. A Relation has two
independent directional slots: `Source {forward-count}RELATION{reverse-count}
Target`. The pre-operator slot constrains Relation instances in the written
Source-to-Target direction per Source; the post-operator slot independently
constrains the reverse count per Target. These are not distinct-target counts. For example, the bound Step selector below
requires exactly one outgoing IS_CONTAINED_BY link per Step to either a Workflow
or another Step; it leaves the reverse count unspecified.
`Property {::1}((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Bearer` requires
exactly one outgoing IS_PROPERTY_OF Relation for each Property occurrence;
postfix-only `{::1}` would instead constrain the reverse count per Bearer.
Each Relation is binary and connects two endpoint nodes or node instances.
The slots count Relation instances, not Relation arity; omitted slots remain
unspecified. This Relation counting is independent of the Property's
direct-value Format and cardinality.
Advanced functions, formulas, interpolation, and bracketed conditions are out
of scope.


```text
Step//$step;
$step{::1}((IS_CONTAINED_BY)) (in (Workflow, Step))//$parent
Atom/(.Header.Role := Method)
Atom.Header.Status >| Status Group:: Draft <+ Draft
Atom.Header.Status >| Status Group:: Archived <+ Archived
Atom.Header.Status >| Status Group:: Current <+ * not in (Draft, Archived)
Source ((RELATION_TYPE)) Target
```

## Semantics

`/` is specialization and supplies inheritance. `+>` and `<+` are containment
and do not supply inheritance, sequence, or a property relation. `//` names
an instance of a kind; `.` addresses a dependent Property; and `::` declares
an allowed value rather than assigning one. A bare qualified address refers to its declared target and creates neither an alias nor a duplicate.

`X.Y` addresses Property Y, and `X.Y:: Z` expresses its allowed value.
`X/(.Y := Z)` instead identifies qualified X entities. For example,
`Atom/(.Header.Form := Method)` means an Atom with the stated Form qualification, not
the Form Property inheriting Atom's features. This syntax example alone does
not admit Method as a Form value; the existing Role use is written
`Atom/(.Header.Role := Method)`. Every qualification still requires its own
admitted Property and allowed value. Existing Carrier keys and encodings
remain governed separately by Delivery; the notation adds no nested object.

Status Group classifies Atom Statuses through
`Atom.Header.Status >| Status Group`. The following `<+` expressions describe each
group's Status parts. In this
mapping, `* not in (Draft, Archived)` selects admitted Atom Status values
other than Draft and Archived. It does not admit new Status values, missing
values or a general expression language. Containment does not imply
inheritance; the Property-qualified Atom kind inherits through `/`.

## Details

Each Module belongs to exactly one Package; Project Implementation is the
parentless root Package and a nested Package belongs to another Package. A Step
is contained by a Workflow or another Step. Scope Unit has structural
parts expressed as `Scope Unit <+ Scope Unit`, `Scope Unit <+ Atom`, and
`Scope Unit <+ Projection`.

Backslash escapes the next literal name character. Single/double quotes are
carrier serialization, not Entity delimiters. One globally unique primary
kind name and one canonical declaration path are required; migration does not
retain aliases. Term-path reconciliation remains subject to C605.

## Summary

Require exactly one immediate bearer for each dependent Entity occurrence

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Model Property occurrences selected by `Node.**` and their direct IS_PROPERTY_OF connections.


Every source-declared model Property occurrence selected by `Node.**` must have exactly one immediate bearer, identified by one outgoing direct IS_PROPERTY_OF connection to that bearer. A source establishes dependence independently of whether the edge is present, so a missing edge fails this requirement. Select source-declared Property occurrences independently of whether their bearer edges exist; do not infer dependence from edges or create a bearer connection.

## Semantics

`Node.**` selects Properties of Node and its narrower branch, grounded in bearer dependence through IS_PROPERTY_OF. Property instances are distinct from model Properties; their HAS_INSTANCE permissions are declared separately. Its lexical Term is separately defined at `Term//Property`. Identifying a source-declared Property occurrence does not invent a bearer edge or treat a missing edge as proof of independence. The Property occurrence has identity qualified by its immediate bearer; the Property definition supplies its value Format and direct-value cardinality. The bearer-Relation count is distinct from the number of values a Property allows.

## Details

This Rule applies to source-declared Properties covered by `Node.**`. Identify the source-declared occurrences independently of their IS_PROPERTY_OF edges. Missing required bearer edges remain failures; this Rule does not infer or create edges.

## Summary

Require exactly one immediate bearer for each dependent Entity occurrence

## Claim

### Prose Claim


Model Property occurrences selected by `Node.**` and their direct IS_PROPERTY_OF connections.


Every source-declared model Property occurrence selected by `Node.**` must have exactly one immediate bearer, identified by one outgoing direct IS_PROPERTY_OF connection to that bearer. A source establishes dependence independently of whether the edge is present, so a missing edge fails this requirement. Select source-declared Property occurrences independently of whether their bearer edges exist; do not infer dependence from edges or create a bearer connection.

## Semantics

`Node.**` selects Properties of Node and its narrower branch, grounded in bearer dependence through IS_PROPERTY_OF. Property instances are distinct from model Properties; their HAS_INSTANCE permissions are declared separately. Its lexical Term is separately defined at `Term//Property`. Identifying a source-declared Property occurrence does not invent a bearer edge or treat a missing edge as proof of independence. The Property occurrence has identity qualified by its immediate bearer; the Property definition supplies its value Format and direct-value cardinality. The bearer-Relation count is distinct from the number of values a Property allows.

## Details

This Rule applies to source-declared Properties covered by `Node.**`. Identify the source-declared occurrences independently of their IS_PROPERTY_OF edges. Missing required bearer edges remain failures; this Rule does not infer or create edges.
